bar_text: De Isar is a Fluss, der wo vo de Oipn durch Minga fliaßt und letzendlich gengiba vo Degndorf in d Donau münden duat.
english: The Isar is a river that flows from the Alps through Munich and ultimately flows into the Danube opposite Deggendorf.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da Ursprung liagt in Estareich im Hinteraudoi vom Kawendl-Gebirg.
english: The origin lies in Austria in the Hinterautal of the Kaunertal mountains.
note: Kawendl means Karwendel, not the Kaunertal mountains.

bar_text: Zwischn Scharnitz und Mittnwoid fliaßts iaba d' Grenz vo Estareich noch Bayern (Deitschland).
english: Between Scharnitz and Mittnwoid, it flows across the border from Austria to Bavaria (Germany).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Se hod a Leng vo 295 Kilometa.
english: It has a length of 295 kilometers.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Neba Minga liang de Städt Däiz, Freising, Moosburg und Landshuad an da Isar.
english: Besides Munich, there are two cities: Dachau, Freising, Moosburg and Landshut on the Isar.
note: Changes Bad Tölz to Dachau and introduces an incorrect count of two cities.

bar_text: De greaßtn Zufliass han d' Amper bei Moosburg, d' Loisach bei Wolfratshausn und d' Moosach bei Freising.
english: The largest tributaries are the Amper near Moosburg, the Loisach near Wolfratshausen, and the Moosach near Freising.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: D' Isar is noch da Donau, am Inn und am Main da viertlängste Fluss in Bayern.
english: The Isar is, after the Danube, the Inn and the Main, the fourth longest river in Bavaria.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Lange Zeit hods ghoaßn, der Nama Isar dad ausm keltischn kemma und sovui wia reißnds Wossa (ys = schnej, reißnd und ura = Wossa, Fluss) bedeitn.
english: For a long time it was said that the name Isar came from Celtic and meant something like rushing water (ys = snow, rushing and ura = water, river).
note: schnej means fast here, not snow; the rest of the historical Celtic explanation is retained.

bar_text: Des guid inzwischn ois vaaltate Meinung.
english: That is now all an outdated opinion.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: D'Sprachforscher moana jetzad es dad vo da indogermanischn Wurzl es/is (fia fließnds Wossa) kemma, de se a in fui andane Flußnama wiadafindt und se in aktuelle Sprachn nua no aufs feste Wossa, oiso s Eis bziagt.
english: Language researchers now think that it would have come from the Indo-European root es/is (for flowing water), which they also find in many other river names, and in current languages it only refers to solid water, i.e., ice.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A guads Drum vom Wossa des auf'd boarischn Oipn unds Kawendl foid fliaßt durch d' Isar zur Donau und so bis ins Schwoazze Meea.
english: A good amount of water that falls on the Bavarian Alps and the foothills flows through the Isar to the Danube and so on into the Black Sea.
note: Kawendl is the Karwendel, not the foothills.

bar_text: S' gsamte Einzugsgebiat hod a Flächn vo 9000 Quadratkilometa.
english: The entire catchment area has an area of 9000 square kilometers.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wei a Guads vom Niedaschlog in de Berg ois Schnee foid hods zur Schneeschmelz as meiste Wossa.
english: Because a good amount of precipitation fell in the mountains as snow, most of the water comes from the snowmelt.
note: Most water coming from snowmelt differs from the source's highest water level occurring during snowmelt.

bar_text: Mit am mittlern Abfluss vo 175 Kubikmeta in da Sekund zählt d' Isar zu de mittlgroßn deitschn Flüss.
english: With an average discharge of 175 cubic meters per second, the Isar is among the medium-sized German rivers.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ma kos sogseng mit am Lech, da Mosel, am Main und am Neckar vagleicha.
english: One can compare it with the Lech, the Moselle, the Main, and the Neckar.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da Ursprung vo da Isar liagt im Hinteraudoi im Karwendl auf 1.160 Meta iaba Normalnui ( Koordinaten fehlen! Hilf mit. ...).
english: The origin of the Isar lies in Hinteraudoi in the Karwendel at 1,160 meters above sea level (coordinates are missing! Help out. ...).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Do fliaßt da Lafatsch an de Isarquelln vorbei.
english: There, Lafatsch flows past the Isar springs.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da Lafatsch hod sei Quelln in da Nach vom Hallerangerhaus.
english: Lafatsch has his spring in the vicinity of the Halleranger house.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Er is da längste vo de Quellbäch.
english: He is the longest of the spring brooks.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Sei Nama ändert se bei de Isarquelln in Isar, oafach wei de Quelln vui mehra Wassa bringa, ois ea sejba hod.
english: His name changes at the Isar springs to Isar, simply because the springs bring much more water than he himself has.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: In de Berg han ois wichtige Nebnflüß da Rißbach, d' Achn und d'Jachn zum dawähna.
english: In the mountains, we have important tributaries, the Rißbach, the Achn, and the Jachn, to mention.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da Rißbach kimmt aus da Eng und trifft bei Vorderriß auf d' Isar.
english: The Rißbach comes from the Eng and meets the Isar at Vorderriß.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: D'Achn kimmt vom Achensee und mündt in Sylvensteinsee, dem sei Zua- und Abfluß d' Isar is.
english: The Ache comes from the Achensee and flows into Sylvensteinsee, whose inflow and outflow is the Isar.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: D'Jachn kimmt vom Walchasee, fliaßt durch d' Jachenau und mündt in da Nach vo Fleck und Wegscheid.
english: The Jachn comes from the Walchsee, flows through the Jachenau and flows into the Isar near Fleck and Wegscheid.
note: Walchsee is a different lake; context identifies the source's Walchasee as Walchensee.

bar_text: De wichtigstn Nebenflüß außahoib vo de Berg han d' Amper und d' Loisach.
english: The most important tributaries outside of the mountains are the Amper and the Loisach.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De meistn Inseln und Kiesbänk in da Isar untaliegn wega de starkn Hochwassa a ständign Änderung in ihra Form und Log.
english: Most of the islands and gravel banks in the Isar are constantly changing in their shape and location due to the strong floods.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: D'Isar werd auf vaschiedne Artn zur Energie-Gewinnung gnutzt.
english: The Isar is used in various ways for energy production.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A guada Tei vom Isarwossa werd in da Nach vo Mittnwoid zum Woichnsää umgleit.
english: A good part of the Isar water will be diverted to the grain field on Wednesday night.
note: Walchensee and near Mittenwald become a grain field and Wednesday night.

bar_text: Des werd gmacht, wei s' Woichnsääkraftwerk mehra Wossa bracht, ois vo sejba in See fliaßt.
english: That will be done because the Woichnsää power plant brought more water than flows into the lake by itself.
note: Needs more water is changed to brought more water, with an unsupported future framing.

bar_text: Da Sylvenstoa is a Stausee, dear vor oim gegas Hochwassa baut worn is, aba a zua Stromerzeugung gnutzt werd.
english: The Sylven Reservoir is a reservoir that was built primarily to protect against high water, but is also used for electricity generation.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im weidan Valauf gibts mehrane Flußkraftwerke z. B. am neadlichn Stadtrand vo Däiz und de Isarwerke 1-3 inahoib vo Minga.
english: In the further course, there are more hydroelectric power plants, e.g., on the northern outskirts of Deggendorf and the Isar plants 1-3 halfway to Munich.
note: Däiz is Bad Tolz, not Deggendorf; inahoib vo Minga means within Munich, not halfway to it.

bar_text: Neba da Nutzung vo da Wassakraft is as Isarwassa indirekt ois Kühlwassa fias Kernkraftwerk Isar bei Landshut vo Bedeitung.
english: Besides the use of hydropower, the Isar water is indirectly of importance as cooling water for the Isar nuclear power plant near Landshut.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A wenn Wassakraft ois was recht umweltfreindlichs ogseng werd hods fia'd Isar einschneidnde Folgn.
english: Even if hydropower is being presented as something very environmentally friendly, it has decisive consequences for the Isar.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Lange Zeit is as ganze Wassa zum Woichasee umgleit worn.
english: For a long time, all the water has been diverted to Lake Woichasee.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da a as meiste vom Rißboch zum Woichasee umgleit wurd is d'Isar zwischn Krea und am Sylvenstoa ab und zua a austrocknd.
english: Since most of the Rißbach was diverted to the Walchensee, the Isar between Kreuth and the Sylvenstein is occasionally drying up.
note: Krea here is Krun, not Kreuth; the drying is also shifted to the present.

bar_text: Des ganze Wassa kimmt zwar letzendlich iaban Kochesee und Loisach wiada zruck in d'Isar, aba bis Wolfratshausn fejds im Flußlauf.
english: All the water does eventually come back into the Isar via the Kochelsee and Loisach, but it is missing from the river course up to Wolfratshausen.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Inzwischn werd a greaßana Teil vom Wossa in da Isar glassn.
english: In the meantime, a larger part of the water is being let into the Isar.
note: Water left in the Isar becomes water let into it, changing the retention mechanism.

bar_text: A de fuin Seitnkanäle fia de Flußkraftwerk z. B. in da Nach vo Minga entziehn am wildn Flußlauf as Wossa.
english: The diversion channels for the hydroelectric power plants, e.g., in the vicinity of Munich, withdraw the water from the wild river course.
note: Omits the quantity many side channels.

bar_text: Außadem vahindern de Wehre an Transport vom Geschiebe.
english: In addition, the weirs prevent the transport of the debris.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Deszweng grobt se d' Isar a tiafas Flußbett.
english: There, the Isar digs a deep riverbed.
note: There replaces because of this, losing the stated causal connection.

bar_text: A de Nutzung ois Kühlwassa fias Kernkraftwerk tuat am Fluß ned guad, wei dadurch sei Temperatur steigt.
english: Using it as cooling water for the nuclear power plant is not good for the river, because its temperature rises as a result.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Dafia gibts aba Grenzwert, in oam hoaßn Somma hod as Kernkraftwerk scho drosselt wern miaßn, weis sonst de Umweltauflagn ned dafüllt hed.
english: But there is a limit to that; in one hot summer, the nuclear power plant already had to be throttled, because otherwise the environmental requirements would not have been met.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fast scho zum Nama dazua gheard ois Zuasotz da Farbeidruck.
english: The color print almost belongs to the name as an addition.
note: Farbeidruck means color impression, not a physical color print.

bar_text: S' is ois greane Isar bekannt.
english: It is known to all of green Isar.
note: to all of mistranslates ois/as and obscures the known-as construction, although green Isar remains.

bar_text: Des is aba nua de Farb vo am klarn Wossa, des erscheint tatsächli greablau.
english: But that is only the color of clear water, which actually appears gray-blue.
note: greablau means green-blue, not gray-blue.

bar_text: De Farb hods in niederschlogsarme Zeitn, wenn da greaßte Teil vom Wossa aus de Quelln stammt.
english: The color is present in low-flow periods, when the greatest part of the water comes from the springs.
note: Low-flow periods replace low-precipitation periods; the conditions are not identical.

bar_text: Noch starke Regnfäll gibts durch Erosion an Haffa Schlamm und Dreck im Wossa, dann werds undurchsichtig lehmig braun.
english: After heavy rainfall, there is mud and dirt in the water due to erosion, then it becomes opaque, loamy brown.
note: Omits an Haffa, the explicitly large amount of mud and dirt.

bar_text: Iaba s' Enstehen vo dea greablaun Farb is ma se ned ganz einig.
english: I am not entirely sure about the emergence of the greenish-blue color.
note: Replaces a lack of general agreement with the speaker's own uncertainty.

bar_text: Wahrscheinlich is a Zammspui vo Algn und am glästn Koich.
english: Probably it is a collusion between Algn and the glästn Koich.
note: Leaves the key algae/lime terms untranslated and renders the interaction as collusion.

bar_text: Da Eindruck werd vastärkt durch de helln Koichsteana am Grund vom Fluß und dem sonst recht klarn Wossa.
english: The impression is reinforced by the bright pebbles at the bottom of the river and the otherwise quite clear water.
note: Bright pebbles omit the limestone material.

bar_text: Dadurch kimmt a Haffa Liacht aus'm Fluß zruck und iabastrahlt des vo da Oberflächn reflektierte Liacht.
english: As a result, a heap of light comes back from the river and it irradiates the light reflected from the surface.
note: Irradiates does not convey outshining the light reflected by the surface.

bar_text: So hod de tatsächliche Farb vom Wassa an greaßan Eifluß auf an Farbeidruck ois de Farb vom Himme oda da Umgebung.
english: So the actual color of the water has a greater influence on a color print than the color of the sky or the surroundings.
note: Farbeidruck means perceived color impression, not color print.

bar_text: Fo da Farb is a as Biamischdrangl d'Isarmass inspiriad.
english: From the color, the beer mixture has been inspired by the iron mass.
note: Isarmass becomes iron mass and the drink's identification and color-inspiration relationship are lost.

bar_text: Zwischn Arzbach und Däiz is oana recht fleißig dabei, daß a noch am jedn Hochwassa seine Stoahaffa nei aufschicht.
english: Between Arzbach and Deiz, someone is quite busy making sure that he piles up his stone heaps again at every flood.
note: At every flood is less precise than the explicit after every flood.

bar_text: De Haffa han ois Isarpyramidn bekannt und a scho mehrmois in da Zeidung und am Fernsehn erwähnt worn.
english: The harbors are known as Isar pyramids and have already been mentioned several times in the newspaper and on television.
note: Haffa refers to the stone heaps, not harbors.

bar_text: Da Erbauer sejba nend des Platzl Kloa-Kairo.
english: The builder himself doesn't think the little place is clear-cut.
note: The Little Cairo naming claim becomes a negative opinion about being clear-cut.

bar_text: A Altarbuidl vo 1480 in da Jakobskirch in Lengrias is a Beispui fia oide Darstellunga vo da Isar.
english: An altar picture from 1480 in the St. James Church in Lengries is an example of old depictions of the Isar.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da unbkannte Moier hod s'Köpfn vom Apostel Jakobus ans Ufer vo da Isar valegt.
english: The unknown Moor laid the head of the Apostle James on the bank of the Isar.
note: Moier is painter, not Moor; s'Köpfn is the beheading scene, not laying a head on the bank.

bar_text: Im 19. Jahrhundert ham an Haffa Mola aus da Münchner Schui d' Isar ois Motiv fia eanane Buidl entdeckt.
english: In the 19th century, a lot of painters from the Munich School discovered the Isar as a motif for their pictures.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wei de recht gnau gmoid hom wern de Buidl a ois Dokumentation fia de Vaänderunga vo da Landschaft durch d'Leid ogseng.
english: Because they were painted very precisely, these pictures will also be seen by people as documentation of the changes to the landscape.
note: Human-caused landscape changes become documentation seen by people, and the current appraisal is shifted to the future.

bar_text: Im Jäger vo Foi hod da Ludwig Ganghofer am Isarwinke und seine Bewohna a literarischs Denkmoi gsetzt und damit zur Bekanntheit vo der Gengd beitrong.
english: In "The Hunter of Fall," Ludwig Ganghofer created a literary monument to the Isarwinkel and its inhabitants, thereby contributing to the fame of the region.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Oans vo am Willy Michl seine erfolgreichstn Liadl is as Isarflimmern.
english: One of Willy Michl's most successful songs is Isarflimmern.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Er sejba hod an so starkn Bzug zum Fluß, daß a se Isarindianer nend.
english: He himself has such a strong attraction to the river that they call them the Isar Indians.
note: He calls himself singular becomes they call them plural.

bar_text: Bejgien (Holländisch: België, Franzesisch: Belgique, Deitsch: Belgien), offiziäi Kinigreich Bejgien (holl.: Koninkrijk België, franz.: Royaume de Belgique) is a fedaral organisirschte parlamentarische Monarchie in Westeiropa, houd uma 10,5 Millionan Einwohna und is 30.528 km² gross und is a Mitglied vo da Eiropäischn Union.
english: Belgium (Dutch: België, French: Belgique, German: Belgien), officially Kingdom of Belgium (Dutch: Koninkrijk België, French: Royaume de Belgique) is a federally organized parliamentary monarchy in Western Europe, has around 10.5 million inhabitants and is 30,528 km² large and is a member of the European Union.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es grenzt an Holland, Deitschland, Luxnbuag, Frankreich und an de Nordsee.
english: It borders Holland, Germany, Luxembourg, France and the North Sea.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Mid Holland und Luxnbuag zomm bijdt Bejgien de Beneluxstootn.
english: With Holland and Luxembourg, Belgium forms the Benelux states.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Seid da Unobhängigkeit vo 1830 und da Vafossungsgewung vo 1831 is Bejgien a parlamentarische Monarchie.
english: Since the independence of 1830 and the constitutional victory of 1831, Belgium has been a parliamentary monarchy.
note: Constitutional victory is an imprecise rendering of the constitution's adoption/granting.

bar_text: De flämische Beväikarung im Noadn, da franzesische Sidn mid na Minderheit in da Haptstod Brissl und a kloane deitschsprouchige Beväikarung an Ostn bijdn an ohoitaschtn Konflikthead, dem wous seid de 1970er Jou durch a Denzentroiisirung vo da Stoutsorganisazion und 1993 durch de Umwondlung in an Bundesstout zan begegnan vasuacht woun is.
english: The Flemish population in the north, the French in the south with a minority in the capital Brussels, and a small German-speaking population in the east have been trying to counter an old conflict issue, which was attempted through a decentralization of the state organization in the 1970s and through the transformation into a federal state in 1993.
note: Makes the populations the agents countering the conflict rather than constituting it; also weakens since the 1970s to in the 1970s.

bar_text: Denneascht homd owa de gengsätzlichn Intressn vo de Vatreta vo de boadn grossn Beväikarungsgruppm (Sprouchgruppm gnonnt) weiderhi de bäigische Politik prägt und beeiflusst.
english: On this day, however, the opposing interests of the representatives of the large population groups in Belgium (referred to as language groups) have continued to shape and influence Belgian politics.
note: Denneascht is nevertheless, not on this day; the number two is also omitted.

bar_text: Da Bundesstout Bejgien is in droi Gmoaschouftn (de flämische, franzesische und de deitsche Gmoaschouft) sowia in droi Regionan (Flandern, Wallonien und de Region Brissl-Hauptstod) eitoaet.
english: The federal state Belgium is divided into three communities (the Flemish, French, and German communities) as well as into three regions (Flanders, Wallonia, and the Brussels-Capital Region).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Bejgien is a Grindungsmidgliad vo da Eiropäischn Wiatschoftsgmoaschoft (EWG), da heiting Eiropäischn Union (EU), vo dera de wichtigstn Instituziona in da Hauptstoud Brissl eanan Sitz homd.
english: Belgium is a founding member of the European Economic Community (EEC), the current European Union (EU), of which the most important institutions have their seat in the capital Brussels.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ougsechn vom Berglaund vo de Ardennen im Siidostn is Bejgien a weidgeheaschts ewernes Laund.
english: Cut off from the mountain range of the Ardennes in the southeast, Belgium is a somewhat eternal land.
note: Apart from becomes cut off from, and largely flat becomes somewhat eternal.

bar_text: De Wossakantn dastreckt se auf 72,3 km.
english: The waterworks stretch out over 72.3 km.
note: Coastline becomes waterworks.

bar_text: 25 Prozent vo da Laundesflächn wernd fia de Laundwirtschouft gnitzt.
english: 25 percent of the land area are used for agriculture.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Uma 95 Prozent vo oie Bäigier leem in Städt.
english: Around 95 percent of all your legs live in cities.
note: Belgians become your legs, destroying the population subject despite retaining the percentage/city pattern.

bar_text: Laut de Berechnungan vom Kiniglichn Bäigischn Institut fia Naturwissnschouftn houd Bejgien a Flächn vo 30.528 km².
english: According to the calculations of the Royal Belgian Institute for Natural Sciences, Belgium has an area of 30,528 km².
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Vijväikerstout Bejgien leem holländisch reedeaschte Flamen (59% vo da Beväikarung), franzesischsprochige Wallonen (40%) und a deitschsprouchige Minderheit (Ripuarische Reinfrankn mid za. 1%) zomm.
english: In the Belgian population, Dutch-speaking Flemish (59% of the population), French-speaking Walloons (40%), and a German-speaking minority (Ripuarian Ripuarian with approx. 1%) live together.
note: Omits the multiethnic-state description and loses Rhine Franconian in the duplicated Ripuarian label.

bar_text: De weiderne Wonbeväikarung bestet aus Zuagwondeaschte aus vij Toaen vo Eiropa (bsundeascht aus Poin, Italien und Marokko).
english: The further population consists of incoming branches from five continents (especially from Asia, Italy and Morocco).
note: Immigrants become incoming branches, many parts of Europe becomes five continents, and Poland becomes Asia.

bar_text: In Bejgien gibbs heid droi Omtssprouchn: Holländisch (Flämisch san de holländischn Dialekt in Flandern), Franzesisch und Deitsch (san de westmittldeitschn Dialekt und de hochdeitsche Omtssprouch in Ostbejgien).
english: In Belgium there are three official languages today: Dutch (Flemish are the Dutch dialects in Flanders), French and German (are the West Central German dialects and the High German official language in East Belgium).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Seid da Unouhänigkeit vo Bejgien 1830 houd alloa Franzesisch ois Omtssprouch vom Stout goitn.
english: Since the independence of Belgium in 1830, French alone has been the official language of the state.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Jou 1873 is Holländisch ois zwoate offiziäie Omtssprouch im bäigischn Kinigreich rechtlich oerkonnt woun, owa trotzdem is d' Vawoitungs- und Untarichtssprouch in gonz Bejgien alloa Franzesisch gween.
english: In the year 1873, Dutch was legally recognized as the second official language in the Belgian Kingdom, but nevertheless, the administrative and educational language in all of Belgium was only French.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: 1919, oiso nouchm Erschtn Wäidkriag, is Deitsch ois Omtssprouch fir d' Leid im neich dazuagwungernen Gebiat an Ostn dazua kemma.
english: 1919, so after the First World War, German was added as the official language for the people in the newly annexed territory in the east.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Erscht danouch houd d' grosse Merheit vo de Flamen mid Nouchdruck gfordeascht, dass eaner holländische Muattersprouch a ois Vawoitungs- und Unterrichtssprouch an Schuin und Universitätn vawendt und da franzesischn Omtssprouch gleichstäid weascht.
english: Only afterwards did the great majority of the French demand through pressure that they use the Dutch mother tongue as an administrative and instructional language at schools and universities and that it be made equal to the French official language.
note: Changes the Flemish majority demanding language equality into the French majority.

bar_text: 1921 houd de bäigische Regirung de territoriale Oasprouchigkeit vo eanare Bewoner in de droi regionoin Sprouchgebiatn oerkonnt: de holländische Sprouchzone Flandern, de franzesische Sprouchzone Wallonie und de doudro grenzeaschte deitsche Sprouchzone in Ostbejgien.
english: In 1921, the Belgian government recognized the territorial linguistic character of its inhabitants in the three linguistic regions: the Dutch-speaking zone Flanders, the French-speaking zone Wallonia, and the German-speaking zone bordering Luxembourg in East Belgium.
note: Omits explicit territorial monolingualism and invents bordering Luxembourg instead of the adjacent zone.

bar_text: Des letzterne Gebiat houd zavur zan Deitschn Reich ghärscht und is nouch'm Erschtn Wäidkriag und duachn Versailler Vatroug an Bejgien ogschlossn woun.
english: The last territory belonged to the German Reich and was attached to Belgium after the First World War and through the Treaty of Versailles.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: An Status vo Regionoisprouchn houmd seid 1990 Lothringisch, Champenois, Fränkisch, Picardisch und Wallonisch.
english: A status of regional dialects has been Lotharingian, Champenois, Franconian, Picard, and Walloon since 1990.
note: Changes the recognized status from regional languages to regional dialects.

bar_text: Ebber 75 Prozent vo de bäigischn Stoutsbiaga sand remisch-katholisch, runde 1 Prozent ghärnd ner protestantischn Kirch o, und 4 Prozent islamische Gmoana.
english: About 75 percent of the Bavarian stout drinkers are Roman Catholic, around 1 percent belong to the Protestant church, and 4 percent to Islamic communities.
note: Belgian citizens become Bavarian stout drinkers, losing the population to which the figures apply.

bar_text: Da Otoae vo konfesionslose betroug uma 20 Prozent.
english: The proportion of non-religious people is around 20 percent.
note: Unaffiliated becomes non-religious, and the past statistic is presented as current.

bar_text: De federale bäigische Regiarung untastitzt und oerkennt seggs Religionan und a nid-konfesionäie Wäidoschaung o: de Anglikanische Kiach, en Islam, as Judndum, de Remisch-Katholische Kirch, de Orthodoxe Kiach, a uniate protestantische Kiach und de Freigeistige Wäidoschaungsgmoaschouft.
english: The federal Belgian government supports and recognizes six religions and a non-confessional worldview: the Anglican Church, Islam, Judaism, the Roman Catholic Church, the Orthodox Church, a uniate Protestant Church, and the freethinking worldview community.
note: uniate does not precisely name the source's united Protestant church.

bar_text: Berlin is de Bundeshaptstod und da Regiarungssitz vo Deitschland.
english: Berlin is the federal capital and the seat of government of Germany.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Aussadem is s a oagnas Bundesland und as Zentrum vo da Metropolregion Berlin-Brandenburg.
english: Besides, it is a federal state and the center of the Berlin-Brandenburg metropolitan region.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Berlin is mit uma 3,6 Milliona Einwohna de gresste Stod vo Deitschland (noch da Bevejkarung und noch da Flächn).
english: Berlin is with around 3.6 million inhabitants the largest city of Germany (according to the population and according to the area).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: In da EU is de gresste Stod noch da Bevejkarung und de fiatgresste noch da Flächn.
english: In the EU, it is the largest city after the population and the largest after the area.
note: Changes the area ranking from fourth to first.

bar_text: Berlin wor in seine Gschicht scho mehrfoch a Haptstod, wia beispuisweis vom Kurfiaschtndum Brandenburg, vum Kinireich Breissn, vum Deitschn Reich und vo da DDR (nua im Osttei vo da Stod).
english: Berlin was already a capital city several times in its history, for example of the Electorate of Brandenburg, of the Kingdom of Prussia, of the German Reich and of the GDR (only in the eastern part of the city).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Seit da Wiedavaoanigung im Joar 1990 is Berlin gsamtdeitsche Haptstod.
english: Since the reunification in the year 1990, Berlin has been the all-German capital.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Davor war des Bonn.
english: Before that was Bonn.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Berlin is a bedeitens Zentrum vo Politik, Medien, Kuitua und Wissnschoft in Eiropa.
english: Berlin is an important center of politics, media, culture and science in Europe.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Stod is a wichtiga Vakeahsknotnpunkt und oane vo de moastbesuchtastn Städt vom Kontinent.
english: The city is an important transport hub and one of the most visited cities on the continent.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Institutiona wia de Universitetn, Forschungseirichtunga, Theata und Museen gniassn internationale Onakennung.
english: Institutions such as universities, research facilities, theaters and museums enjoy international recognition.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Stod is a Magnet fia Kunst- und Kuituaschoffende aus da ganzn Wejd.
english: The city is a magnet for artists and cultural workers from the whole world.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: As gschichtliche Vamächtnis, as Nochtlem, und de vuifejtige Architektua san iba de Grenzn ausse bekannt.
english: As historical heritage, the nightshade, and the diverse architectures are known beyond the borders.
note: Nochtlem means nightlife, not nightshade.

bar_text: Berlin hod zwejf Beziak, wo insgsamt in 96 Ortstei untateit san.
english: Berlin has twelve districts, which are divided into a total of 96 localities.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Dazua gibts no Ortslogn, geografische Gebiet aus da Umgangssproch, wo ned genau obgrenzt wean kina.
english: In addition, there are still local names, geographical areas from the colloquial language, which cannot be precisely delimited.
note: Calls the geographic localities local names.

bar_text: Wei de Ortstei und de Ortslogn historisch gwoxn san, spuins in da Oidogssproch a gressane Roin wia de Beziak.
english: Since the districts and the local names have grown historically, they play a large role in the old dialect, like the district.
note: Greater importance than boroughs becomes a large role like the district; everyday speech becomes old dialect.

bar_text: Des Woarzeichn vo Berlin is as Brandenburger Tor.
english: The trademark of Berlin is the Brandenburg Gate.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Boarisch bzw. oda Boirisch is a Sproch im Siidostn vom deitschn Sprochraum.
english: Bavarian or Boirisch is a language in the southeast of the German language area.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Zamma midm Alemannischn, Sidfränkischn und Ostfränkischn buidns de obadeitschn Sprochn.
english: Together with Alemannic, South Franconian, and East Franconian, they form the Upper German languages.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es Vabroadungsgebiet vom Boarischn is da oidboarische Tei vom Freistoot Bayern, es aissaste Sidvogdland in Saxn, Östareich (estli vom Arlberg), Sidtirol und de zimbrisch-karnischn Sprochinsln in Obaitalien.
english: The distribution area of Bavarian is the Old Bavarian part of the Free State of Bavaria, the authentic South Westphalia in Saxony, Austria (east of the Arlberg), South Tyrol, and the Cimrian-Carnic language islands in Northern Italy.
note: The extreme southern Vogtland becomes authentic South Westphalia.

bar_text: Meara wia de Hejft vo de Boarischn Muaddasprochla wohna aussahoib vom heitign Freistoot Bayern (Boarn).
english: More than the speakers of the Bavarian mother tongue live outside of today's Free State of Bavaria (Bavaria).
note: More than the speakers loses the essential half/majority quantity.

bar_text: Schaug unta: Portal:Boarisch – fia Informationa iwa d Boarische Kuitua.
english: Look below: Portal:Bavarian – for information about Bavarian culture.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fria hod ma gmoand doss da boarische bzw. bajuwarische Nama vo da kejtisch-germanischn heakimmt.
english: Previously, one thought that the Bavarian or Bajuvarian name comes from the Celtic-Germanic.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Bezoachnung baio-wariōz bedeit sovui wia de Weahhoftn Mauna vo de Baiern .
english: The designation Bavarian means as much as the strong men of Bavaria.
note: Substitutes modern Bavarian for the historical form and changes martial men of the Bavarians to strong men of Bavaria.

bar_text: S Grundwort "war" existiat heit nua no ois Voadagliad in da Zammasetzung Werwolf und Wergeld.
english: The basic word "war" only exists today as a prefix in the compounds Werwolf and Wergeld.
note: Voadagliad is a first compound member, not technically a prefix.

bar_text: Des is a oide aus indogermanischa Zeid stommande Bezoachnung fia Mo (vagleich z. B. lateinisch vir oda s isländische Suffix -verji wia in Bæverji, Baier).
english: This is an old designation for man originating from Indo-European times (comparable to, e.g., Latin vir or the Icelandic suffix -verji as in Bæverji, Baier).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fria hod ma gsogd, de Baiern waradn de Fuaßkraungn vo da Vejkawaundarung.
english: Earlier, one was told that the Bavarians are the foot soldiers of the change in the population.
note: Fuaßkraungn becomes foot soldiers and the Migration Period becomes a change in population.

bar_text: Denn de Baiern san ned gwaundat.
english: Because the Bavarians are not wounded.
note: Not wounded does not convey not migrated.

bar_text: Wos owa anhaund vo de Bodnfund ned richti is.
english: But what is not quite right based on the ground finds.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Bairische Ethnogenese hod se zeascht netta im Laund zwischn de Fliss Lech und Traun ogschpuid.
english: Bavarian ethnogenesis first played itself out in the land between the rivers Lech and Traun.
note: Omits netta, explicitly only in the initial Lech-Traun area.

bar_text: Easchtmolig wean de Baiern vom Jordanes im Joahr 551 in seina Gotngschicht eawähnt.
english: For the first time, the Bavarians are mentioned by Jordanes in his book of history in the year 551.
note: Omits that Jordanes's history is specifically Gothic history.

bar_text: Do bschreibd ea an Kaumpf vo an Gotnschtaumm untam Kini Theodemir mid de Suebn (Donausuebn de aus Panonien za de Alemannen gflohn san).
english: He describes a fight of a mountain tribe under King Theodemir with the Suebi (Danube Suebi who fled from Pannonia to the Alemanni).
note: Gotnschtaumm means a Gothic tribe, not a mountain tribe.

bar_text: Des soid se im Winta 469/470 ogschpuid hom.
english: That should have played itself out in the winter 469/470.
note: Should have suggests expectation rather than the source's reportative is said to have.

bar_text: Da Kini Theodemir hod de Gotn iwa an zuagfroana Fluss in Ruckkn vo de Suebn gfiad und so gschlong.
english: King Theodemir led the gods across a frozen river behind the Suebi and thus struck them down.
note: Gotn means Goths, not gods.

bar_text: ...Nam regio illa Suavorum ab oriente Baioras habet, ab occidente Francos, a meridie Burgundiones, a septemtrione Thuringos; quibus Suavis tunc iuncti adherant Alamanni...
english: ...That region of the Suebi is bordered by the Bavarians to the east, the Franks to the west, the Burgundians to the south, and the Thuringians to the north; to whom the Suebi were then joined and adhere, the Alamanni...
note: Misparses the last clause: the Alamanni were joined to the Suebi, not the Suebi to the Alamanni.

bar_text: Des Gebiet vo de Suebn hod im Ostn de Baiern, im Westn de Frankn, im Sidn de Burgunda, im Noadn de Thüringa.
english: The territory of the Swabians has the Bavarians in the east, the Franks in the west, the Burgundians in the south, and the Thuringians in the north.
note: Swabians is an imprecise modern/regional label for the historical Suebi in this context.

bar_text: De Suebn haum se domois de Alemannen augschlossn.
english: The Suebi had shut out the Alemanni back then.
note: augschlossn here means joined, not shut out.

bar_text: Boarisch bzw. bairisch wean fias Sprochgebiet vawendt.
english: Bavarian or bairisch is used for the language area.
note: Anglicizes the cited spelling Boarisch to Bavarian, losing one of the precise forms being contrasted.

bar_text: Bayerisch und Bayrisch beziang se dageng afs politische Territorium vom Freistoot Bayern.
english: Bavarian and Bayrisch refer to the political territory of the Free State of Bavaria.
note: Replaces the cited Bayerisch form with Bavarian, weakening the spelling contrast.

bar_text: De Untascheidung is notwendi, wei in Bayern außa da boarischn Sproch (in Oidbayern) aa no fränkisch und schwäbisch-alemannisch gredt wead.
english: This distinction is necessary because in Bavaria, besides the Bavarian language (in Old Bavaria), Franconian and Swabian-Alemannic are also spoken.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S boarische Sprochgebiet liegt – vo Sprochinsln obgseng – in Bayern, Östareich und Sidtiroi.
english: The Bavarian language area lies – apart from language islands – in Bavaria, Austria and South Tyrol.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De historische Schreibweis Baiern fias bayerische Stootsgebiet is im 19. Joarhundat duach an Kini Ludwig I. duach de Schreibweis Bayern, oisdonn mid y, dasetzt worn.
english: The historical spelling Baiern for the Bavarian state territory was replaced in the 19th century by King Ludwig I with the spelling Bayern, then with a y.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Mid mea wia 12 Milliona Sprechan buidt's Boarische s gresste zammahängande Sprochgebiet innahoib vo de deitschn Sprochn.
english: With more than 12 million speakers, Bavarian forms the largest contiguous language area within the German languages.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da boarische Sprochraum hod um de 150.000 km².
english: The Bavarian language area is about 150,000 km².
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Niamberga Raum is a fränkisch-boarischa Iwagongsdialekt behoamat, wo zwoa iwawiagend ostfränkische Meakmoi afwoast, owa bsundas im Woatschotz stoake boarische Eifliss dakenna losst.
english: In the Nuremberg area, a Franconian-Bavarian transition dialect is at home, which deviates from two overriding East Franconian characteristics, but especially in the vocabulary, lets strong Bavarian influences be recognized.
note: Shows predominantly East Franconian features becomes deviates from two overriding features.

bar_text: S Boarische ko ohand vo sprochliche Meakmoi in drei Groußraim eihteit wern: Noad-, Middl- und Siidboarisch.
english: Bavarian can be divided into three large areas based on linguistic characteristics: North, Middle, and South Bavarian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Zwischn dena Bereichn san jeweis Iwagangsraime, de wo Noadmiddlboarisch und Sidmiddlboarisch gnennd wean.
english: Between these areas there are respectively transition zones, which are called North Bavarian and South Bavarian.
note: Drops Middle/Central from both transition-zone names, changing them to the main North/South categories.

bar_text: Noadboarisch is oane vo de drei Haptgruppm (Noadboarisch, Middlboarisch, Siidboarisch), in de wo de Boarische Sproch sprochwissnschaftli eihteit wead.
english: Upper Bavarian is one of the three main groups (Upper Bavarian, Middle Bavarian, South Bavarian) into which the Bavarian language is linguistically divided.
note: Changes North Bavarian to Upper Bavarian.

bar_text: Noadboarisch wead heitzatog im gräistn Deu vo da Owapfoiz gredt.
english: Nowadays, people are talking about the greatest German of the Upper Palatinate.
note: Northern Bavarian spoken through most of Upper Palatinate becomes talking about the greatest German there.

bar_text: Im Siidostn (in da sidestlichn Owoapfoiz und im neadlichn Nidabayern) ab Rengschbuag zwischan Reng und da Doana owezua bis duif in boarischn Woid eine wiad a Mischfoam des Noadmiddlboarische gsprocha.
english: In the southeast (in the southern part of the Upper Palatinate and in northern Lower Bavaria) from Regensburg down towards Regensburg between Regensburg and the Danube deep into the Bavarian Forest, a mixed dialect called Middle Bavarian will be spoken.
note: Changes North-Central to Central Bavarian, confuses Regen with Regensburg and shifts the speech to the future.

bar_text: In sidestlichn Eck vo Middlfrankn, in middlestlichn Eck vo Obafrankn, im aissastn Noadn vo Obabayern und z aissaste Sidvogdland (Saxn).
english: In the western corner of Middle Franconia, in the central corner of Upper Franconia, in the northernmost part of Upper Bavaria and in the northernmost part of the Palatinate (Saxony).
note: Southeastern Middle Franconia becomes western, and southern Vogtland becomes northern Palatinate.

bar_text: Middlboarisch wead z Niedabayern, Obabayern, im Sidn vo da Obapfoiz (Noadmidlboarisch), im neadlichn Soizburga Land (Flochgau und Tennengau), z Owaestareich, Nidaestareich, im neadlichn Burgnland und z Wean gredt.
english: Middle Bavarian is spoken in Lower Bavaria, Upper Bavaria, in the south of Upper Palatinate (North Middle Bavarian), in the northern Salzburg Land (Flachgau and Tennengau), in Lower Austria, Lower Austria, in the northern Burgenland and in Vienna.
note: Upper Austria becomes a repeated Lower Austria, losing one region.

bar_text: Es hod an groußn Eihfluss af seine Schwestadialekte im Noadn und Sidn.
english: It has a great influence on its sister dialects in the north and south.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Siidboarisch wead im Werdnfejsa Land, z Noad- Ost- und Sidtiroi, Karntn, in Tein vo da Steiamoak (voa oim in da Weststeiamoak) und in de deitschn Sprochinsln z Karnien gredt.
english: South Bavarian is spoken in the Werdensee region, in North-East and South Tyrol, Carinthia, in parts of Styria (primarily in West Styria) and in the German language islands in Carnia.
note: Changes Werdenfels to Werdensee and combines separate North and East Tyrol into North-East Tyrol.

bar_text: Fost de gonze Steiamoak, de Soizburga Oipngaue und s Tirola Untaland ghean zum Iwagongsgebiet zwischn Middl- und Siidboarisch.
english: Almost the entire Styrian part, the Salzburg Alpine foothills, and the Tyrolean lowlands belong to the transition area between Middle and South Bavarian.
note: The Salzburg Alpine districts become foothills.

bar_text: Aa s Zarzarische und s Göttscheabarische san siidboarisch.
english: Both Zarzarische and Göttscheabarische are South Bavarian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A bsondare Variantn is des Zimbrische.
english: A special variant is the Zimbrische.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es hod si scho in oidhochdeitscha Zeid obgsondat und wead heit no in obaitalienischn Sprochinseln vo de Zimbarn gredd.
english: It has already separated itself in Old High German times and will still be spoken today in the Upper Italian language islands of the Zimbarn.
note: Present continued speech is shifted to will still be spoken today.

bar_text: Nem dena historischn "Isoglossn" ko s Boarische aa no in weidane Dialekte untagliedat wern.
english: With these historical "isoglosses," Bavarian can also be subdivided into further dialects.
note: With changes the relation from subdivisions in addition to the historical isoglosses to subdivisions using them.

bar_text: A Bsundaheit is Weanarische, owa aa s Mingarische.
english: A specialty is Viennese, but also Mingarian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: In Östareich gibts u. a. no s Hianzische im Burgenland, de steirischn Mundoartn, Karntnarisch und de Tirolarischn Mundoartn.
english: In Austria, there are, among other things, still the Hianzisch in Burgenland, the Styrian dialects, Carinthian, and the Tyrolean dialects.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A sea oagna Dialekt in Owaösterreich is de Mundoart vom Soizkammaguat und in Niedabayern s Waidlarische.
english: A lot of dialects in Upper Austria is the dialect of the Salzkammergut and in Lower Bavaria the Waidlarische.
note: A very distinctive dialect becomes a lot of dialects, while the two location/name associations remain.

bar_text: Dazua kema s Zimbrische (Owaitalien), s Göttscheabarische (Slowenien) und s Egerdeitsche (Behmen).
english: To that come the Cimrian (Upper Italy), the Görtschabarian (Slovenia) and the Eger German (Bohemia).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: As Boarische untascheidt lange und kuaze Vokai.
english: The Bavarian distinction [is] long and short vocals.
note: Vokai are vowels, not vocals; the target misidentifies the category.

bar_text: Wia im Standarddeitschn wead des duach de Ozoi vo de nochfoigadn Konsonantn zum Ausdruck brocht.
english: As in standard German, this is expressed through the number of the following consonants.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Stäht nua oa oda goa koa Konsonant nochm Vokaj, dann is dea in da Regl lang; wann zwoa oda mehrane Konsonantn foign dann is a kuaz.
english: If only one or no consonant follows the vowel, then it is usually long; if two or more consonants follow, then it is short.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Boarischn san siem Vokaj untascheidboa.
english: In Bavarian, there are two distinguishable vowels.
note: Changes seven vowels to two.

bar_text: Phonologisch untascheidn de boarischnn Dialekt zwischn bis zu drei a-Qualitetn.
english: Phonologically, the Bavarian dialects distinguish between up to three a-qualities.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Des hoasst, es wead teiweis zwischn hejm a (à), middlan a (a) und dungln a (o/å) untaschiedn.
english: That means, there will be a distinction sometimes between hejm a (à), middlan a (a) and dungln a (o/å).
note: Leaves the key bright/middle/dark labels untranslated and shifts a current distinction into the future.

bar_text: Des helle a (à) kimmt ausm Middlhochdeitschn ä, bzw. vo de Diphthongen ou/öu, im Weanarischn aa ausm Diphthong ei.
english: The "a" (à) comes from Middle High German "ê", or from the diphthongs "ou/öu", and in Viennese also from the diphthong "ei".
note: Changes ä to ê and omits the bright quality label.

bar_text: So hoassts im Boarischn laa (lààr) im Vagleich zu standarddeitsch leer, ausm mhd.
english: In Bavarian, it is called "laa" (lààr) in comparison to standard German "leer", from Middle High German.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: lære, i glaab (i glààb) im Vagleich zu ich glaube, aus ich g(e)loube, wean.
english: learn, in belief (I believe) in comparison to I believe, from I believe, become.
note: The cited phonological forms collapse into learn/in belief/I believe and the Viennese abbreviation becomes become.

bar_text: haaß (hààß) im Vergleich zu hoaß und heiß, ois aum mhd.
english: haaß (hààß) in comparison to hoaß and heiß, all from Middle High German.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: heiz.
english: heat.
note: The cited adjective form heiz is lost and misglossed as the noun/verb heat.

bar_text: De Vatretung fian middlhochdeitschn a-Laut is dagegn fia gwähnli a „vadunklts“, des wo scho ins o iwageht.
english: The representation for the Middle High German a-sound is against it, for a while a "darkened" one, which already flows into one.
note: Usually becomes for a while and the phoneme o becomes one, corrupting the phonological relation.

bar_text: So wead aus middelhochdeitsch wazzer, hase, wâr beispuisweis Wossa (Wåsser), Hos (Håås), woa (wåår) im Vagleich zu standarddeitsch Wasser, Hase und wahr.
english: So Middle High German water, hare, was, for example, Wossa (Wåsser), Hos (Håås), woa (wåår) in comparison to standard German Wasser, Hase and wahr.
note: Replaces cited Middle High German forms with English glosses and misreads wâr as was, losing the phonological comparisons.

bar_text: Regional ko s a zu Variationa zwischn dunklem und middlan a gebm (schaug mia homma/mia håmma/mia hamma).
english: Regionally, there are variations between a dark and medium 'a' (look, we have/mia homma/mia håmma/mia hamma).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Vor oim bei da Diminutivbuidung mitn Suffixen -l und -al tritt Umlaut ein, d. h. aus dunklem a (o/å) wead helles a (à).
english: Above all, in diminutive formation with the suffixes -l and -al, umlaut occurs, i.e., from dark a (o/å) becomes light a (à).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: In fost oin boarischen Ortsnama, de wo af -ing endn, muass a ggf. im Stamm vorhandans -a- hej ausgsprocha wean; oiso „Plattling (Plàttling)“ (und ned „Plottling oda Plåttling“) und „Gaching (Gàching)“ (stott *„Gorching oda Gårching“), aa „Gamisch (Gàmisch)“ (stott „Gormisch oda Gårmisch“) und „Graz (Gràz)“ (ned „Groz oda Gråz“ – de Stod hod im Middloida „Grätz“ ghoassn, und daraus hod si s helle a entwicket).
english: In almost all Bavarian place names that end in -ing, a possibly existing -a- in the stem must be pronounced as "ej"; so "Plattling (Plàttling)" (and not "Plottling or Plåttling") and "Gaching (Gàching)" (instead of *"Gorching or Gårching"), also "Gamisch (Gàmisch)" (instead of "Gormisch or Gårmisch") and "Graz (Gràz)" (not "Groz or Gråz" – the city was called "Grätz" in the Middle Ages, and the latter developed from it).
note: hej means bright here, not pronunciation as ej; the final bright-a development is also obscured.

bar_text: Ausnahma san owa manche Ortsnama mit -all- wia „Boing (Bålling/Båing)“ (Palling) oda „Dolling (Dålling)“ (Thalling).
english: Exceptions are, however, some place names with -all- like „Boing (Bålling/Båing)“ (Palling) or „Dolling (Dålling)“ (Thalling).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S helle a (à) wead im Boarischen gwehnlich ois a wiedagem, s dunkle a (å) dagegn moastns ois o, (oiso mocha statt måcha).
english: The light a (à) becomes in Bavarian usually all a again, the dark a (å) against it most often all, (so mocha instead of måcha).
note: Misreads as and o as all, losing the central a/o representation rules.

bar_text: Es liegt fia deitsch Ohrn a näha am o.
english: It is close to the German ears.
note: Close to ears loses the actual comparison with o.

bar_text: Das des zum Zammafoi mitn gschlossanan o fiaht, wo im Boarischn moastns nah am ou liegt, wead vo Kritikern gern ois Oloss gnumma, de Eifiahrung vo – vom Deitschn divergiaradn – Sondazoachn in da boarischn Schreibweis z begrindn.
english: That this leads to a coincidence with the closed one, which in Bavaria is mostly located near the mouth, is gladly taken by critics as an excuse to justify the introduction of – diverging from German – special characters in the Bavarian writing style.
note: Closed o and ou become a closed one and a mouth, destroying the sound comparison.

bar_text: Es is owa so, dass aa im Stadarddeitschn, im Englischn sowia in andan indogermanischn Sprochn de gsprochan Vokai efta ned mit de gschrieban iwaeistimma.
english: But it is the case that even in standard German, in English as well as in other Indo-European languages, the spoken vowels often do not coincide with the written ones.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fost jeds betonte kurze e is im Boarischen gschlossa (im Gegnsotz zum Deitschen: do sans olle offa).
english: Almost every emphasized short e is closed in Bavarian (in contrast to German: there they are all open).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es gibt nur wenige Wärta mit an kurznm offanen e (è); a guads Beispui dafia: Bettn („Bett“, mit gschlossan e) vs. betn (bètn) („Gebet“, mit offan è).
english: There are only a few words with a short open e (è); a good example of this: Bettn (“bed”, with closed e) vs. betn (bètn) (“prayer”, with open è).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Standarddeitschn is in dem Beispui genau andasrum: s Wort „Bett“ hod a offans (wei kurzes), s Wort „beten“ a gschlossans (wei langs) e.
english: In standard German, it is exactly for a different reason in this example: the word "Bett" has an open (because short) e, the word "beten" a closed (because long) e.
note: Exactly the other way around becomes exactly for a different reason, though the two vowel facts remain.

bar_text: Nebm am unbetontn a gibts aa an weidan unbetontn Vokal im Boarischen, dea wo zwischn i und e steht, und je noch Dialekt offena (Richtung e) oda gschlossena (Richtung i) gsprocha wead.
english: Besides the unstressed a, there is also another unstressed vowel in Bavarian, which stands between i and e, and is spoken depending on the dialect either open (towards e) or closed (towards i).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Er is moastns aus da Nebmsuibm -el entstanda, z. B. in Weatan wia grabbin oda Deifi.
english: He is created from the mist column in the mornings - e.g. in stories like Grabbin or Deifi.
note: The unstressed -el syllable becomes a morning mist column, and words become stories.

bar_text: In de moastn Boarischen Dialekte hod da Schwa-Laut, dea wo am unbetontn e im Standarddeitschn entspricht, koan Phonemstatus.
english: In the most Bavarian dialects, the schwa sound, which corresponds to the unstressed e in Standard German, has no phonemic status.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Regional tritt a in bestimmten Positiona ois Allophon zua unbetontn a und i af.
english: Regionally, a also occurs in certain positions as an allophone to unstressed a and i.
note: The pronoun a refers to schwa; the target instead identifies the sound as a.

bar_text: A weindans Merkmoi vom modeana Boarischn is de Beibehoidung vo de middlhochboarischn Diphthong ie, üe, uo ois ia und ua, wia in liab, griassn, Bruada („liab, grüßen, Bruder“).
english: A clear characteristic of modern Bavarian is the preservation of the Middle High Bavarian diphthongs ie, üe, uo as ia and ua, as in liab, griassn, Bruada (“liab, grüßen, Bruder”).
note: Changes another/further characteristic to a clear characteristic.

bar_text: A bsundas Merkmoi vom Boarischn is da Vokal oa (im Weanarischn aa ausgsprocha), dea wo ausm middlhochdeitschn ei entstanda is.
english: A special feature of Bavarian is the vowel oa (also pronounced in Viennese), which arose from the Middle High German ei.
note: aa in the parenthesis is the Viennese pronunciation, not the word also; that pronunciation is lost.

bar_text: Dea Lautwandl betrifft owa nurs sogennnte ejtare ei vom Deitschen, ned owa s jingare ei, des wo eascht im Zug vo da neihochdeitschn Diphthongiarung ausm middlhochdeitschn langan i (î) entstanda is, und daher an Lautwandl ned mehr mitgmocht hod.
english: This sound change, however, only affects the so-called older part of German, not the younger part, which only arose in the course of the New High German diphthongization from the Middle High German long i (î), and therefore did not participate in a sound change anymore.
note: The older and younger ei sounds become older and younger parts of German, losing the actual phonological targets.

bar_text: Deshoib hoassts af Boarisch hoid „oans, zwoa, drei“ (oans und zwoa hom a ejtas ei ois Stammvokal, drei a jingas ei, des wo af Middlhochdeitsch no drî ghoassn hod.
english: That's why in Bavarian it's just called "one, two, three" (one and two have an old ei as a stem vowel, three a younger ei, which was still called drî in Middle High German.
note: Replaces the essential cited oans/zwoa/drei forms with English one/two/three, erasing the oa contrast.

bar_text: Olladings gibts im Boarischn no dritts, no jigas ei, des wo durch de Entrundung vom Diphthong nhd.
english: Anyway, there is still a third thing in Bavarian, don't enter it yet, that which [comes] through the denasalization of the diphthong nhd.
note: Even younger ei becomes don't enter it yet and unrounding becomes denasalization.

bar_text: eu, äu entstanda is, dea wo vom Langvokal mhd.
english: eu, eu arose, that which from the long vowel Middle High German.
note: Changes the second cited form äu to a repeated eu.

bar_text: iu, bzw. mhd.
english: yes, or rather Middle High German.
note: Changes the cited vowel form iu to yes.

bar_text: öu obstammt.
english: all fruit.
note: All fruit does not convey descent from the vowel form öu.

bar_text: (De Entrundung hod owa in de moastn Tirola Mundoatn ned stottgfundn.)
english: (However, the de-runcation did not take place in the most Tyrolean Mundoatn.)
note: Unrounding becomes an undefined de-runcation and dialects remains untranslated.

bar_text: Um aussazfindn, wos fia a deitsches ei im Boarischen zu oa wead, und wos fia oans ned, huift moastns a Blick afs Englische.
english: To find out what kind of German "ei" becomes "oa" in Bavarian, and what kind doesn't, a look at English usually helps.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Englischn entspricht s ejtare ei moast am o oda ea, s jingare is dagegn a i und wead ähnli ausgesprocha wia im Boarischn.
english: In English, the "-age" corresponds to a "moast" (most) to an "o" or "ea", the "-ing" is conversely an "i" and will be pronounced similarly to in Bavarian.
note: Older/younger ei become -age/-ing and moast is left as an object, destroying the sound correspondences.

bar_text: Geistliche Weata
english: Spiritual weather
note: Weata means words here, not weather.

bar_text: Es gibt owa Ausnahma vo da Lautwandlregl ei > oa, de wo vor oim Weata betreffa, de wo durch ian Brauch im vom Godsdeanst in iara oidn Gstoit bewoart worn san; dabei handeltsa si um Geist, Fleisch, heilig und en Monatsnam Mai, de wo normalaweis Goast, Floasch, hoalig, und Moa hoassn miassadn, owa so im Boarischn extrem sejtn sand.
english: However, there are exceptions to the sound change rule > one, which primarily concern words that have been preserved in their old form through their custom in the divine service; these are about spirit, flesh, holy and the month name May, which would normally have to be called Goast, Floasch, hoalig, and Moa, but are extremely rare in Bavarian.
note: Corrupts ei > oa to > one and replaces the essential German cited word forms with English glosses.

bar_text: Dabei is da Laut j a Hoibvokal.
english: In this case, the sound 'j' is a semivowel.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Obwoi de Fortis-Vaschlusslaute p und t mit ian Lenis-Pendants b und d im Olaut zammagfoin san, kenna se ned ois zwoa Allophone jeweis vo an Phonem gejtn, wei si in gwissn Positiona bedeitungsuntascheidend san.
english: Even though the Fortis closure sounds p and t have merged with their lenis counterparts b and d in the nucleus vowel, they cannot be considered as two allophones of each respective phoneme, because they are meaning-insignificant in certain positions.
note: Word-initial position becomes nucleus vowel, and meaning-distinguishing becomes meaning-insignificant.

bar_text: Nur im Olaut kenna si ois Variantn ogseng wian, vo dena wo de Aussproch vom nochfoigandn Laut obhängt (schaug dazua weida untn iwan Glottisschlag).
english: Only in Old High German can they be seen as variants, of which the pronunciation depends on the following sound (look further down at the glottal stop).
note: Word-initial position becomes Old High German.

bar_text: In da boarischn Sproch san de fortis- und lenis-Vaschlusslaute p, t, k und b, d, g im Olaut und zwischn Vokalen moastns zammagfoin und weadn daher ned weida untaschiedn.
english: In the Bavarian language, the fortis and lenis consonants p, t, k and b, d, g in the allophone and between vowels mostly merged and therefore are not further distinguished.
note: The word-initial environment becomes in the allophone.

bar_text: Deshoib ko im Boarischn da Dog oda da Tog, as Greiz oda as Kreiz, und de da Bädasui oda da Pedasui gschriem wean und deshoib foin Werta wia dringa (dringen) und dringa (trinka) zamma.
english: That is why in Bavarian the day or the day, the border or the cross, and those who are written as the bath-sui or the foot-sui, and that is why words like dringa (to press/to urge) and dringa (to drink) fall together.
note: Loses Dog/Tog and Greiz/Kreiz spellings through glosses, misreads cross as border and parsley forms as bath/foot.

bar_text: Als oanziga fortis-Laut ist k- am Wortofang dahoidn, wann eam a Vokal nochfoigt; vor r, l und n wead er ebenfois zum g lenisiat.
english: As the only strong consonant, k- is maintained at the beginning of a word when a vowel follows it; before r, l, and n, it is likewise lenited to g.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Laute b, d und g wean owa am Wortofang vor s, sch, f und h fortisiat; de neien fortis-Laute hom owa koan Phonem-, sondan nur Allophon-Status, wei se nur in bestimmta Umgebung aftretn, wo eanare lenis-Variantn ned vorkema.
english: The sounds b, d and g will however be fortified at the beginning of a word before s, sch, f and h; the new fortis sounds however have no phoneme, but only allophone status, because they only occur in a certain environment where their lenis variants do not occur.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Und daher vahoidn sa se zu dena ned bedeitungsuntascheidend.
english: And therefore they claim to themselves that those are not significantly different.
note: Behave in relation to becomes claim to themselves, and semantic distinctiveness becomes general difference.

bar_text: S Boarische kennt fimf Frikative; f (stimmlos) und w (stimmhoft) buidn dabei a Poar.
english: Bavarian knows five fricatives; f (voiceless) and w (voiced) form a pair in the process.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da Frikativ s is außa vor n imma stimmlos, oiso im Gengsotz zum Deitschn aa am Wortofang.
english: The fricative [f] is always voiceless outside of [v], so in contrast to German, also at the beginning of a word.
note: Changes s to f and except before n to outside v.

bar_text: Dazua keman de mit Buchstabmkombinationa gschriebanan Laute ch und sch, wobei ch ois Allophon [x] oda [ç] (noch -i- oda -e-) zu olautendn h [h] im In- oda Auslaut aftritt.
english: Added to this are the sounds ch and sch written with letter combinations, where ch occurs as the allophone [x] or [ç] (after -i- or -e-) and as the fully pronounced h [h] in syllable onset or coda.
note: Initial h with medial/final ch allophones becomes h also in syllable onset/coda, with initial misread as fully pronounced.

bar_text: Da Laut ch kimmt andas ois im Standarddeitschen ned noch -n- vor, daher Minga, mank, Menk vs. stdt.
english: The sound 'ch' comes differently than in Standard German - it comes before 'n-' - therefore Minga, mank, Menk vs. stdt.
note: Not after n becomes occurs before n, changing both the condition and polarity.

bar_text: München, manch, Mönch.
english: Munich, many, monk.
note: Translates away the German ch-bearing forms that are the phonological examples; manch is also imprecisely many.

bar_text: S Boarische hod s gleiche Sonorantninventar wia s Standarddeitsche, nämli de Nasallaute m, n und ng [ŋ] sowia l, r und j. S r wead in mangn Gegandn mit da Zunganspitzn geroit, in andan Gegandn mitn Gaumenzapfal (sog. uvulares r), ohne dass des vo Boarisch-Sprechan ois Fehla empfundn wead.
english: Bavarian has the same sonorant inventory as Standard German, namely the nasal sounds m, n and ng [ŋ] as well as l, r and j. The r is produced with the tip of the tongue in many regions, in other regions with the uvula (so-called uvular r), without this being perceived as an error when speaking Bavarian.
note: Produced omits the explicitly rolled/trilled manner of r.

bar_text: Da stimmlose glottale Plosiv (Glottisschlag) tritt wia im Standarddeitschn vorm vokalischn Olaut (duatn vapflichtend) af.
english: The voiceless glottal plosive (glottal stop) occurs, as in Standard German, before a vocalic semivowel (mandatory).
note: Vowel-initial onset becomes semivowel and mandatory loses its Standard-German scope.

bar_text: Im Gengasotz dazua is des oba nur am Sotzofang oda am Ofang vo am Einschub vapflichtend: Sunstan ko ma Weata owa scho zammziagn.
english: In the counter-clause to that, however, it is only mandatory at the beginning of a sentence or at the beginning of an insertion: On Sunday, one can, however, pull oneself together.
note: Sunstan means otherwise, not Sunday; joining words becomes pulling oneself together.

bar_text: De gsamte boarische Nominalflexion richt si am Substantiv aus.
english: The entire Bavarian nominal inflection is based on the noun.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S grammatische Gschlecht (Genus) vom Haptwort bestimmt de Deklination vo da Nominalphrasn; d. h. sowoi da Artikl ois aa s Adjektiv und andare Attribute miassn in Genus, Kasus und Numerus ans Substantiv, wo se begleitn, anglicha wean.
english: The grammatical gender (genus) of the main word determines the declension of the noun phrase; i.e., both the article as well as the adjective and other attributes must become similar to the noun they accompany in gender, case, and number.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S gibt drei Genera: maskulin, feminin und neutrum.
english: There are three genders: masculine, feminine and neuter.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ois paradigmatische Kategorien gibts de Fälle (Kasus) Nominativ, Dativ und Akkusativ sowia de Numeri Singular und Plural.
english: As paradigmatic categories, there are the cases (Kasus) nominative, dative and accusative as well as the numbers singular and plural.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Adjektive käna aa gsteigat wean.
english: Adjectives cannot be increased.
note: Cannot negates can; gsteigat refers to adjective comparison.

bar_text: Da unbstimmte Artikl is dageng fia olle drei Genera im Nominativ identisch
english: The indefinite article is therefore identical for all three genders in the nominative.
note: Therefore changes the source's contrast marker dageng/however into a causal link.

bar_text: Da Artikl wead im Boarischn flektiat, d. h. da Kasus wead so deitli gmochd.
english: The article is inflected in Bavarian, i.e., the case is made so clearly.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wei de moastn Substantive im Boarischn olle Kasusendunga valuan hom, wead da Kasus praktisch nur iwan Artikl ozoagt.
english: Since most nouns in Bavarian have lost all case endings, the case is practically only shown via the article.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da unbestimmte Artikl is etymologisch duach de unbetonte Aussproch vom Zoiwort "oa" entstondn (noch oidboarischa Schreibung <ain>, gsprochn /oã/).
english: The indefinite article etymologically arose through the unstressed pronunciation of the numeral "oa" (according to Old Bavarian spelling <ain>, pronounced /oã/).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da unbestimmte Artikl wead z. B. ois /ə/, /ɐ/ o.
english: The indefinite article is, for example, pronounced as /ə/, /ɐ/.
note: The completed list omits the source's trailing or indicating further similar realizations.

bar_text: ä. ausgsprochen, im Dativ z. B. /ənə/, /ɐnɐ/ o.
english: ä. pronounced, in the dative e.g. /ənə/, /ɐnɐ/ or.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: ä. Gschriebm wead da unbestimmte Artikl in da boarischn Dialektliteratur und heitign Umschriftn, z. B. in Internetforen, haifi ois <a>, sejten aa ois <oa>, im Dativ ois <ana>, vor oim im Dat.
english: e. The indefinite article is written in Bavarian dialect literature and today's transcriptions, e.g., in internet forums, often as <a>, sometimes also as <oa>, in the dative as <ana>, especially in the dat.
note: Changes the rarity of oa to sometimes.

bar_text: aa ois <oana>.
english: also everything <one>.
note: As becomes everything and the actual spelling oana becomes one.

bar_text: Im Ostmiddlboarischn imma ois <a> und <ana>.
english: In East Central Bavarian, it is always all <a> and <ana>.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: As Substantiv gheat im Boarischn zu de flektiaradn Woatoartn.
english: As a noun, it belongs to the inflected parts of speech in Bavarian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wia in andane germanische Sprochn is es Geschlecht (Genus) es markantaste Kriterium vom Haptwort.
english: As in other Germanic languages, gender (genus) is the most prominent criterion of the noun.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: E Boarische hod no drei vo de urspringli via germanischn Kasus: Nominativ, Dativ und Akkusativ.
english: A Bavarian has still three of the original via Germanic cases: nominative, dative and accusative.
note: The language becomes a Bavarian person and the total original four is left as via.

bar_text: De letztn zwoa foin zum Tei zamma.
english: The last two sometimes fall together.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da Genitiv is nur in a poar Redewendunga dahoidn.
english: The genitive is only preserved in a few idioms.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wia im Standarddeitschn wead es boarische Substantiv nur sejtn dekliniat, sundan druckd an Kasus durch de Artikl aus.
english: As in standard German, the Bavarian noun is not only declined in the singular, but expresses the case through the article.
note: Rarely declined becomes not only declined in the singular, inventing a number-based restriction.

bar_text: Es gibt vaschiedane Deklinationsklassn, de wo se haptsächli in da Pluralbuidung untascheidn.
english: There are different declension classes, which mainly differ in plural formation.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ois grobe Richtlinie wead zwischn da schwochn Deklination (sog. n-Klasse) und da stoarkn Deklination (sog. a-Klasse) untaschiedn.
english: As a rough guideline, a distinction will be made between the weak declension (so-called n-class) and the strong declension (so-called a-class).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Schwoche Substantive endn fia gewähnlich af -n im Plural.
english: Weak nouns usually end in -n in the plural.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Vui schwoche Feminina buidn an Singular af es Suffix -n, so dass se im Plural entweda glei hoassn oda a -a ofiagn.
english: Many feminine words form a singular on the suffix -n, so that they in the plural either are called the same or end with an -a.
note: Omits the weak-declension restriction on the feminine nouns.

bar_text: Bsundas de schwochn Maskulina hom im Singular a Endung fia de obliquen Kasus, d. h. fia olle Kasus aussam Nominativ.
english: Especially the weak masculines have an ending in the singular for the oblique cases, i.e., for all cases except the nominative.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Se hom moastns a -n am End.
english: They usually have a -n at the end.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Zua Klassn vo de schwochn Substantive (W1) zejn Maskulina und Feminina af -n im Plural und aa olle Feminina mit da Pluralendung -an (de moastns im Singular af -ng endn; es -a- is dabei a sog. Sprossvokal bzw. epenthetisch).
english: For the class of weak substantives (W1), list masculines and feminines ending in -n in the plural and also all feminines with the plural ending -an (which most often end in -ng in the singular; an -a- is a so-called epenthetic vowel).
note: zejn means count/belong here; list turns the membership statement into an instruction.

bar_text: Driwa ausse lossa se olle Maskulina und Neutra, de wo im Singular af es Suffix -i endn, do einordna.
english: Let all masculines and neuters that end in the suffix -i in the singular be classified outside.
note: Driwa ausse means additionally here, not classification outside the class.

bar_text: Bei de stoarkn Deklinationsklassn gibts koane Kasusendungan; de oanzige Vaendarung am Woat findt bei da Numerusflexion stodd, oisdann beim Wechsel vom Singular zun Plural.
english: With the strong declension classes, there are no case endings; the only change to the word takes place during the number inflection, i.e., during the change from singular to plural.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es gibt dabei vaschiedene Meglichkeitn, an Plural im Boarischn z markian.
english: There are various possibilities to mark a plural in Bavarian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Stoarke Maskulina und Neutra nutzen de Endung -a, de moast aus da middelhochdeitschen Endung -er entstandn und ois soiche im Neihochdeitschn no dahoidn is.
english: Strong masculine and neuter nouns use the ending -a, which mostly arose from the Middle High German ending -er and as such is still preserved in New High German.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es gibt oba a Weata, de wo se eascht in neia Zeit in de Klase eingreiht hom, oiso an a-Plural buidn, ohne jemois an er-Plural ghobt z hom.
english: But there are also words that only formed a plural in modern times, so they form a plural, without ever having had an er-plural.
note: Joining this class recently becomes only forming a plural in modern times; the a-plural marker is lost.

bar_text: Feminina buidn eanan Plural oft mit da Endung -an, so wias es Woat Endung sejm duat: oa Endung, zwoa Endungan.
english: Feminine nouns often form their plural with the ending -an, just as the word ending does: one ending, two endings.
note: The essential Endungan example is replaced with English endings, which does not illustrate -an.

bar_text: Ma ko Substantive afgrund eanara Pluralsforman in vaschiedene Klassn eintein.
english: One can classify nouns according to their plural forms into different classes.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De haifigstn Meglichkeitn vo da Pluralbuidung san Umlaut od Suffigiarung; boade Meglichkeitn kena aa kombiniad wean.
english: The most common possibilities for plural formation are umlaut or suffixation; both possibilities can also be combined.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De do ogfiadn Beispui buidn de de Klass 1 und 2 vo de stoarkn Substantive, vo dena as Kennzeichn a Umlautplural is.
english: These examples here form the classes 1 and 2 of the strong substantives, which are characterized by an umlaut plural.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Klass (S1) hod nebmam Umlaut koa weidas Pluralkennzoachn, is oiso endungslos; ia ghean nur Maskulina und Feminina o. Oft kimmt im Plural no a Vokalkiazung dazua, beispuisweis: Hand – Händt, Stod – Städt, Wand – Wändt, Grund – Grindt.
english: The class (S1) has no further plural markers besides the umlaut, so it is thus endless; it only belongs to masculines and feminines. Often, a vowel shortening is also added in the plural, for example: Hand – Händt, Stod – Städt, Wand – Wändt, Grund – Grindt.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Zua Klass S2, de wo im Umlautplural plus Endung -a (de wo moastns da deitschn Endung -er entspricht) hom, ghean oanige Maskulina und vui Neutra.
english: To the class S2, which has the umlaut plural plus the ending -a (which mostly corresponds to the German ending -er), belong some masculines and many neuters.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es gejten de gleichn Umlautregeln wia obm:
english: The same umlaut rules apply as above:
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Zur Klasse S3 ghean olle Maskulina, Feminina und Neutra ohne Umlaut mit Pluralendung -a; dabei endn de moastn Feminina im Singular af de urspringlige Dativendung -n.
english: Class S3 includes all masculines, feminines, and neuters without an umlaut with the plural ending -a; in doing so, most feminines end in the singular with the original dative ending -n.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ois letzte storke Klasse (S4) gejten Substantive mit Nullplural, zum Beispui ‚Fisch‘
english: In the last strong class (S4), nouns with zero plural apply, for example 'Fisch'
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: (m) und ‚Schof‘
english: (m) and 'Schof'
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: In manchen Dialektn druckn de Substantive den Plural owa durch Vokalkiazung oda -längung aus, beispuisweis da Hund und de Hundt.
english: In some dialects, the nouns express the plural through vowel shortening or lengthening, for example the dog and the dogs.
note: Translates away da Hund/de Hundt into dog/dogs, replacing the vowel-change example with English suffixation.

bar_text: De Klass bstäht eigentli nur aus Maskulina und Neutra; olle Feminina af -n, de wo historisch gseng zu de schwochn Substantivn ghean, kena owa aa dazuazejt wean, wei ia Plural ebenso unmarkiat is: ‚Antn – Antn‘ „Ente“.
english: The class actually consists only of masculines and neuters; all feminines ending in -n, which historically belong to the weak nouns, can however also be counted among them, because their plural is likewise unmarked: 'Antn – Antn' "duck".
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Feminina wexln owa langsam zur Gruppe S3 und nehman im Plural de Endung -a o (vgl. obm s Beispui Ein „Eule“).
english: The feminine forms are however slowly changing to group S3 and take the ending -a in the plural (cf. the example above, an "Eule").
note: The formal example Ein becomes an Eule, erasing the -n noun being referenced.

bar_text: Vuifoch wead d/ iwa de Wortgrenz wegga assimiliat (Sandhi), so hoassts moastns Nom.
english: Often, it is assimilated (Sandhi) across the word boundary, so it is mostly Nom.
note: Omits the specified assimilating sound d/.

bar_text: b Vodan und b Buam(a).
english: and the father and the boy(s).
note: Translates away the actual assimilated b Vodan/b Buam(a) forms, which are the example.

bar_text: Ebenso wia Voda flektian Baua, Boi, Breiss, Depp, Buasch [österr.], Frank, Franzos, Hiasch, Hos, Läw und andare mehr.
english: Just as Father, farmers, boys, brutes, idiots, youths [Austrian], Franks, Frenchmen, rascals, scoundrels, rascals and others more.
