bar_text: Seit da Wiedavaoanigung im Joar 1990 is Berlin gsamtdeitsche Haptstod.
english: Since the reunification in the year 1990, Berlin has been the all-German capital.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Davor war des Bonn.
english: Before that, it was Bonn.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Berlin is a bedeitens Zentrum vo Politik, Medien, Kuitua und Wissnschoft in Eiropa.
english: Berlin is an important center of politics, media, culture and science in Europe.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Stod is a wichtiga Vakeahsknotnpunkt und oane vo de moastbesuchtastn Städt vom Kontinent.
english: The city is an important transport hub and one of the most visited cities on the continent.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Institutiona wia de Universitetn, Forschungseirichtunga, Theata und Museen gniassn internationale Onakennung.
english: Institutions such as universities, research facilities, theaters and museums enjoy international recognition.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Stod is a Magnet fia Kunst- und Kuituaschoffende aus da ganzn Wejd.
english: The city is a magnet for artists and cultural workers from the whole world.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: As gschichtliche Vamächtnis, as Nochtlem, und de vuifejtige Architektua san iba de Grenzn ausse bekannt.
english: The historical heritage, the nightlife, and the diverse architecture are known beyond the borders.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Berlin hod zwejf Beziak, wo insgsamt in 96 Ortstei untateit san.
english: Berlin has twelve districts, which are subdivided into a total of 96 localities.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Dazua gibts no Ortslogn, geografische Gebiet aus da Umgangssproch, wo ned genau obgrenzt wean kina.
english: In addition, there are still local names, geographical areas from colloquial language, which cannot be precisely delimited.
note: Ortslogn refers to local areas/localities, not merely local names.

bar_text: Wei de Ortstei und de Ortslogn historisch gwoxn san, spuins in da Oidogssproch a gressane Roin wia de Beziak.
english: Because the localities and the local names have grown historically, they play a large role in the local dialect, just like the districts.
note: Everyday speech becomes local dialect, and greater than boroughs becomes just like them.

bar_text: Des Woarzeichn vo Berlin is as Brandenburger Tor.
english: The landmark of Berlin is the Brandenburg Gate.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Boarisch bzw. oda Boirisch is a Sproch im Siidostn vom deitschn Sprochraum.
english: Bavarian, or Boirisch, is a language in the southeast of the German language area.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Zamma midm Alemannischn, Sidfränkischn und Ostfränkischn buidns de obadeitschn Sprochn.
english: Together with Alemannic, South Franconian, and East Franconian, they form the Upper German languages.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es Vabroadungsgebiet vom Boarischn is da oidboarische Tei vom Freistoot Bayern, es aissaste Sidvogdland in Saxn, Östareich (estli vom Arlberg), Sidtirol und de zimbrisch-karnischn Sprochinsln in Obaitalien.
english: The distribution area of Bavarian is the Old Bavarian part of the Free State of Bavaria, the authentic Carinthia in Saxony, Austria (east of the Arlberg), South Tyrol, and the Cimrian-Carnic language islands in Northern Italy.
note: The extreme southern Vogtland is changed to authentic Carinthia in Saxony.

bar_text: Meara wia de Hejft vo de Boarischn Muaddasprochla wohna aussahoib vom heitign Freistoot Bayern (Boarn).
english: More than the majority of Bavarian native speakers live outside of today's Free State of Bavaria (Bavaria).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Schaug unta: Portal:Boarisch – fia Informationa iwa d Boarische Kuitua.
english: Look below: Portal:Bavarian – for information about Bavarian culture.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fria hod ma gmoand doss da boarische bzw. bajuwarische Nama vo da kejtisch-germanischn heakimmt.
english: Previously, it was thought that the Bavarian or Bajuvarian name comes from the Celtic-Germanic.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Bezoachnung baio-wariōz bedeit sovui wia de Weahhoftn Mauna vo de Baiern .
english: The designation bajuwarisch means as much as the strong men of the Bavarians.
note: Replaces the historical form baio-warioz with bajuwarisch and weakens martial to strong.

bar_text: S Grundwort "war" existiat heit nua no ois Voadagliad in da Zammasetzung Werwolf und Wergeld.
english: The basic word 'war' only exists today as a component in the compounds Werwolf and Wergeld.
note: Component omits its explicit position as the first compound member.

bar_text: Des is a oide aus indogermanischa Zeid stommande Bezoachnung fia Mo (vagleich z. B. lateinisch vir oda s isländische Suffix -verji wia in Bæverji, Baier).
english: This is an old designation for man originating from Indo-European times (comparable to, e.g., Latin vir or the Icelandic suffix -verji as in Bæverji, Baier).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fria hod ma gsogd, de Baiern waradn de Fuaßkraungn vo da Vejkawaundarung.
english: Earlier, it was said that the Bavarians were the foot soldiers of the migration of peoples.
note: Foot soldiers does not preserve the footsore/infirm stragglers sense.

bar_text: Denn de Baiern san ned gwaundat.
english: Because the Bavarians are not wounded.
note: Not wounded does not convey not migrated.

bar_text: Wos owa anhaund vo de Bodnfund ned richti is.
english: But what is not quite right based on the ground finds.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Bairische Ethnogenese hod se zeascht netta im Laund zwischn de Fliss Lech und Traun ogschpuid.
english: Bavarian ethnogenesis first played itself out in the land between the rivers Lech and Traun.
note: Omits netta, explicitly only in the initial Lech-Traun area.

bar_text: Easchtmolig wean de Baiern vom Jordanes im Joahr 551 in seina Gotngschicht eawähnt.
english: For the first time, the Bavarians are mentioned by Jordanes in his Gothic history in the year 551.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Do bschreibd ea an Kaumpf vo an Gotnschtaumm untam Kini Theodemir mid de Suebn (Donausuebn de aus Panonien za de Alemannen gflohn san).
english: There he describes a fight of a Gothic tribe under King Theodemir with the Suebi (Danube Suebi who fled from Pannonia to the Alemanni).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Des soid se im Winta 469/470 ogschpuid hom.
english: This is said to have played itself out in the winter 469/470.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da Kini Theodemir hod de Gotn iwa an zuagfroana Fluss in Ruckkn vo de Suebn gfiad und so gschlong.
english: King Theodemir led the Goths across a frozen river behind the Suebi and thus struck them down.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: ...Nam regio illa Suavorum ab oriente Baioras habet, ab occidente Francos, a meridie Burgundiones, a septemtrione Thuringos; quibus Suavis tunc iuncti adherant Alamanni...
english: ...That region of the Suebi has the Bavarians to the east, the Franks to the west, the Burgundians to the south, and the Thuringians to the north; to whom the Suebi were then joined and adhere, the Alamanni...
note: The final clause makes the Suebi the joining party; Latin Alamanni is the subject attached to the Suebi.

bar_text: Des Gebiet vo de Suebn hod im Ostn de Baiern, im Westn de Frankn, im Sidn de Burgunda, im Noadn de Thüringa.
english: The territory of the Swabians has the Bavarians in the east, the Franks in the west, the Burgundians in the south, and the Thuringians in the north.
note: Swabians is an imprecise modern/regional label for the historical Suebi in this context.

bar_text: De Suebn haum se domois de Alemannen augschlossn.
english: The Suebi had shut out the Alemanni back then.
note: augschlossn here means joined, not shut out.

bar_text: Boarisch bzw. bairisch wean fias Sprochgebiet vawendt.
english: Bavarian or bairisch is used for the language area.
note: Anglicizes the cited spelling Boarisch to Bavarian, losing one of the precise forms being contrasted.

bar_text: Bayerisch und Bayrisch beziang se dageng afs politische Territorium vom Freistoot Bayern.
english: Bavarian and Bayrisch, on the other hand, refer to the political territory of the Free State of Bavaria.
note: Anglicizes Bayerisch to Bavarian, losing one exact y-spelling under discussion.

bar_text: De Untascheidung is notwendi, wei in Bayern außa da boarischn Sproch (in Oidbayern) aa no fränkisch und schwäbisch-alemannisch gredt wead.
english: This distinction is necessary because in Bavaria, besides the Bavarian language (in Old Bavaria), Franconian and Swabian-Alemannic are also spoken.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S boarische Sprochgebiet liegt – vo Sprochinsln obgseng – in Bayern, Östareich und Sidtiroi.
english: The Bavarian language area lies – apart from language islands – in Bavaria, Austria and South Tyrol.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De historische Schreibweis Baiern fias bayerische Stootsgebiet is im 19. Joarhundat duach an Kini Ludwig I. duach de Schreibweis Bayern, oisdonn mid y, dasetzt worn.
english: The historical spelling Baiern for the Bavarian state territory was replaced in the 19th century by King Ludwig I with the spelling Bayern, then with a y.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Mid mea wia 12 Milliona Sprechan buidt's Boarische s gresste zammahängande Sprochgebiet innahoib vo de deitschn Sprochn.
english: With more than 12 million speakers, Bavarian forms the largest contiguous language area within the German languages.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da boarische Sprochraum hod um de 150.000 km².
english: The Bavarian language area is about 150,000 km².
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Niamberga Raum is a fränkisch-boarischa Iwagongsdialekt behoamat, wo zwoa iwawiagend ostfränkische Meakmoi afwoast, owa bsundas im Woatschotz stoake boarische Eifliss dakenna losst.
english: In the Nuremberg area, a Franconian-Bavarian transition dialect is at home, which deviates from two overriding East Franconian characteristics, but especially in the vocabulary, lets strong Bavarian influences be recognized.
note: Shows predominantly East Franconian features becomes deviates from two overriding features.

bar_text: S Boarische ko ohand vo sprochliche Meakmoi in drei Groußraim eihteit wern: Noad-, Middl- und Siidboarisch.
english: Bavarian can be divided into three large areas based on linguistic characteristics: North, Middle, and South Bavarian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Zwischn dena Bereichn san jeweis Iwagangsraime, de wo Noadmiddlboarisch und Sidmiddlboarisch gnennd wean.
english: Between these areas there are respectively transition zones, which are called North Middle Bavarian and South Middle Bavarian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Noadboarisch is oane vo de drei Haptgruppm (Noadboarisch, Middlboarisch, Siidboarisch), in de wo de Boarische Sproch sprochwissnschaftli eihteit wead.
english: Upper Bavarian is one of the three main groups (Upper Bavarian, Middle Bavarian, South Bavarian) into which the Bavarian language is linguistically divided.
note: Changes North Bavarian to Upper Bavarian.

bar_text: Noadboarisch wead heitzatog im gräistn Deu vo da Owapfoiz gredt.
english: North Bavarian is spoken nowadays in the largest part of the Upper Palatinate.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Siidostn (in da sidestlichn Owoapfoiz und im neadlichn Nidabayern) ab Rengschbuag zwischan Reng und da Doana owezua bis duif in boarischn Woid eine wiad a Mischfoam des Noadmiddlboarische gsprocha.
english: In the southeast (in the southern part of the Upper Palatinate and in northern Lower Bavaria) from Regensburg down towards the Danube and deep into the Bavarian Forest, a mixed form called North Middle Bavarian is spoken.
note: Omits the Regen boundary and weakens southeastern Upper Palatinate to southern.

bar_text: In sidestlichn Eck vo Middlfrankn, in middlestlichn Eck vo Obafrankn, im aissastn Noadn vo Obabayern und z aissaste Sidvogdland (Saxn).
english: In the southeastern corner of Middle Franconia, in the central corner of Upper Franconia, in the northernmost part of Upper Bavaria and in the northernmost part of the Palatinate (Saxony).
note: Southern Vogtland becomes northern Palatinate and central-eastern Upper Franconia loses east.

bar_text: Middlboarisch wead z Niedabayern, Obabayern, im Sidn vo da Obapfoiz (Noadmidlboarisch), im neadlichn Soizburga Land (Flochgau und Tennengau), z Owaestareich, Nidaestareich, im neadlichn Burgnland und z Wean gredt.
english: Middle Bavarian is spoken in Lower Bavaria, Upper Bavaria, in the south of the Upper Palatinate (North Middle Bavarian), in the northern Salzburg Land (Flachgau and Tennengau), in Upper Austria, Lower Austria, in the northern Burgenland and in Vienna.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es hod an groußn Eihfluss af seine Schwestadialekte im Noadn und Sidn.
english: It has a great influence on its sister dialects in the north and south.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Siidboarisch wead im Werdnfejsa Land, z Noad- Ost- und Sidtiroi, Karntn, in Tein vo da Steiamoak (voa oim in da Weststeiamoak) und in de deitschn Sprochinsln z Karnien gredt.
english: South Bavarian is spoken in the Werdensee region, in North, East and South Tyrol, Carinthia, in parts of Styria (primarily in West Styria) and in the German language islands in Carnia.
note: Werdnfejsa Land is Werdenfels, not Werdensee.

bar_text: Fost de gonze Steiamoak, de Soizburga Oipngaue und s Tirola Untaland ghean zum Iwagongsgebiet zwischn Middl- und Siidboarisch.
english: Almost the entire Styria, the Salzburg Alpine foothills, and the Tyrolean lowlands belong to the transition area between Middle and South Bavarian.
note: Salzburg's Alpine Gaue/districts become Alpine foothills, a different geographic zone.

bar_text: Aa s Zarzarische und s Göttscheabarische san siidboarisch.
english: The Zarzarische and the Göttscheabarische are also South Bavarian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A bsondare Variantn is des Zimbrische.
english: A special variant is thecimbrische.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es hod si scho in oidhochdeitscha Zeid obgsondat und wead heit no in obaitalienischn Sprochinseln vo de Zimbarn gredd.
english: It has already separated itself in Old High German times and is still spoken today in the Upper Italian language islands of the Walser.
note: Changes Cimbrians to Walser.

bar_text: Nem dena historischn "Isoglossn" ko s Boarische aa no in weidane Dialekte untagliedat wern.
english: In addition to these historical 'isoglosses,' Bavarian can also be subdivided into further dialects.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A Bsundaheit is Weanarische, owa aa s Mingarische.
english: A specialty is Viennese, but also Mingarian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: In Östareich gibts u. a. no s Hianzische im Burgenland, de steirischn Mundoartn, Karntnarisch und de Tirolarischn Mundoartn.
english: In Austria, there are, among other things, still the Hianzisch in Burgenland, the Styrian dialects, Carinthian, and the Tyrolean dialects.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A sea oagna Dialekt in Owaösterreich is de Mundoart vom Soizkammaguat und in Niedabayern s Waidlarische.
english: A special dialect in Upper Austria is the dialect of the Salzkammergut and in Lower Austria the Waidlarische.
note: Niedabayern is Lower Bavaria, not Lower Austria.

bar_text: Dazua kema s Zimbrische (Owaitalien), s Göttscheabarische (Slowenien) und s Egerdeitsche (Behmen).
english: Added to these are the Zimbrish (Upper Italy), the Görtschabarian (Slovenia), and the Eger German (Bohemia).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: As Boarische untascheidt lange und kuaze Vokai.
english: Bavarian distinguishes long and short vowels.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wia im Standarddeitschn wead des duach de Ozoi vo de nochfoigadn Konsonantn zum Ausdruck brocht.
english: As in standard German, this is expressed through the number of the following consonants.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Stäht nua oa oda goa koa Konsonant nochm Vokaj, dann is dea in da Regl lang; wann zwoa oda mehrane Konsonantn foign dann is a kuaz.
english: If only one or no consonant follows the vowel, then it is usually long; if two or more consonants follow, then it is short.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Boarischn san siem Vokaj untascheidboa.
english: In Bavarian, the vowels are distinguishable.
note: Omits the specified count of seven.

bar_text: Phonologisch untascheidn de boarischnn Dialekt zwischn bis zu drei a-Qualitetn.
english: Phonologically, the Bavarian dialects distinguish between up to three a-qualities.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Des hoasst, es wead teiweis zwischn hejm a (à), middlan a (a) und dungln a (o/å) untaschiedn.
english: That means, there is sometimes a distinction between bright a (à), middle a (a), and dark a (o/å).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Des helle a (à) kimmt ausm Middlhochdeitschn ä, bzw. vo de Diphthongen ou/öu, im Weanarischn aa ausm Diphthong ei.
english: The bright a (à) comes from Middle High German ä, or from the diphthongs ou/öu, and in Viennese also from the diphthong ei.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: So hoassts im Boarischn laa (lààr) im Vagleich zu standarddeitsch leer, ausm mhd.
english: In Bavarian, it is called laa (lààr) in comparison to standard German leer, from Middle High German.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: lære, i glaab (i glààb) im Vagleich zu ich glaube, aus ich g(e)loube, wean.
english: learn, I believe (I glààb) in comparison to I believe, from I believe, become.
note: Translates away most cited historical/modern word forms, misreads lære as learn and Viennese abbreviation wean. as become.

bar_text: haaß (hààß) im Vergleich zu hoaß und heiß, ois aum mhd.
english: haaß (hààß) in comparison to hoaß and heiß, all from MHG.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: heiz.
english: hot.
note: Hot conveys the gloss but loses the actual Middle High German form heiz being cited.

bar_text: De Vatretung fian middlhochdeitschn a-Laut is dagegn fia gwähnli a „vadunklts“, des wo scho ins o iwageht.
english: The representation for the Middle High German a-sound is, by contrast, for the most part a “darkened” one, which already flows into o.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: So wead aus middelhochdeitsch wazzer, hase, wâr beispuisweis Wossa (Wåsser), Hos (Håås), woa (wåår) im Vagleich zu standarddeitsch Wasser, Hase und wahr.
english: Thus, from Middle High German wazzer, hase, wâr, for example, Wossa (Wåsser), Hos (Håås), woa (wåår) in comparison to standard German Wasser, Hase and wahr.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Regional ko s a zu Variationa zwischn dunklem und middlan a gebm (schaug mia homma/mia håmma/mia hamma).
english: Regionally, there can be variations between dark and medium 'a' (look, we have/mia homma/mia håmma/mia hamma).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Vor oim bei da Diminutivbuidung mitn Suffixen -l und -al tritt Umlaut ein, d. h. aus dunklem a (o/å) wead helles a (à).
english: Above all, in diminutive formation with the suffixes -l and -al, umlaut occurs, i.e., from dark a (o/å) becomes light a (à).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: In fost oin boarischen Ortsnama, de wo af -ing endn, muass a ggf. im Stamm vorhandans -a- hej ausgsprocha wean; oiso „Plattling (Plàttling)“ (und ned „Plottling oda Plåttling“) und „Gaching (Gàching)“ (stott *„Gorching oda Gårching“), aa „Gamisch (Gàmisch)“ (stott „Gormisch oda Gårmisch“) und „Graz (Gràz)“ (ned „Groz oda Gråz“ – de Stod hod im Middloida „Grätz“ ghoassn, und daraus hod si s helle a entwicket).
english: In almost all Bavarian place names that end in -ing, a possibly existing -a- in the stem must be pronounced as a bright a (à); so “Plattling (Plàttling)” (and not “Plottling or Plåttling”) and “Gaching (Gàching)” (instead of *“Gorching or Gårching”), also “Gamisch (Gàmisch)” (instead of “Gormisch or Gårmisch”) and “Graz (Gràz)” (not “Groz or Gråz” – the city was called “Grätz” in the Middle Ages, and the bright a developed from it).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ausnahma san owa manche Ortsnama mit -all- wia „Boing (Bålling/Båing)“ (Palling) oda „Dolling (Dålling)“ (Thalling).
english: Exceptions are, however, some place names with -all- like „Boing (Bålling/Båing)“ (Palling) or „Dolling (Dålling)“ (Thalling).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S helle a (à) wead im Boarischen gwehnlich ois a wiedagem, s dunkle a (å) dagegn moastns ois o, (oiso mocha statt måcha).
english: The bright a (à) becomes usually an a in Bavarian, the dark a (å) against it most often an o (so mocha instead of måcha).
note: Becomes is imprecise for the written representation being described.

bar_text: Es liegt fia deitsch Ohrn a näha am o.
english: It is close to German ears.
note: Omits the o comparison and turns perceived sound proximity into proximity to ears.

bar_text: Das des zum Zammafoi mitn gschlossanan o fiaht, wo im Boarischn moastns nah am ou liegt, wead vo Kritikern gern ois Oloss gnumma, de Eifiahrung vo – vom Deitschn divergiaradn – Sondazoachn in da boarischn Schreibweis z begrindn.
english: That this leads to the convergence with the closed [o], which in Bavarian is mostly close to [ou], is gladly taken by critics as an excuse to justify the introduction of – diverging from German – special characters in the Bavarian writing style.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es is owa so, dass aa im Stadarddeitschn, im Englischn sowia in andan indogermanischn Sprochn de gsprochan Vokai efta ned mit de gschrieban iwaeistimma.
english: But it is the case that even in standard German, in English as well as in other Indo-European languages, the spoken vowels often do not coincide with the written ones.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fost jeds betonte kurze e is im Boarischen gschlossa (im Gegnsotz zum Deitschen: do sans olle offa).
english: Almost every emphasized short e is closed in Bavarian (in contrast to German: there they are all open).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es gibt nur wenige Wärta mit an kurznm offanen e (è); a guads Beispui dafia: Bettn („Bett“, mit gschlossan e) vs. betn (bètn) („Gebet“, mit offan è).
english: There are only a few words with a short open e (è); a good example of this: Bettn (“bed”, with closed e) vs. betn (bètn) (“prayer”, with open è).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Standarddeitschn is in dem Beispui genau andasrum: s Wort „Bett“ hod a offans (wei kurzes), s Wort „beten“ a gschlossans (wei langs) e.
english: In standard German, it is exactly the other way around in this example: the word “Bett” has an open e (because it is short), the word “beten” a closed e (because it is long).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Nebm am unbetontn a gibts aa an weidan unbetontn Vokal im Boarischen, dea wo zwischn i und e steht, und je noch Dialekt offena (Richtung e) oda gschlossena (Richtung i) gsprocha wead.
english: Besides the unstressed a, there is also another unstressed vowel in Bavarian, which stands between i and e, and is spoken depending on the dialect either open (towards e) or closed (towards i).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Er is moastns aus da Nebmsuibm -el entstanda, z. B. in Weatan wia grabbin oda Deifi.
english: It is mostly created from the mist column -e.g. in stories like Grabbin or Deifi.
note: Nebmsuibm -el becomes a mist column and words become stories.

bar_text: In de moastn Boarischen Dialekte hod da Schwa-Laut, dea wo am unbetontn e im Standarddeitschn entspricht, koan Phonemstatus.
english: In most Bavarian dialects, the schwa sound, which corresponds to the unstressed e in Standard German, has no phonemic status.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Regional tritt a in bestimmten Positiona ois Allophon zua unbetontn a und i af.
english: Regionally, a also occurs in certain positions as an allophone to unstressed a and i.
note: The pronoun a refers to schwa; the target instead identifies the sound as a.

bar_text: A weindans Merkmoi vom modeana Boarischn is de Beibehoidung vo de middlhochboarischn Diphthong ie, üe, uo ois ia und ua, wia in liab, griassn, Bruada („liab, grüßen, Bruder“).
english: A clear characteristic of modern Bavarian is the preservation of the Middle High Bavarian diphthongs ie, üe, uo as ia and ua, as in liab, griassn, Bruada (“liab, grüßen, Bruder”).
note: Changes another/further characteristic to a clear characteristic.

bar_text: A bsundas Merkmoi vom Boarischn is da Vokal oa (im Weanarischn aa ausgsprocha), dea wo ausm middlhochdeitschn ei entstanda is.
english: A special feature of Bavarian is the vowel oa (also pronounced in Viennese), which arose from the Middle High German ei.
note: aa in the parenthesis is the Viennese pronunciation, not the word also; that pronunciation is lost.

bar_text: Dea Lautwandl betrifft owa nurs sogennnte ejtare ei vom Deitschen, ned owa s jingare ei, des wo eascht im Zug vo da neihochdeitschn Diphthongiarung ausm middlhochdeitschn langan i (î) entstanda is, und daher an Lautwandl ned mehr mitgmocht hod.
english: This sound change, however, only affects the so-called older ei of German, not the younger ei, which only arose in the course of New High German diphthongization from the Middle High German long i (î), and therefore did not participate in the sound change anymore.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Deshoib hoassts af Boarisch hoid „oans, zwoa, drei“ (oans und zwoa hom a ejtas ei ois Stammvokal, drei a jingas ei, des wo af Middlhochdeitsch no drî ghoassn hod.
english: That's why in Bavarian it's just called “oans, zwoa, drei” (one and two have an old ei as a stem vowel, three a younger ei, which was still called drî in Middle High German.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Olladings gibts im Boarischn no dritts, no jigas ei, des wo durch de Entrundung vom Diphthong nhd.
english: Anyway, there is still a third thing in Bavarian, not just the old ei, that which [was created] through the denasalization of the New High German diphthong eu, äu, or iu, or rather the mhd. öu.
note: Unrounding becomes denasalization, even younger is lost and later source-fragment forms are inserted.

bar_text: eu, äu entstanda is, dea wo vom Langvokal mhd.
english: eu, äu, which arose from the Middle High German long vowel
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: iu, bzw. mhd.
english: iu, or rather mhd.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: öu obstammt.
english: comes from eu.
note: Changes the cited source form öu to eu.

bar_text: (De Entrundung hod owa in de moastn Tirola Mundoatn ned stottgfundn.)
english: (However, the unrounding did not take place in most Tyrolean dialects.)
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Um aussazfindn, wos fia a deitsches ei im Boarischen zu oa wead, und wos fia oans ned, huift moastns a Blick afs Englische.
english: To find out what kind of German 'ei' becomes 'oa' in Bavarian, and what kind doesn't, a look at English usually helps.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Englischn entspricht s ejtare ei moast am o oda ea, s jingare is dagegn a i und wead ähnli ausgesprocha wia im Boarischn.
english: In English, the older 'ei' corresponds mostly to an 'o' or 'ea', the younger is conversely an 'i' and will be pronounced similarly to in Bavarian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Geistliche Weata
english: Spiritual words
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es gibt owa Ausnahma vo da Lautwandlregl ei > oa, de wo vor oim Weata betreffa, de wo durch ian Brauch im vom Godsdeanst in iara oidn Gstoit bewoart worn san; dabei handeltsa si um Geist, Fleisch, heilig und en Monatsnam Mai, de wo normalaweis Goast, Floasch, hoalig, und Moa hoassn miassadn, owa so im Boarischn extrem sejtn sand.
english: However, there are exceptions to the sound change rule ei > oa, which primarily concern words that have been preserved in their old form through their custom in the divine service; these involve spirit, flesh, holy, and the month name May, which would normally have to be called Goast, Floasch, hoalig, and Moa, but are extremely rare in Bavarian.
note: Loses the German ei-bearing word forms by translating them and leaves rare ambiguous between retained words and predicted forms.

bar_text: Dabei is da Laut j a Hoibvokal.
english: In this case, the sound 'j' is a semivowel.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Obwoi de Fortis-Vaschlusslaute p und t mit ian Lenis-Pendants b und d im Olaut zammagfoin san, kenna se ned ois zwoa Allophone jeweis vo an Phonem gejtn, wei si in gwissn Positiona bedeitungsuntascheidend san.
english: Even though the fortis closure sounds p and t have merged with their lenis counterparts b and d in the unstressed vowel, they cannot be considered as two allophones of each respective phoneme, because they are meaning-insignificant in certain positions.
note: Olaut means word-initial position, not unstressed vowel; meaning-distinguishing is reversed to meaning-insignificant.

bar_text: Nur im Olaut kenna si ois Variantn ogseng wian, vo dena wo de Aussproch vom nochfoigandn Laut obhängt (schaug dazua weida untn iwan Glottisschlag).
english: Only in the unstressed vowel can they be seen as variants, of which the pronunciation depends on the following sound (look further down at the glottal stop).
note: Olaut is word-initial position, not unstressed vowel.

bar_text: In da boarischn Sproch san de fortis- und lenis-Vaschlusslaute p, t, k und b, d, g im Olaut und zwischn Vokalen moastns zammagfoin und weadn daher ned weida untaschiedn.
english: In the Bavarian language, the fortis and lenis stop consonants p, t, k and b, d, g in unstressed syllables and between vowels have mostly merged and are therefore not further distinguished.
note: Changes word-initial position to unstressed syllables.

bar_text: Deshoib ko im Boarischn da Dog oda da Tog, as Greiz oda as Kreiz, und de da Bädasui oda da Pedasui gschriem wean und deshoib foin Werta wia dringa (dringen) und dringa (trinka) zamma.
english: That is why in Bavarian the day or the day, the border or the cross, and those that are written as the bath-sui or the foot-sui, and that is why words like dringa (to press/to urge) and dringa (to drink) fall together.
note: Erases the stop-letter contrasts and garbles the parsley forms as bath-sui/foot-sui.

bar_text: Als oanziga fortis-Laut ist k- am Wortofang dahoidn, wann eam a Vokal nochfoigt; vor r, l und n wead er ebenfois zum g lenisiat.
english: As the only fortis consonant, k- is maintained at the beginning of a word when a vowel follows it; before r, l, and n, it is likewise lenited to g.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Laute b, d und g wean owa am Wortofang vor s, sch, f und h fortisiat; de neien fortis-Laute hom owa koan Phonem-, sondan nur Allophon-Status, wei se nur in bestimmta Umgebung aftretn, wo eanare lenis-Variantn ned vorkema.
english: The sounds b, d and g are however fortified at the beginning of a word before s, sch, f and h; the new fortis sounds however have no phoneme status, but only allophone status, because they only occur in a certain environment where their lenis variants do not occur.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Und daher vahoidn sa se zu dena ned bedeitungsuntascheidend.
english: And therefore they do not behave in a way that is significant for meaning regarding them.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S Boarische kennt fimf Frikative; f (stimmlos) und w (stimmhoft) buidn dabei a Poar.
english: Bavarian knows five fricatives; f (voiceless) and w (voiced) form a pair in the process.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da Frikativ s is außa vor n imma stimmlos, oiso im Gengsotz zum Deitschn aa am Wortofang.
english: The fricative [f] is always voiceless except before [v], so in contrast to German, also at the beginning of a word.
note: Changes s to f and the following n to v.

bar_text: Dazua keman de mit Buchstabmkombinationa gschriebanan Laute ch und sch, wobei ch ois Allophon [x] oda [ç] (noch -i- oda -e-) zu olautendn h [h] im In- oda Auslaut aftritt.
english: Added to this are the sounds ch and sch written with letter combinations, where ch occurs as the allophone [x] or [ç] (after -i- or -e-) and as the fully pronounced h [h] in syllable onset or coda.
note: Initial h with medial/final ch allophones becomes h also in syllable onset/coda, with initial misread as fully pronounced.

bar_text: Da Laut ch kimmt andas ois im Standarddeitschen ned noch -n- vor, daher Minga, mank, Menk vs. stdt.
english: The sound 'ch' comes differently than in Standard German, as it does not precede '-n-'—therefore Minga, mank, Menk vs. stdt.
note: Reverses the position from not following n to not preceding it.

bar_text: München, manch, Mönch.
english: Munich, many, monk.
note: Translates away the German ch-bearing forms that are the phonological examples; manch is also imprecisely many.

bar_text: S Boarische hod s gleiche Sonorantninventar wia s Standarddeitsche, nämli de Nasallaute m, n und ng [ŋ] sowia l, r und j. S r wead in mangn Gegandn mit da Zunganspitzn geroit, in andan Gegandn mitn Gaumenzapfal (sog. uvulares r), ohne dass des vo Boarisch-Sprechan ois Fehla empfundn wead.
english: Bavarian has the same sonorant inventory as Standard German, namely the nasal sounds m, n and ng [ŋ] as well as l, r and j. The r is produced with the tip of the tongue in many regions, in other regions with the uvula (so-called uvular r), without this being perceived as an error when speaking Bavarian.
note: Produced omits the explicitly rolled/trilled manner of r.

bar_text: Da stimmlose glottale Plosiv (Glottisschlag) tritt wia im Standarddeitschn vorm vokalischn Olaut (duatn vapflichtend) af.
english: The voiceless glottal plosive (glottal stop) occurs, as in Standard German, before a vocalic unstressed vowel (mandatory).
note: Word-initial vowel becomes unstressed vowel and mandatory there loses its Standard-German scope.

bar_text: Im Gengasotz dazua is des oba nur am Sotzofang oda am Ofang vo am Einschub vapflichtend: Sunstan ko ma Weata owa scho zammziagn.
english: In contrast to that, however, it is only mandatory at the beginning of a sentence or at the beginning of an insertion: But one can already contract words on Sundays.
note: Changes otherwise to on Sundays, inventing a temporal condition.

bar_text: De gsamte boarische Nominalflexion richt si am Substantiv aus.
english: The entire Bavarian nominal inflection is based on the noun.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S grammatische Gschlecht (Genus) vom Haptwort bestimmt de Deklination vo da Nominalphrasn; d. h. sowoi da Artikl ois aa s Adjektiv und andare Attribute miassn in Genus, Kasus und Numerus ans Substantiv, wo se begleitn, anglicha wean.
english: The grammatical gender (genus) of the main word determines the declension of the noun phrase; i.e., both the article as well as the adjective and other attributes must become similar to the noun they accompany in gender, case, and number.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S gibt drei Genera: maskulin, feminin und neutrum.
english: There are three genders: masculine, feminine and neuter.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ois paradigmatische Kategorien gibts de Fälle (Kasus) Nominativ, Dativ und Akkusativ sowia de Numeri Singular und Plural.
english: As paradigmatic categories, there are the cases (Kasus) nominative, dative and accusative as well as the numbers singular and plural.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Adjektive käna aa gsteigat wean.
english: Adjectives cannot also be inflected.
note: Negates the source and replaces comparison with general inflection.

bar_text: Da unbstimmte Artikl is dageng fia olle drei Genera im Nominativ identisch
english: The indefinite article is, however, identical for all three genders in the nominative.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da Artikl wead im Boarischn flektiat, d. h. da Kasus wead so deitli gmochd.
english: The article is inflected in Bavarian, i.e., the case is made so clearly.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wei de moastn Substantive im Boarischn olle Kasusendunga valuan hom, wead da Kasus praktisch nur iwan Artikl ozoagt.
english: Since most nouns in Bavarian have lost all case endings, the case is practically only shown via the article.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da unbestimmte Artikl is etymologisch duach de unbetonte Aussproch vom Zoiwort "oa" entstondn (noch oidboarischa Schreibung <ain>, gsprochn /oã/).
english: The indefinite article etymologically arose through the unstressed pronunciation of the numeral word 'oa' (according to Old Bavarian spelling <ain>, pronounced /oã/).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da unbestimmte Artikl wead z. B. ois /ə/, /ɐ/ o.
english: The indefinite article is, for example, pronounced as /ə/, /ɐ/.
note: The completed list omits the source's trailing or indicating further similar realizations.

bar_text: ä. ausgsprochen, im Dativ z. B. /ənə/, /ɐnɐ/ o.
english: e.g. pronounced, in the dative e.g. /ənə/, /ɐnɐ/ etc.
note: The carried-over abbreviation fragment ä. is changed to e.g. rather than completing or similar.

bar_text: ä. Gschriebm wead da unbestimmte Artikl in da boarischn Dialektliteratur und heitign Umschriftn, z. B. in Internetforen, haifi ois <a>, sejten aa ois <oa>, im Dativ ois <ana>, vor oim im Dat.
english: e. Written, the indefinite article is in Bavarian dialect literature and today's transcriptions, e.g., in internet forums, often as <a>, sometimes also as <oa>, in the dative as <ana>, especially in the dat.
note: Sometimes replaces rarely for the oa spelling.

bar_text: aa ois <oana>.
english: also as <oana>.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Ostmiddlboarischn imma ois <a> und <ana>.
english: In East Central Bavarian, it is always <a> and <ana>.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: As Substantiv gheat im Boarischn zu de flektiaradn Woatoartn.
english: As a noun, it belongs to the inflected parts of speech in Bavarian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wia in andane germanische Sprochn is es Geschlecht (Genus) es markantaste Kriterium vom Haptwort.
english: As in other Germanic languages, gender (genus) is the most prominent criterion of the headword.
note: Haptwort means noun here, not the more general headword.

bar_text: E Boarische hod no drei vo de urspringli via germanischn Kasus: Nominativ, Dativ und Akkusativ.
english: Bavarian still has three of the original via Germanic cases: nominative, dative and accusative.
note: Leaves via untranslated and thus loses the original count of four.

bar_text: De letztn zwoa foin zum Tei zamma.
english: The last two sometimes merge.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da Genitiv is nur in a poar Redewendunga dahoidn.
english: The genitive is only preserved in a few idioms.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wia im Standarddeitschn wead es boarische Substantiv nur sejtn dekliniat, sundan druckd an Kasus durch de Artikl aus.
english: As in standard German, the Bavarian noun is not only rarely declined, but expresses the case through the article.
note: Not only ... but replaces the source's rarely ... rather through the article relation.

bar_text: Es gibt vaschiedane Deklinationsklassn, de wo se haptsächli in da Pluralbuidung untascheidn.
english: There are different declension classes, which mainly differ in plural formation.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ois grobe Richtlinie wead zwischn da schwochn Deklination (sog. n-Klasse) und da stoarkn Deklination (sog. a-Klasse) untaschiedn.
english: As a rough guideline, a distinction will be made between the weak declension (so-called n-class) and the strong declension (so-called a-class).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Schwoche Substantive endn fia gewähnlich af -n im Plural.
english: Weak nouns usually end in -n in the plural.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Vui schwoche Feminina buidn an Singular af es Suffix -n, so dass se im Plural entweda glei hoassn oda a -a ofiagn.
english: Many weak feminine nouns form a singular with the suffix -n, so that they in the plural either remain the same or end in an -a.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Bsundas de schwochn Maskulina hom im Singular a Endung fia de obliquen Kasus, d. h. fia olle Kasus aussam Nominativ.
english: Especially the weak masculines have an ending in the singular for the oblique cases, i.e., for all cases except the nominative.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Se hom moastns a -n am End.
english: They usually have a -n at the end.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Zua Klassn vo de schwochn Substantive (W1) zejn Maskulina und Feminina af -n im Plural und aa olle Feminina mit da Pluralendung -an (de moastns im Singular af -ng endn; es -a- is dabei a sog. Sprossvokal bzw. epenthetisch).
english: The class of weak substantives (W1) includes masculines and feminines ending in -n in the plural and also all feminines with the plural ending -an (which most often end in -ng in the singular; an -a- is a so-called epenthetic vowel in this case).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Driwa ausse lossa se olle Maskulina und Neutra, de wo im Singular af es Suffix -i endn, do einordna.
english: All masculines and neuters that end in the suffix -i in the singular are to be classified outside [of this class].
note: The source includes these -i nouns in the class; outside explicitly excludes them.

bar_text: Bei de stoarkn Deklinationsklassn gibts koane Kasusendungan; de oanzige Vaendarung am Woat findt bei da Numerusflexion stodd, oisdann beim Wechsel vom Singular zun Plural.
english: With the strong declension classes, there are no case endings; the only change to the word takes place during number inflection, i.e., during the change from singular to plural.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es gibt dabei vaschiedene Meglichkeitn, an Plural im Boarischn z markian.
english: There are various possibilities to mark a plural in Bavarian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Stoarke Maskulina und Neutra nutzen de Endung -a, de moast aus da middelhochdeitschen Endung -er entstandn und ois soiche im Neihochdeitschn no dahoidn is.
english: Strong masculine and neuter nouns use the ending -a, which mostly arose from the Middle High German ending -er and as such is still preserved in New High German.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es gibt oba a Weata, de wo se eascht in neia Zeit in de Klase eingreiht hom, oiso an a-Plural buidn, ohne jemois an er-Plural ghobt z hom.
english: But there are also words that have joined the class only in recent times, so they form an a-plural without ever having had an er-plural.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Feminina buidn eanan Plural oft mit da Endung -an, so wias es Woat Endung sejm duat: oa Endung, zwoa Endungan.
english: Feminine nouns often form their plural with the ending -an, just as the word ending does: one ending, two endings.
note: The essential Endungan example is replaced with English endings, which does not illustrate -an.

bar_text: Ma ko Substantive afgrund eanara Pluralsforman in vaschiedene Klassn eintein.
english: Nouns can be classified into different classes based on their plural forms.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De haifigstn Meglichkeitn vo da Pluralbuidung san Umlaut od Suffigiarung; boade Meglichkeitn kena aa kombiniad wean.
english: The most common possibilities for plural formation are umlaut or suffixation; both possibilities can also be combined.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De do ogfiadn Beispui buidn de de Klass 1 und 2 vo de stoarkn Substantive, vo dena as Kennzeichn a Umlautplural is.
english: The examples listed here form classes 1 and 2 of the strong substantives, which are characterized by an umlaut plural.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Klass (S1) hod nebmam Umlaut koa weidas Pluralkennzoachn, is oiso endungslos; ia ghean nur Maskulina und Feminina o. Oft kimmt im Plural no a Vokalkiazung dazua, beispuisweis: Hand – Händt, Stod – Städt, Wand – Wändt, Grund – Grindt.
english: The class (S1) has no further plural marker besides the umlaut, so it is thus endless; it only belongs to masculines and feminines. Often, a vowel shortening is also added in the plural, for example: Hand – Händt, Stod – Städt, Wand – Wändt, Grund – Grindt.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Zua Klass S2, de wo im Umlautplural plus Endung -a (de wo moastns da deitschn Endung -er entspricht) hom, ghean oanige Maskulina und vui Neutra.
english: The class S2, which has the umlaut plural plus the ending -a (which mostly corresponds to the German ending -er), includes other masculines and many neuters.
note: oanige means some, not other, masculine nouns.

bar_text: Es gejten de gleichn Umlautregeln wia obm:
english: The same umlaut rules apply as above:
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Zur Klasse S3 ghean olle Maskulina, Feminina und Neutra ohne Umlaut mit Pluralendung -a; dabei endn de moastn Feminina im Singular af de urspringlige Dativendung -n.
english: Class S3 includes all masculines, feminines, and neuters without an umlaut with the plural ending -a; in doing so, most feminines end in the singular with the original dative ending -n.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ois letzte storke Klasse (S4) gejten Substantive mit Nullplural, zum Beispui ‚Fisch‘
english: As the last strong class (S4), nouns with zero plural apply, for example 'Fisch'
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: (m) und ‚Schof‘
english: (m) and 'Schof'
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: In manchen Dialektn druckn de Substantive den Plural owa durch Vokalkiazung oda -längung aus, beispuisweis da Hund und de Hundt.
english: In some dialects, the nouns express the plural through vowel shortening or lengthening, for example the dog and the dogs.
note: Translates away da Hund/de Hundt into dog/dogs, replacing the vowel-change example with English suffixation.

bar_text: De Klass bstäht eigentli nur aus Maskulina und Neutra; olle Feminina af -n, de wo historisch gseng zu de schwochn Substantivn ghean, kena owa aa dazuazejt wean, wei ia Plural ebenso unmarkiat is: ‚Antn – Antn‘ „Ente“.
english: The class actually consists only of masculines and neuters; all feminines ending in -n, which historically belong to the weak nouns, can however also be counted among them, because their plural is likewise unmarked: 'Antn – Antn' 'duck'.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Feminina wexln owa langsam zur Gruppe S3 und nehman im Plural de Endung -a o (vgl. obm s Beispui Ein „Eule“).
english: The feminine forms are however slowly changing to group S3 and take the ending -a in the plural (cf. the example above, an “Eule”).
note: Loses the actual Ein owl form by treating it as an indefinite article.

bar_text: Vuifoch wead d/ iwa de Wortgrenz wegga assimiliat (Sandhi), so hoassts moastns Nom.
english: Often, it is assimilated (Sandhi) across the word boundary, so it is mostly Nom.
note: Omits the specified assimilating sound d/.

bar_text: b Vodan und b Buam(a).
english: and the father and the boy(s).
note: Translates away the actual assimilated b Vodan/b Buam(a) forms, which are the example.

bar_text: Ebenso wia Voda flektian Baua, Boi, Breiss, Depp, Buasch [österr.], Frank, Franzos, Hiasch, Hos, Läw und andare mehr.
english: Just as Father, farmers, boys, brutes, idiots, youths [Austrian], Franks, Frenchmen, rascals, scoundrels, rascals and others more.
note: Replaces the actual noun forms with several false glosses and loses the explicit inflection claim.

bar_text: Ähnli wia Bua flektian de Wärter Rob und Schwob: olle Forman außa Nominativ Singular hom an Stej vo -b an Stammauslaut -m: Rom (Robm), Schwom (Schwobm); de Pluralform Roma (Robma), Schwoma (Schwobma) san sejtn.
english: Similar to Bua, the words Rob and Schwob decline: all forms except nominative singular have a change from -b to the stem consonant -m: Rom (Robm), Schwom (Schwobm); the plural forms Roma (Robma), Schwoma (Schwobma) are rare.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: As grammatische Gschlecht vo an Substantiv wead am Artikel markiat.
english: The grammatical gender of a noun is marked by the article.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Oft is as Gschlecht wia im Deitschn.
english: Often the gender is like in German.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Bei de Personalpronomina untascheidd s Boarische teiweis, so wia vui romanische und slawische Sprochn, zwischn betontn und unbetontn Foama im Dativ (nur 1.,
english: Regarding the personal pronouns, Bavarian partially distinguishes, like many Romance and Slavic languages, between stressed and unstressed forms in the dative (only 1.,
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: 2. Singular) und Akkusativ (nur
english: 2. Singular) and accusative (only
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: * De Foama gejten ois „weniga“ boarisch, san dafia oba typisch ostfränggisch.
english: * These forms are considered “less” Bavarian, but are in return typically East Franconian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Bei da Kombination vo mearan unbetontn Personalpronomina, de wo af -'s verkiazt san, wead da Bindevokal -a- einegschom; bei da Reihenfoige vo da Ordnung gibts, im Gengasotz zum Deitschn, vaschiedane Variantn.
english: In the case of a combination of several unstressed personal pronouns that are shortened with -'s, the connecting vowel -a- is inserted; regarding the sequence of the order, in contrast to German, there are different variants.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Dabei ko in (1.a) und (1.b) ebmso weng wia im Deitschn untaschiedn wean, obsa si bei erra um de 3. Person Singular feminin oda um de 3. Person Plural handlt.
english: In this regard, (1.a) and (1.b) can be distinguished about as much as in German, whether it concerns the 3rd person singular feminine or the 3rd person plural.
note: Loses the explicit cannot/as-little distinction and the actual ambiguous form erra.

bar_text: Aa de Possessivpronomina deina und seina flektiaen so.
english: The possessive pronouns deina and seina inflect like that.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S Possessivpronomen (Fem. Sg.) iara is vom Standarddeitschn iwanumma woan; urspringli vawendt s Boarische fia weibliche Bsitza ebmfois s Pronomen seina.
english: The possessive pronoun (fem. sg.) iara was generally taken from Standard German; originally, Bavarian also used the pronoun seina for female owners.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Oft wead a s substantiviate Adjektiv da mei(nige) (da dei(nige), da sei(nige), im Plural: de meinign, de deinign …) vawendt: „Wem ghead der?“ – „Des is da mei!“
english: Often a substantivized adjective is used as my (yours, his, in the plural: mine, yours, his ...) : “Whom does it belong to?” – “That is mine!”
note: English glosses replace the actual mei(nige)/dei(nige)/sei(nige) and plural forms being exemplified.

bar_text: So wia de Possessivpronomina flektian de Indefinitpronomina koana sowia oana; ma ko vors Letztare s Wort iagad- stejn.
english: Just as the possessive pronouns inflect, the indefinite pronouns koana and oana do so in the same way; one can place the word iagad- before the last syllable.
note: Before the latter pronoun becomes before the last syllable.

bar_text: Do wead oiso ned zwischn de Geschlechta, sundan zwischn Persona und Socha untaschiedn.
english: So, one does not distinguish between the genders, but rather between person and thing.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Vui vo de boarischn Adjektive hom a Kurzfoam und a Langfoam.
english: Many of the Bavarian adjectives have a short form and a long form.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Kurzfoam wead in prädikativa Stellung vawendt.
english: The short form is used in a predicative position.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: D. h. dann, wen s Adjektiv mitm Huifsverb sein a Prädikat buidt (de Schuah san schwoaz).
english: I.e. then, when the adjective forms a predicate with the auxiliary verb (the shoes are black).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Langfoam kimmt dann vor, wann s Adjektiv ois Attribut vo am Substantiv vawendt wead (de schwoazn Schuah).
english: The long form then occurs when the adjective is used as an attribute of a noun (the black shoes).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Moastns liegt da Untaschied zwischn Kurz- und Langfoam im Endkonsonanten.
english: Mostly, the difference between short and long forms lies in the final consonant.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Oft san des -n, -ch, -g.
english: Often these are -n, -ch, -g.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wia im Deitschn wean Adjektive in attributiva Stejung flektiat, d. h. se griagn vaschiedne Endunga.
english: As in German, adjectives in attributive position are inflected, i.e., they receive different endings.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Dabei muass untaschiedn wean, obs mid an Substantiv mid bstimmtn Artikl gengan (und dahea sejm in bstimmta Foam flektian), oda obs mid an unbstimmtn Artikl zamm san (und nacha dementsprechend nach an unbstimmtn Musta dekliniat wean).
english: In this case, a distinction must be made whether it is with a noun with a definite article (and therefore must be inflected in a certain form), or whether it is together with an indefinite article (and is then subsequently declined according to an indefinite pattern).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wean Adjektive substantiviat vawendt, oiso nua mit Artikl, nacha richtn sa si ebnfois noch dem.
english: When adjectives are used substantively, i.e., only with an article, they also inflect accordingly.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ois Beispui deant as Adjektiv schee, des wo am Stamm bei da Flexion um -n daweitad wead (aussa beim Neutrum Singular).
english: As an example, the adjective 'schee' serves, which is extended by -n at the stem during inflection (except in the neuter singular).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Boarischen deant as Suffix -a zur Buidung vom Komparativ, vo da easchtn Steigarungsform.
english: In Bavarian, the suffix -a serves for the formation of the comparative, from the first degree of comparison.
note: Changes the first-degree apposition to a from relation.

bar_text: Grundlog vom Komparativ is de obm bschriebane Langform; bei mangn Adjektivn kimts zu Umlautn, bei andan zua Vaendarung in da Vokalleng oda im konsonantischn Auslaut.
english: The basis of the comparative is the long form described above; with many adjectives it leads to umlauts, with others to a change in the vowel or in the consonantal coda.
note: Generic change in the vowel loses the source's specific length change.

bar_text: Fian Superlativ wead je nach Landschaft, a eigane Form af -st buidd oda owa aa ned.
english: For the superlative, depending on the region, a special form ending in -st is formed, or not.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: In letztan Foi wead da Komparativ ois Superlativasotz heagnumma.
english: In the last case, the comparative is taken as a superlative sentence.
note: Superlativasotz means superlative substitute/replacement, not a superlative sentence.

bar_text: So ko da Sotz „Max Müller ist der größte der zwölf Knaben“ im Boarischen foigende Varianten produzian: „Vo de zwejf Buam is da Müller Max am gressan (Komparativ)/am gresstn (Superlativ)/sejtn da gresste/da gressane.“
english: Thus the sentence “Max Müller is the greatest of the twelve boys” can produce the following variants in Bavarian: “Of the twelve boys, Müller Max is the greatest (comparative)/the greatest (superlative)/seldom the greatest/the greatest.”
note: All cited comparative/superlative forms become greatest, losing the actual morphological variants.

bar_text: Boarische Zoiweata endn moastns af -e, des wo owa in attributiva Stejung oft wegfoid.
english: Bavarian number words mostly end in -e, which however often falls away in the attributive position.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Numeralia flektian ned, Ausnohm is as Zoiwoat oans fia de Zoi 1.
english: The numerals do not inflect, with the exception of the number word one for the number 1.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Boarischn is da Iwagang vo da Wortbeigung zum Sotzbau (Sidntax) oft fliaßend, desweng kena vui Bereiche in da boarischen Grammatik vo da Morphosyntax am bestn eafosst wean.
english: In Bavarian, the transition from word inflection to sentence structure (syntax) is often fluid, which is why many areas in Bavarian grammar can best be understood as morphosyntax.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Prepositiona kena im Boarischn wia im Deitschn mit am bestimmtn Artikl zu am Woat vaschmejzn (vgl. dt. bei dem = beim, an dem = am, unter den = untern usw.).
english: Prepositions in Bavarian, like in German, can merge with a certain article into a word (cf. German bei dem = beim, an dem = am, unter den = untern etc.).
note: Certain article is imprecise for the grammatical category definite article.

bar_text: Im Boarisch wead des vui efta ogwendt.
english: In Bavarian, this is used much more frequently.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wei Prepositiona de Betonung af s nochfoigande Sotzelement lenka, kena eahna nua betonte, obwa nia unbetonte Peasonalpronomina foign.
english: Since prepositions direct the emphasis onto the following sentence element, they can only be stressed if no unstressed personal pronouns follow.
note: Changes which personal pronouns can follow into a condition on stressing the prepositions themselves.

bar_text: Im Boarischn wean fia Ortschaftn und Städt eascht seitm Eifluss ausm Hochdeitschn aa "nach" und "in" braucht.
english: In Bavarian, too, the words for towns and cities, such as 'nach' and 'in', are only used since the influence of High German.
note: Words for towns and cities blurs the fact that nach/in are used with place names rather than naming places.

bar_text: Traditionej sogt ma im Boarischn owa a oda af/auf (= nach) und z (= in).
english: Traditionally, however, one says in Bavarian also 'oda af/auf' (= nach) and 'z' (= in).
note: Misreads a oda af/auf as the single quoted sequence oda af/auf.

bar_text: Ma foaht oisdann af Augschburg oda bleibt z Minga.
english: One then drives to Augsburg or stays in Munich.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Bei Feiatog findt se je noch Region entweda ebmfois as z: z Ostan, z Weihnachtn; oda af: af Ostan, af Weihnachtn; oda untam Eifluss vo da Standardsproch an.
english: On holidays, depending on the region, it is either influenced by: either 'z: z Ostan, z Weihnachtn' [at Easter, at Christmas]; or 'af: af Ostan, af Weihnachtn' [on Easter, on Christmas]; or by the influence of the standard language.
note: Omits an and changes the statement of preposition use into being influenced by the quoted forms.

bar_text: Im Boarischn sogt ma soichane Weata owa nia nid ohne Prepositiona zua Zeitogob.
english: In Bavarian, however, such words are never said regarding a time of day without prepositions.
note: Narrows general temporal expressions/holidays to time of day.

bar_text: A regionale Besonderheit is de temporale Konjunktion aft, de wo in großn Toaln vom boarischn Sprochgebiet vawendt wiad.
english: A regional peculiarity is the temporal conjunction 'aft', which is used in large parts of the Bavarian language area.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Etymologisch gseng entspricht des am englischn after und hoasst „nacha, danoch“.
english: Etymologically speaking, this corresponds to the English 'after' and means 'after, afterwards'.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: In de siidboarischn Dialekte tretn präpositionslose Orts- und Richtungsogobm (Adverbialien) af.
english: In the South Bavarian dialects, prepositionless locational and directional specifications (adverbials) occur.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ma gähd oisdann ned in de Kira oda afn Moakt, sundan ma gähd Kira/Moakt, ohne a Präposition z vawendn.
english: One doesn't go into the church or to the market then, but one goes church/market, without using a preposition.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Lokalbedeitung wiad duachs Ausbleibm vom Artikl markiat, dea wo sont bei jedm Substantiv obligatorisch is.
english: The local meaning is marked through the absence of the article, which is otherwise mandatory with every noun.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Weidane Beispui: i wohn Augschburg, i wor Schui, ea gähd easchte Klass Schui (vgl. aa lat. Romae in Rom, Romam nach Rom; Hindi Dillî calnâ af Delhi foahn, stott Dillî ko calnâ).
english: Further examples: I live in Augsburg, I was at school, he goes to first grade school (cf. also lat. Romae in Rome, Romam to Rome; Hindi Dillî calnâ from Delhi, instead of Dillî ko calnâ).
note: Hindi travel to Delhi becomes from Delhi; normal English prepositions also hide the Bavarian omissions.

bar_text: S Boarische hod a komplexes System vo Richtungsadverbialien, de wo oan Bezug zua Perspektivn vom Sprecha nehma.
english: Bavarian has a complex system of directional adverbials, which take a reference to the perspectives of the speaker.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wia im Deitschn muass, je noch dem, ob de Bewegung vom Sprecha weg oda zum Sprecha hi voizong wiad, a ensprechends Affix ogfiagt wean (im Weanarischn san de zwoa Affixe zammagfoin, s wead do oisdann koa Untaschied mea gmocht).
english: As in German, depending on whether the movement is counted away from or towards the speaker, a corresponding affix must be attached (in Viennese, the two affixes have merged, so no distinction is made there anymore).
note: Movement counted is imprecise for movement performed/directed.

bar_text: Im Deitschn wean de Affixe ois Präfixe (hin- bzw. her-) vawendt, oisa am Adverb vorogstejt.
english: In German, the affixes are used as prefixes (hin- or her-), thus placed before the adverb.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Boarischn wean de Affixe ois Suffixe eigsetzt, d. h. am Adverb hinten ogfiagt; s Suffix -hin wead zu -i, regional -e obgschwächt, s Suffix -her zu -a.
english: In Bavarian, the affixes are used as suffixes, i.e., attached to the end of the adverb; the suffix -hin becomes -i, regionally weakened to -e, the suffix -her to -a.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Iwasicht zoagt de Richtungsadverbien, wias worscheinli im gonzn boarischn Raum iblich gwen san.
english: The overview shows the directional adverbs as they were probably common throughout the entire Bavarian region.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im westlichn Obabayern gengan de Formen scho längere Zeit ollawei mehra zruck und ma verwendt Formen de näha on da Hochsproch und näha am Schwäbischn san.
english: In western Upper Bavaria, the forms have been receding more and more for a long time, and forms are being used that are closer to the standard language and closer to Swabian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es is dort oiso im easchtn Schritt "auffi, auffa", "obi, oba", "eini, eina", "ummi, umma" durch "nauf, rauf", "no, ro", "nei, rei", "num, rum" ersetzt worn.
english: There, in the first step, it was replaced by 'nauf, rauf', 'no, ro', 'nei, rei', 'num, rum' instead of 'auffi, auffa', 'obi, oba', 'eini, eina', 'ummi, umma'.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wei se "no, ro" und "num", "rum" aa net so hochsprochli ohearn, wead des haintztog aa oft mit "nunta, runta" und "niba/nüba, riba/riwa/rüba" ersetzt.
english: Because they [the forms] 'no, ro' and 'num', 'rum' also do not sound so high-register, this is also often replaced nowadays with 'nunta, runta' and 'niba/nüba, riba/riwa/rüba'.
note: High-register is imprecise for resemblance to the standard language.

bar_text: Es gibt an broatn Stroafa wo ma "nauf, rauf"... und "auffi/auffar" … nebmanand verwendt.
english: There is a broad range where one uses both 'nauf, rauf'... and 'auffi/auffar' … side by side.
note: Broad range loses the explicit strip/band-shaped geographic area.

bar_text: Im Sidwestn vo Oberbayern hom se de Richtungsadverbien mit da Nochsuibm "i" und "a/ar/r" bessar hoitn kenna wia im Nordwestn vo Obabayern.
english: In the southwest of Upper Bavaria, they were able to hold onto the directional adverbs with the suffix 'i' and 'a/ar/r' better than in the northwest of Upper Bavaria.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Boarischn hods an Prozess gebm, dea wo in da Sprochwissnschoft Klitisiarung hoasst.
english: In Bavarian, there has been a process that is called cliticization in linguistics.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wos Boarische betrifft, so is damit s Drohenga vo Personalpronomina ans konjugiate Verb gmoant.
english: As far as Bavarian is concerned, this refers to the cliticization of personal pronouns to a conjugated verb.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Aus mia wiad -ma, aus dia wiad -da, se wiad zu -s usw. Vo da Obschwechung is nacha aa nua mea a kloana Schritt zua Kontraktion vom Verb mitm Personalpronom.
english: From me becomes -ma, from you becomes -da, she becomes zu -s etc. After the weakening, it is then also just a small step towards the contraction of the verb with the personal pronoun.
note: Translates away the cited input forms and leaves zu untranslated, obscuring the actual reductions.

bar_text: De Klitisiarung is a da Grund, weshoib s Pronoma vo da 1. Person Plural im Boarischn af m- olautet.
english: Cliticization is also the reason why the pronoun of the 1st person plural in Bavarian ends in m.
note: Reverses the location of m from initial to final.

bar_text: De middlhochdeitsche Verb-Endung -n und da Olaut vom Persoanalpronom wir san zum m vaschmoizn (ebenso im Schwäbischn).
english: The Middle High German verb ending -n and the umlaut of the personal pronoun wir are used to merge into m (likewise in Swabian).
note: The initial sound of wir becomes an umlaut.

bar_text: m is dann vom Sprecha nimma länga ois Verb-Endung ogseng worn, sondan ois Olaut vom Personalpronom.
english: m is then no longer perceived as a verb ending by the speaker, but as a full vowel of the personal pronoun.
note: The initial sound of the pronoun becomes a full vowel, although m is a consonant.

bar_text: Des Phänomen tritt oba ned nua in da 1. Person Plural im Nominativ af, a andane Persona wean klitisiat.
english: This phenomenon does not only occur in the 1st person plural in the nominative, other persons are also cliticized.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Omeakung: De klitisiatn Personalpronoma san durch Bindestriche trennt.
english: Note: The cliticized personal pronouns are separated by hyphens.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im easchtn Beispui weads direkte Objekt (Akkusativobjekt) klitisiat, wearend im zwoatn Subjekt und Akkusativobjekt ons Verb ogfiagt wean.
english: In the first example, the direct object (accusative object) is cliticized, whereas in the second, the subject and accusative object are attached to the verb.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im drittn Beispui gengan sogoa Subjekt, Akkusativ- und Dativobjekt a Vabindung mitm Verb ein.
english: In the third example, even subject, accusative and dative objects form a connection with the verb.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Oba ned nua de Verbn kenna ois Element gnutzt wean, an de wo de obgschächtn Personalpronomina ogfiagt wean.
english: But not only the verbs can be used as an element to which the cliticized personal pronouns are attached.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Des is aa bei Nebmsotzeinleitan mäglich.
english: This is also possible with subordinate clause initiators.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wen a Personalpronoma klitisiat worn is, dann deaf de Voifoam davo nimma im gleichn Sotz vorkema: Se schloft oda Schloft-s?
english: Once a personal pronoun has been cliticized, then the full form of it may no longer appear in the same sentence: Se schloft or Schloft-s?
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: owa nia ned Se schloft-s, des warad ungrammatisch.
english: but never ever she sleeps-s, that would be ungrammatical.
note: Replaces the cited Bavarian Se schloft-s with an English hybrid, obscuring the actual clitic example.

bar_text: A Sondafoi und a Ausnohm za dem buidd de Nominativ-Form vo da 2. Person Singular und in an grossn Tei vom Boarischn aa de 2. Person Plural, sowia ia a poa Regiona aa de 1. Person Plural.
english: A special case and an exception to this picture: the nominative form of the 2nd person singular and, in a large part of Bavarian, also the 2nd person plural, as well as in a few regions also the 1st person plural.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Do liegt nacha ned nua a Klitisiarung vor, sondan de ehemolign Klitika hom scho an Status vo ana Flexionsendung.
english: In this case, it is not just cliticization that occurs, but the former clitics already have the status of a flexion ending.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Das du vo da 2. Person Singular is scho im Oidhochdeitschn duach inverse Sotzstellung an de urspringliche Endung -s ogfiagt worn, de wo de heite aa standardsprochliche Endung -st eagem hod.
english: The 'du' of the 2nd person singular was already attached to the original ending -s through inverse word order in Old High German, which has since been replaced by today's standard language ending -st.
note: Changes the causal formation of -st by attachment into a later replacement.

bar_text: Regional kena aa andane Obweichunga fiakema.
english: Regionally, other deviations can also occur.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Manche Verbn vom Boarischn erfordan a andane Rektion wia im Standarddeitschn, z. B. diaschtn („duastig sei“), drama („träumen“) und rein („bereuen“).
english: Some verbs of Bavarian require a different government than in Standard German, e.g., diaschtn (“to be dusty”), drama (“to dream”) and rein (“to regret”).
note: Changes thirsty to dusty in the verb's gloss.

bar_text: Se wean mitm logischn Subjektiv im Dativ oda Akkusativ gnuzd (sog. Quirky Case).
english: They are used with the logical subject in the dative or accusative (so-called Quirky Case).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A formals Subjekt ist efta ned voahandn.
english: A formal subject is often not present beforehand.
note: Adds beforehand; vorhanden only means present/existing.

bar_text: Im Boarischn wean, andas wiar im Standarddeitschn, Adjektive in attributiva Stejung markiat; dazu deant s invariable Suffix -a bzw. -e; s handelt se dobei um erstoarte Nom.
english: In Bavarian, unlike in Standard German, adjectives in the attributive position are marked; for this purpose, the invariable suffix -a or -e is used; these are strengthened nouns.
note: erstoarte Nom. means fossilized nominative, not strengthened nouns.

bar_text: -Forman (maskulin bzw. feminin).
english: -forms (masculine or feminine).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Soichane Attribute kenna af Subjekt wia aa Objekt bezogn sei.
english: Such attributes can be related to a subject as well as an object.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Des schmeggt koida bessa.
english: Nobody tastes it better.
note: That tastes better cold becomes nobody tastes it better, changing the subject and omitting cold.

bar_text: – Das schmeckt kalt besser.
english: – That tastes better cold.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fost hedns eam lebanda eigrom.
english: They almost had him buried alive.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: – Fast hätten sie ihn lebendig eingegraben.
english: – They almost would have buried him alive.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Boarischn kimmt da doppetn Vanaanung a grosse Bedeitung zua.
english: In Bavarian, double negation is of great importance.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Beispui: In da Stod huift koana neamd neda.
english: Example: In the city, no one helps anyone else.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Boarischn ko a Sotz amoi oda meamois vaneint wean, da Sinn bleibt in da Regl da gleiche.
english: In Bavarian, a sentence can sometimes or mostly be negated, but the meaning remains the same in principle.
note: The count once/multiple times becomes sometimes/mostly, losing the multiple-negation contrast.

bar_text: * neamdm und neamdn san vo da Aussproch hea ned zan Untascheidn.
english: * neamdm and neamdn cannot be distinguished by pronunciation.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S formale Subjekt es wiad efta elidiat, z. B. er is da gresste Depp, wo gibt.
english: The formal subject 'es' is often eliminated, e.g., er is da gresste Depp, wo gibt.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A kloana Ibablick iba de wichtigstn Wortfejda und Meglichkeitn vo da Wortbuidung:
english: A small overview of the most important word fields and possibilities of word formation:
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Um dena regionaln Untaschiedn grecht zum wean, wean mange Wäate gsondat kennzeichnet: A Österreichischa Wortschotz B Oidbayrischa Wortschotz H Burgnländischa Wortschotz (Heanzisch) K Karntna Wortschotz S Steirischa Wortschotz T Tirola Wortschotz W Weana Wortschotz
english: To do justice to the regional differences, many words will be specially marked: A Austrian vocabulary B Old Bavarian vocabulary H Burgenland vocabulary (Heanzisch) K Carinthian vocabulary S Styrian vocabulary T Tyrolean vocabulary W Viennese vocabulary
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fleischa (Metzger), Tischla (Schreiner), Spangla (Klempner), Bäck (Bäcker), Zeidla (Imker), Hafna (Töpfa), Sandla (W; Obdachlosa), Striezi (W; Zuahejta)
english: Butcher (metzger), carpenter (schreiner), plumber (klempner), baker (bäcker), beekeeper (imker), potter (töpfer), homeless person (W; obdachloser), outsider (W; zuhejter)
note: Loses the Bavarian lexical forms and changes Zuhalter/pimp to outsider.

bar_text: S Boarische hod oft a Vuizoi vo ausdrucksstoarkn Begriff fia a Soch.
english: Bavarian often has a multitude of expressive terms for a thing.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fia Mund gibts zum Beispui Mai (ugs.), Goschn (frech) oda Goschal (liabevoi), Babbn (frech), Lätschn (obweatend) oda Fotzn (beleidigend).
english: For mouth, there are for example Mai (colloquial), Goschn (cheeky) or Goschal (full of love), Babbn (cheeky), Lätschn (disrespectful) or Fotzn (insulting).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A fias Gwand gibts an Hafa typisch boarische Ausdrick: Gwand sejm,Joppn („Jackn“), Pfoidl oda Pfoadl (fia Hemad), Diandl z. B.
english: For clothing, there is a lot of typical Bavarian expression: Gwand (clothing), Joppn (“jacket”), Pfoidl or Pfoadl (for shirts), Diandl, for example.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fia d Viecha gibt aa an bsondan boarischn Woatschotz, z. B. Giggal (Hahn), Bibbal oda Ziwarl (kloans Hendl), Heiß(al) (jungs Pferd, Foihn), Goaß, Hebbal (junge Goaß), For(n) (Jungstia, Stiakaibe), Böichn (ahd. belihha; Blässhendl), da Imp oda de Impn (Biene), Oachkatzl, Brotz (lat. Loanwoat, Grod), Hotz (Eichlhäha) usw.
english: For animals, there is also a special Bavarian vocabulary, e.g., Giggal (rooster), Bibbal or Ziwarl (small chicken), Heiß(al) (young horse, foal), Goaß (goat), Hebbal (young goat), For(n) (young deer, stag), Böichn (Old Bavarian belihha; speckled chicken), da Imp or de Impn (bee), Oachkatzl (squirrel), Brotz (Latin loanword, Grod), Hotz (squirrel) etc.
note: Young bull, coot and jay are mistranslated; Grod/toad is left untranslated and ahd. becomes Old Bavarian.

bar_text: Zum boarischn Vokabulaa im Bereich vo de Lebmsmiddl schaug: Austro-Boarischa Kuchlwoatschotz.
english: For the Bavarian vocabulary in the area of food, look: Austro-Bavarian kitchen vocabulary.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Des produktivste Suffix zua Buidung vo Adjektiven is -ad; des gehd entweda afs Suffix -ert zruck, oda afs Suffix -end, dees wo eigentli zur Buidung vom Partizip Präsens vawendt wiad (boade Suffixe san im Boarischen lautli zammagfoin).
english: The most productive suffix for the formation of adjectives is -ad; this either goes back to the suffix -ert, or to the suffix -end, which is actually used for the formation of the present participle (both suffixes have merged phonetically in Bavarian).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Stammendunga in Klamman (moast -g oda -ch) wean im traditionejn Boarisch nur gsogt, wens Adjektiv flektiat wead und daduach a vokalische Endung dahoit.
english: Derivations in parentheses (mostly -g or -ch) are only said in traditional Bavarian when the adjective is inflected and thereby maintains a vocalic ending.
