note: Stem endings become derivations and acquiring a vowel ending becomes maintaining one.

bar_text: Es gibt owa aa regionale und lokale Ausnohma.
english: But there are also regional and local exceptions.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: 12:15 – Viadl noch zwejfe (sejtana: Viadl iwa zwejfe); weanarisch, nordobaboarisch : Viadl aans
english: 12:15 – Quarter to twelve (dialect: Quarter past twelve); Viennese, North Upper Bavarian: Quarter one
note: Quarter to twelve gives 11:45 rather than 12:15, and rarely becomes dialect.

bar_text: 12:30 – hoibe/a oans
english: 12:30 – half/half past one
note: Half past one changes the clock value from 12:30 to 1:30.

bar_text: 12:45 – Dreiviadl oans/Viadl vor oans, sejten: Viadl af oans
english: 12:45 – Three quarters one/Quarter to one, seldom: Quarter to one
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Bei voin Stundn, ob viar kimmt imma no a -e dazua:
english: With full hours, such as four, an -e is always added:
note: Such as four replaces the explicit starting-at-four restriction.

bar_text: 16:00 – viare
english: 16:00 – four o'clock
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: 16:30 – hoibe fimfe
english: 16:30 – half five
note: Half five conventionally means 5:30 in English; the source means half past four.

bar_text: Wia im engl.
english: As in English.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Sprochraum wead in Bayern des 12 h Format vawendd:
english: In the language area, the 12 h format is used in Bavaria:
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: 14:30 – hoibe drei (am Nammidog)
english: 14:30 – half three (in the afternoon)
note: Half three conventionally means 3:30 in English, not 14:30.

bar_text: De boarischn Wochadogsnama, de wo vom Standarddeitschn etymologisch obweicha (oiso da Deansdog und da Dunnasdog), stamma ausn Einflussbereich vo da Gotischn Sproch.
english: The Bavarian weekday names, which etymologically deviate from Standard German (namely Deansdog and Dunnasdog), stem from the sphere of influence of the Gothic language.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fir Details schaug: De boarische Wocha
english: For details look: The Bavarian Week
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es gibt zwoa aa im Standarddeitschn verbale Prefixe, im Boarischn san de owa vui produktiva.
english: There are also two verbal prefixes in standard German, but in Bavarian they are much more productive.
note: Misreads the concessive zwoa ... owa as two verbal prefixes.

bar_text: da- (< der-) entspricht am standarddeitschn er-, kimmt owa a mit Verben voa, de wo im Hochdeitsch des Präfix ned hom kena.
english: da- (< der-) corresponds to the standard German er-, but also occurs with verbs that could not have had the prefix in High German.
note: Uses a past could-not-have-had formulation for the source's general cannot-have restriction.

bar_text: zamm (zamma) [com-] entspricht am Standarddeitschn zusammen-, es wead no haifiga vawendt ois dees.
english: zamm (zamma) [com-] corresponds to the standard German zusammen-, it is used even more frequently than that.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S Boarische hod regional vaschiedane Diminutivsuffixe, vo dena -l, -e und -al (< -erl) de haifgstn san.
english: Bavarian has regionally different diminutive suffixes, of which -l, -e and -al (< -erl) are the most common.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Des -l is sogoa stoark lexikalisiat, d. h. s wiad oft gor nimma ois Diminutiv vastandn.
english: This -l is even strongly lexicalized, i.e., it is often no longer understood as a diminutive.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Vui vo de Diminutive ohne a Grundwort beziang se oft af Meschn, deo wo oan af irenoa Oat load doa.
english: Many of the diminutives without a base word often refer to people who act in their own particular way.
note: Acting in their own particular way loses the key evoking-pity meaning.

bar_text: Im Berchtesgoana Land, Cheamgau, Toaln vom Soizburga Land, Soizkammaguad und vom Bayrischn Oberland sowia aa im Tirola Untaland und im steirischn Tauerngebiet is des Diminutivsuffix moast ned -(a)l, sondern -ei.
english: In the Berchtesgaden area, Chiemgau, valleys of the Salzburg area, Salzkammergut and from the Bavarian Upper Land as well as also in the Tyrolean Lowland and in the Styrian Tauern region, the diminutive suffix is mostly not -(a)l, but -ei.
note: Toaln means parts here, not valleys, narrowing the regional distribution.

bar_text: Da Hiasl wiad dann zum Hiasei.
english: Hiasl then becomes a Hiasei.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Andane Beispui: Dirnei fia Madl, Hansei fia Hansl usw.
english: Other examples: Dirnei for girls, Hansei for Hansl etc.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Deitschland (amtle: Bundesrepublik Deutschland) is a Stoot in Middleiropa.
english: Germany (officially: Federal Republic of Germany) is a state in Central Europe.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ois Bundesstoot wiad de Bundesrepublik Deutschland aus dena 16 deitschn Ländan buidt.
english: As a federal state, the Federal Republic of Germany is built from the 16 German states.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Lända gliedan se wieda nochm Vafossungsprinzip vo da kommunaln Sejbstvawoitung in kommunale Gebietskeapaschoftn.
english: The lands are again divided according to the constitutional principle of municipal self-administration into municipal territorial authorities.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Bundeshaptstod is Berlin.
english: The federal capital is Berlin.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: As politische System is fedaral und ois parlamentarische Demokratie organisiat.
english: The political system is federal and organized as a parliamentary democracy.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Deitschland is mid eppa 81,8 Mijona Eihwohna (2015) da bevejkarungsreichste Stoot vo da EU.
english: Germany is, with about 81.8 million inhabitants (2015), the most populous state of the EU.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Deitschland is unta andam Mitgliad vo de Vaeintn Nationa, vo da NATO und vo de G7 (Gruppm vo de Siem), sowia Grindungsmitgliad vo da EU.
english: Germany is among other members of the United Nations, of NATO and of the G7 (Group of Seven), as well as a founding member of the EU.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Des gresste Bundesland vo Deitschland is Bayern, s beväikarungsreichste is Noadrhein-Westfoin.
english: The largest federal state of Germany is Bavaria, the most populous is North Rhine-Westphalia.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da Begriff Deutschland wead in dera Foam eascht seit da Friajn Neizeit vawendt, zum Beispui in Die Verfassung des deutschen Reiches (1667) vom Samuel von Pufendorf.
english: The term Germany is first used in this form since the Early Modern period, for example in The Constitution of the German Empire (1667) by Samuel von Pufendorf.
note: The historical word under discussion is Deutschland, not the English word Germany.

bar_text: Voahea hods deitsch nua ois Eigschoftswoat gebm, in da Foam vo: a deitsches Land oda de deitschn Lända owa ned zammagsetz; ned amoi ois das deitsche Land.
english: Previously, German was only given as an attributive word, in the form of: a German country or the German lands, but not as a compound; not even as the German country.
note: Replaces the essential German word forms with English glosses in the metalinguistic history claim.

bar_text: Deitschland liegt in Middleiropa, zwischn 47°16′15″ und 55°03′33″ neadlicha Broadn und 5°52′01″ und 15°02′37″ estlicha Leng.
english: Germany lies in Central Europe, between 47°16′15″ and 55°03′33″ northern latitude and 5°52′01″ and 15°02′37″ eastern longitude.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Noadn grenzt Deitschland an Dänemark (auf ana Läng vo 67 km), im Nordostn an Poin (442 km), im Ostn an d Tschechei (811 km), im Südosten an Östareich (815 km; ohne Grenz im Bodnsee), im Sidn an d Schweiz (316 km; mid Grenzn vo da Exklave Büsingen, owa ohne Grenz im Bodnsee), im Siidwestn an Frankreich (448 km), im Westn an Luxmburg (135 km) und Belgien (156 km) und im Nordwestn an Holland (567 km).
english: In the north, Germany borders Denmark (along a length of 67 km), in the northeast Poland (442 km), in the east the Czech Republic (811 km), in the southeast Austria (815 km; without a border in Lake Constance), in the south Switzerland (316 km; with borders from the exclave Büsingen, but without a border in Lake Constance), in the southwest France (448 km), in the west Luxembourg (135 km) and Belgium (156 km) and in the northwest Holland (567 km).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Grenzläng betrogt insgesamt 3757 km.
english: The border length amounts to a total of 3757 km.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wearend im Nordwestn de Kistn vo da Nordsee und im Nordostn de vo da Ostsee de natialichn Stootsgrenzn buidn, hod Deitschland im Sidn Ontei on de Oipn.
english: While the North Sea forms the natural state borders in the northwest and the Baltic Sea in the northeast, Germany has the Alps to the south.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Deitschland gheat voiständig zua gmäßigtn Klimazone vo Middleiropa im Bereich vo da Westwindzone.
english: Germany belongs entirely to the temperate climate zone of Central Europe in the area of the westerlies.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S liegt im Iwagangsbereich zwischn am Seeklima in Westeiropa und am Kontinentalklima in Osteiropa.
english: It lies in the transition zone between a maritime climate in Western Europe and a continental climate in Eastern Europe.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S Klima wead zuadem vom Goifstrom stoak beeinflusst, dea wo de klimatischn Weate fia de Broadnlog ungwehnli muid gstoitn duat.
english: The climate is also strongly influenced by the Gulf Stream, which makes the climatic weather for the latitudes unusually mild.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De middlare jearliche Niedaschlogsmenge is 700 Millimeter (begzong auf de Joar vo 1961 -1990).
english: The average annual precipitation amount is 700 millimeters (referring to the years 1961 - 1990).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De middlare Niadaschlogsmenge pro Monat liegt zwischn 40 Millimeta im Feba und 77 Millimeta im Juni.
english: The average precipitation amount per month lies between 40 millimeters in February and 77 millimeters in June.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De tiafste jo in Deitschland gmessane Temparatua woa −45,9 Grad Celsius; se is am 24. Dezemba 2001 am Funtensee gmessn woan.
english: The lowest temperature measured in Germany was −45.9 degrees Celsius; it was measured on December 24, 2001, at Funtensee.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De bislang hechste Temparatur woa 40,3 Grad Celsius und is am 8. August 2003 in Nennig im Saarland erfosst woan.
english: The highest temperature so far was 40.3 degrees Celsius and was recorded on August 8, 2003, in Nennig in Saarland.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Ogobm dazua san owa zum Tei wiedasprichli.
english: The values for this are, however, partly contradictory.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Dees kristalline Gstoa in Deitschland, wia Gneis und Granit in de Middlgebiag, geht afs Paleozoikum (Eadoitadum) zruck.
english: The crystalline rocks in Germany, such as gneiss and granite in the central uplands, date back to the Paleozoic (Eoarchean).
note: Eadoitadum refers to the Paleozoic, not the Eoarchean era added in parentheses.

bar_text: Deitschland liegt voi af da Eirasischn Plottn, trotzdem keman schwoche Eadbebm fia.
english: Germany lies completely on the Eurasian plate, nevertheless weak earthquakes occur.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Bsundas guit dees fia Sidwestn (Region vo de Riftzona) und im Westn (Obarheingrobm, Rheingrobm, Hohenzollangrobm).
english: This is especially true for the southwest (region of the rift zone) and in the west (Upper Rhine Graben, Rhine Graben, Hohenzollern Graben).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: In da Nordsee dominian de Inselgruppm vo de Nordfriesischn Insln und de Inslkettn vo de Ostfriesischn Insln.
english: In the North Sea, the island groups of the North Frisian Islands and the island chain of the East Frisian Islands predominate.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Helgoland und Neuwerk san aa bewont.
english: Helgoland and Neuwerk are also inhabited.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Nordfriesischn Insln san Restln vom Festland, wo duach Landsenkung und nochfoigende Iwaflutung vo da Kistn trennt worn san.
english: The North Frisian islands are remnants of the mainland, which were separated by land subsidence and subsequent flooding of the sea.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Ostfriesischn Insln san Barriereinsln, wo duach de Brandungsdynamik aus Sandbenkn enstondn san.
english: The East Frisian Islands are barrier islands that were created from sandbanks through surf dynamics.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Flora is in Deitschland vo da gmäßigtn Klimazone vun Lab- und Nodlwejida pregt.
english: The flora in Germany is characterized by the temperate climate zone of broadleaf and needle forests.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Labwejda bestenga moastns aus Rotbuachn, danem gibts Oachnwejda und imma sejtna aa Auwejda.
english: The riparian forests consist mostly of beech, besides that there are oak forests and even more rarely also willow forests.
note: Changes broadleaf forests to riparian and floodplain forests to willow forests.

bar_text: In de Oipn und Middlgebiag gibts Schluchtwoid.
english: In the Alps and mountain regions, there are coniferous forests.
note: Schluchtwoid means ravine/gorge forests, not coniferous forests.

bar_text: Ohne menschlichn Eifluss dadat de Vegetation in Deitschland haaptsächli aus Woid besteh.
english: Without human influence, the vegetation in Germany would mainly consist of forest.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Deazeit san 29,5 Prozent vo da Stootsflöchn Woid.
english: At present, 29.5 percent of the national area is forest.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Damit gheat Deitschland zu dena woidreichstn Lända vo da Eiropejischen Union(EU).
english: Because of this, Germany is among the most forested countries of the European Union (EU).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Weidas gibts no Hoad- und Moorlandschoftn sowia vegetationsoame oipine Regiona.
english: Furthermore, there are also heath and moor landscapes as well as vegetationally open regions.
note: Omits that the sparsely vegetated regions are Alpine.

bar_text: Da gresste Otei vom unbebautn Land wead fian Obau vo Nutzpflanzn vawendd; voa oim Droad wia Geastn, Hafa, Roggn und Woazn; dozua kema voa oim no Erdepfi un Raps.
english: The largest part of the unbuilt land is used for the cultivation of crops; above all grain such as spelt, barley, rye and wheat; in addition to that, above all potatoes and rapeseed.
note: The barley/oats pair Geastn/Hafa becomes spelt/barley.

bar_text: In mangn Flussdoin wia an da Mosl, am Main und am Rhein zum Beispui wead Wein obaut.
english: In many river valleys, such as the Moselle, the Main, and the Rhine for example, wine is grown.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De moastn Saigeviecha in Deitschland lebm in de Labwejda.
english: Most of the wild animals in Germany live in the meadows.
note: Changes mammals to wild animals and deciduous forests to meadows.

bar_text: Do gibts vaschiedane Marderoatn, Dam- und Rothiaschn, Reh, Wuidsaun und Fuxn.
english: There are various types of martens, roe deer, red squirrels, roe deer, wild boar and foxes.
note: Fallow and red deer become roe deer and red squirrels.

bar_text: Biba und Otta findt ma in Flussauen nua no sejtn, zum Tei gibts owa aa wieda steigende Beständ.
english: Biba and Otta are only found rarely in river meadows now, though in part there are also rising populations again.
note: The two animal names are left in Bavarian, losing their English identification.

bar_text: Andane gräßare Saigeviecha de wo friaha in Middleiropa glebt hom gibts nimma.
english: Other larger wild animals that used to live in Central Europe no longer exist.
note: Wild animals is less specific than the source's mammals.

bar_text: An Auaoxn (seit 1846), an Braunbär (seit 1835), an Ejch (seitm Middloida), s Wuidpferd (seitm 19. Joahundat), an Wisent (seitm 17./18.
english: An auk (since 1846), a brown bear (since 1835), an elk (since the Middle Ages), the wild horse (since the 19th century), a wisent (since the 17./18.
note: Changes aurochs to the bird auk.

bar_text: Joahhundat und an Woif (seit 1904).
english: centuries and a wolf (since 1904).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: In neiara Zeit wandan gelegentli Ejche, Wejfe und mangmoi sogoa Bärn ein.
english: In modern times, badgers, foxes, and sometimes even bears are occasionally moving back in.
note: Elk and wolves become badgers and foxes.

bar_text: Wengam schlechtn Ruaf vom Woif und vom Bärn fiaht dees owa efta za Problem.
english: Because of the bad reputation of the wolf and the bear, this often leads to problems.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Deitschland besteht aus 16 teisouvarena Lenda.
english: Germany consists of 16 sovereign states.
note: Drops partly from the sovereignty description.

bar_text: De ejtastn Siadlungsbelege afn Gebiet vom heitign Deitschland san etwa 700.000 Joar oid und ma gehd davo aus, dass de Region seit 500.000 Joar permanent bsiadlt is.
english: The oldest settlement evidence in the area of present-day Germany is about 700,000 years old and it is assumed that the region has been permanently inhabited for 500,000 years.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es gibt dahea in Deitschland aa bedeitende paläoanthropologische Fundstättn: Nöchm Fundort bei Heidelberg is de Hominini-Oat Homo heidelbergensis gnennt woan und nochm Neandertal in Mettmann da Homo neanderthalensis, dea wo ausm Homo heidelbergensis heavoagangane Neandertaler.
english: There are also significant paleoanthropological sites there in Germany: after the discovery site near Heidelberg, the Hominini species was called Homo heidelbergensis, and after the Neander Valley in Mettmann, Homo neanderthalensis, the Neanderthal who descended from Homo heidelbergensis.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Menschnoat is voa etwa 40.000 Joar dann vom Homo sapiens(moderna Mensch), dea wo aus Afrika kema is, vadrängt woan.
english: Neanderthal man was displaced about 40,000 years ago by Homo sapiens (modern human), who came from Africa.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: In da Jungstoazeit hom se nacha Ackabau, Viechazucht und feste Siedlungsplätz entwicket.
english: In the Neolithic period, they later developed arable farming, animal husbandry, and permanent settlements.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Aus dera Zeit san bedeitende kuituarelle Funde dahoidn, wia etwa de Himmesscheibm vo Nebra, de zoagt, dass scho um 2000 v. Kr.
english: Significant cultural finds from that time are preserved, such as the Nebra sky disc, which shows that already around 2000 BC.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: in da Region Astronomie betriebm woan is.
english: astronomy was being practiced in the region.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Um 500 v. Kr.
english: Around 500 BC
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: woas heitige Siiddeitschland kejtisch und s heitige Norddeitschland germanisch besiedlt.
english: around 500 BC, today's southern Germany was Celtic-settled and today's northern Germany was Germanic-settled.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Germanen san im Laf vo de Joarhundate imma weida inan Sidn gwandat.
english: The Germanic peoples migrated further and further south over the course of the centuries.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Um Christi Geburt woa dann de Donau de ungefäare Siedlungsgrenz zwischn Kejten und Germanen.
english: At the birth of Christ, the Danube was then the approximate settlement border between Celts and Germans.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: So san a vui kejtische Orts- und Gwässanama und kejtische Lehnweata in de germanischn Sprochn kema.
english: In this way, many Celtic place and water names and Celtic loanwords have come into the Germanic languages.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Des Heilige Remische Reich (deitscha Nation), des de mehra Zeit vo de Habsburga ois Kaiser vo Wean aus regiad worn is, hod vo 962 bis 1806 Bstand ghabt.

note: Omits Austria and adds Scharnitz-relative location and 1160 m altitude.

bar_text: Zwischn Scharnitz und Mittnwoid fliaßts iaba d' Grenz vo Estareich noch Bayern (Deitschland).
english: Between Scharnitz and Mittenwald, it flows across the border from Austria to Bavaria (Germany).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Zwischn Scharnitz und Mittnwoid fliaßts iaba d' Grenz vo Estareich noch Bayern (Deitschland).
english: The Isar enters Upper Bavaria after c. 22 km just north of Scharnitz and the Isar is dammed for the first time between Mittenwald and Krün.
note: Adds 22 km and a dam; omits the explicit Austria-to-Bavaria crossing between the two places.

bar_text: Se hod a Leng vo 295 Kilometa.
english: It has a length of 295 kilometers.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Se hod a Leng vo 295 Kilometa.
english: With 295 km (183 mi) length, it is among the longest rivers in Bavaria, and it is Germany's second most important tributary of the Danube.
note: Adds longest-river and second-most-important-tributary claims to the length statement.

bar_text: Neba Minga liang de Städt Däiz, Freising, Moosburg und Landshuad an da Isar.
english: Besides Munich, the cities of Dachau, Freising, Moosburg and Landshut lie on the Isar.
note: Däiz refers to Bad Tölz, not Dachau.

bar_text: Neba Minga liang de Städt Däiz, Freising, Moosburg und Landshuad an da Isar.
english: The Isar river enters Germany near Mittenwald and flows through Krün, Wallgau, Bad Tölz, Munich, and Landshut, before entering the Danube near Deggendorf. With 295 km (183 mi) length, it is among the longest rivers in Bavaria, and it is Germany's second most important tributary of the Danube.
note: Omits Freising and Moosburg and adds route, length and tributary-ranking claims.

bar_text: De greaßtn Zufliass han d' Amper bei Moosburg, d' Loisach bei Wolfratshausn und d' Moosach bei Freising.
english: The largest tributaries are the Amper near Moosburg, the Loisach near Wolfratshausen, and the Moosach near Freising.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De greaßtn Zufliass han d' Amper bei Moosburg, d' Loisach bei Wolfratshausn und d' Moosach bei Freising.
english: Just north of the town the Loisach flows into the Isar. The Isar continues on to and through the Munich gravel plain which ends within the city limits of Munich.
note: Omits two tributaries and their locations and replaces the list with Loisach and Munich-route details.

bar_text: D' Isar is noch da Donau, am Inn und am Main da viertlängste Fluss in Bayern.
english: After the Danube, the Inn, and the Main, the Isar is the fourth longest river in Bavaria.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: D' Isar is noch da Donau, am Inn und am Main da viertlängste Fluss in Bayern.

english: For a long time it was said that the name Isar came from Celtic and meant something like rushing water (ys = snow, rushing and ura = water, river).
note: schnej means fast here, not snow; the rest of the historical Celtic explanation is retained.

bar_text: Lange Zeit hods ghoaßn, der Nama Isar dad ausm keltischn kemma und sovui wia reißnds Wossa (ys = schnej, reißnd und ura = Wossa, Fluss) bedeitn.

bar_text: Des guid inzwischn ois vaaltate Meinung.

bar_text: D'Sprachforscher moana jetzad es dad vo da indogermanischn Wurzl es/is (fia fließnds Wossa) kemma, de se a in fui andane Flußnama wiadafindt und se in aktuelle Sprachn nua no aufs feste Wossa, oiso s Eis bziagt.
english: Linguists now think that it may have come from the Indo-European root es/is (for flowing water), which can also be found in many other river names and, in current languages, only refers to frozen water, i.e., ice.

bar_text: D'Sprachforscher moana jetzad es dad vo da indogermanischn Wurzl es/is (fia fließnds Wossa) kemma, de se a in fui andane Flußnama wiadafindt und se in aktuelle Sprachn nua no aufs feste Wossa, oiso s Eis bziagt.
english: One theory is that the name Isar stems from *es or *is in the Indo-European languages, meaning "flowing water", and later turned into a word with a meaning narrowed to frozen water (hence English ice, German: Eis) in Proto-Germanic.
note: Omits occurrence in other river names and changes the current-language restriction to a Proto-Germanic account with added examples.

bar_text: A guads Drum vom Wossa des auf'd boarischn Oipn unds Kawendl foid fliaßt durch d' Isar zur Donau und so bis ins Schwoazze Meea.

bar_text: A guads Drum vom Wossa des auf'd boarischn Oipn unds Kawendl foid fliaßt durch d' Isar zur Donau und so bis ins Schwoazze Meea.

bar_text: S' gsamte Einzugsgebiat hod a Flächn vo 9000 Quadratkilometa.

bar_text: Wei a Guads vom Niedaschlog in de Berg ois Schnee foid hods zur Schneeschmelz as meiste Wossa.

bar_text: Wei a Guads vom Niedaschlog in de Berg ois Schnee foid hods zur Schneeschmelz as meiste Wossa.

english: For a long time, all the water was diverted to Lake Walchensee.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da a as meiste vom Rißboch zum Woichasee umgleit wurd is d'Isar zwischn Krea und am Sylvenstoa ab und zua a austrocknd.
english: Since most of the Rißbach was diverted to the Walchensee, the Isar between Krün and the Sylvenstein occasionally dries up.
note: Uses a current habitual dries up where the source describes past occasional drying associated with the diversion.

bar_text: Des ganze Wassa kimmt zwar letzendlich iaban Kochesee und Loisach wiada zruck in d'Isar, aba bis Wolfratshausn fejds im Flußlauf.
english: All the water does eventually come back into the Isar via the Kochelsee and Loisach, but it is missing from the river course up to Wolfratshausen.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Inzwischn werd a greaßana Teil vom Wossa in da Isar glassn.
english: In the meantime, a larger part of the water is being left in the Isar.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A de fuin Seitnkanäle fia de Flußkraftwerk z. B. in da Nach vo Minga entziehn am wildn Flußlauf as Wossa.
english: Even the side channels for the hydroelectric power plants, e.g., in the vicinity of Munich, withdraw water from the wild river course.
note: Omits that the side channels are numerous.

bar_text: Außadem vahindern de Wehre an Transport vom Geschiebe.
english: In addition, the weirs prevent the transport of sediment.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Deszweng grobt se d' Isar a tiafas Flußbett.
english: Because of this, the Isar digs itself a deep riverbed.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A de Nutzung ois Kühlwassa fias Kernkraftwerk tuat am Fluß ned guad, wei dadurch sei Temperatur steigt.
english: Using it as cooling water for the nuclear power plant is not good for the river, because its temperature rises as a result.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Dafia gibts aba Grenzwert, in oam hoaßn Somma hod as Kernkraftwerk scho drosselt wern miaßn, weis sonst de Umweltauflagn ned dafüllt hed.
english: However, there is a limit to that; in one hot summer, the nuclear power plant already had to be throttled, because otherwise the environmental requirements would not have been met.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fast scho zum Nama dazua gheard ois Zuasotz da Farbeidruck.
english: The impression of color almost belongs to the name as an addition.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S' is ois greane Isar bekannt.
english: It is known as the green Isar.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Des is aba nua de Farb vo am klarn Wossa, des erscheint tatsächli greablau.
english: But that is only the color of clear water, which actually appears gray-blue.
note: greablau means green-blue, not gray-blue.

bar_text: De Farb hods in niederschlogsarme Zeitn, wenn da greaßte Teil vom Wossa aus de Quelln stammt.
english: This color is present in periods of low precipitation, when the greatest part of the water comes from the springs.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Noch starke Regnfäll gibts durch Erosion an Haffa Schlamm und Dreck im Wossa, dann werds undurchsichtig lehmig braun.
english: After heavy rainfall, there is a lot of mud and dirt in the water due to erosion, then it becomes opaque and loamy brown.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Iaba s' Enstehen vo dea greablaun Farb is ma se ned ganz einig.
english: There is no consensus on the emergence of the greenish-blue color.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wahrscheinlich is a Zammspui vo Algn und am glästn Koich.
english: It is probably a combination of algae and the bright pebbles.
note: glästn Koich is dissolved lime, not bright pebbles.

bar_text: Da Eindruck werd vastärkt durch de helln Koichsteana am Grund vom Fluß und dem sonst recht klarn Wossa.
english: The impression is reinforced by the bright pebbles at the bottom of the river and the otherwise quite clear water.
note: Bright pebbles omit the limestone material.

bar_text: Dadurch kimmt a Haffa Liacht aus'm Fluß zruck und iabastrahlt des vo da Oberflächn reflektierte Liacht.
english: As a result, a lot of light comes back from the river and irradiates the light reflected from the surface.
note: Changes outshines to irradiates, losing the comparison between the two light sources.

bar_text: So hod de tatsächliche Farb vom Wassa an greaßan Eifluß auf an Farbeidruck ois de Farb vom Himme oda da Umgebung.
english: Thus, the actual color of the water has a greater influence on a color impression than the color of the sky or the surroundings.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fo da Farb is a as Biamischdrangl d'Isarmass inspiriad.
english: Regarding the color, the beer mixture has also been inspired by the Isar mass.
note: Treats Isarmass as the inspiration for a separate beer mixture; the named drink itself is inspired by the river's color.

bar_text: Zwischn Arzbach und Däiz is oana recht fleißig dabei, daß a noch am jedn Hochwassa seine Stoahaffa nei aufschicht.
english: Between Arzbach and Deiz, someone is quite busy making sure that he piles up his stone heaps again at every flood.
note: At every flood is less precise than the explicit after every flood.

bar_text: De Haffa han ois Isarpyramidn bekannt und a scho mehrmois in da Zeidung und am Fernsehn erwähnt worn.
english: The piles of gravel are known as Isar pyramids and have already been mentioned several times in the newspaper and on television.
note: Narrows the stone heaps to gravel piles; the naming and media coverage are retained.

bar_text: Da Erbauer sejba nend des Platzl Kloa-Kairo.
english: The builder himself doesn't call the little spot 'Little Cairo'.
note: Doesn't call reverses the source's statement that he calls the spot Little Cairo.

bar_text: A Altarbuidl vo 1480 in da Jakobskirch in Lengrias is a Beispui fia oide Darstellunga vo da Isar.
english: An altar picture from 1480 in St. James Church in Lenggries is an example of old depictions of the Isar.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da unbkannte Moier hod s'Köpfn vom Apostel Jakobus ans Ufer vo da Isar valegt.
english: The unknown Moor laid the head of the Apostle James on the bank of the Isar.
note: Moier is painter, not Moor; s'Köpfn is the beheading scene, not laying a head on the bank.

bar_text: Im 19. Jahrhundert ham an Haffa Mola aus da Münchner Schui d' Isar ois Motiv fia eanane Buidl entdeckt.
english: In the 19th century, a lot of painters from the Munich School discovered the Isar as a motif for their pictures.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wei de recht gnau gmoid hom wern de Buidl a ois Dokumentation fia de Vaänderunga vo da Landschaft durch d'Leid ogseng.
english: Because they were painted quite precisely, these pictures are also seen by people as documentation of the changes to the landscape.
note: durch d'Leid modifies the landscape changes caused by people, not who regards the pictures as documentation.

bar_text: Im Jäger vo Foi hod da Ludwig Ganghofer am Isarwinke und seine Bewohna a literarischs Denkmoi gsetzt und damit zur Bekanntheit vo der Gengd beitrong.
english: In *The Hunter of Fall*, Ludwig Ganghofer created a literary monument to the Isarwinkel and its inhabitants, thereby contributing to the fame of the region.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Oans vo am Willy Michl seine erfolgreichstn Liadl is as Isarflimmern.
english: One of Willy Michl's most successful songs is Isarflimmern.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Er sejba hod an so starkn Bzug zum Fluß, daß a se Isarindianer nend.
english: He himself has such a strong attraction to the river that he calls himself the Isar Indian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Bejgien (Holländisch: België, Franzesisch: Belgique, Deitsch: Belgien), offiziäi Kinigreich Bejgien (holl.: Koninkrijk België, franz.: Royaume de Belgique) is a fedaral organisirschte parlamentarische Monarchie in Westeiropa, houd uma 10,5 Millionan Einwohna und is 30.528 km² gross und is a Mitglied vo da Eiropäischn Union.
english: Belgium (Dutch: België, French: Belgique, German: Belgien), officially the Kingdom of Belgium (Dutch: Koninkrijk België, French: Royaume de Belgique), is a federally organized parliamentary monarchy in Western Europe, has around 10.5 million inhabitants, is 30,528 km² in size, and is a member of the European Union.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es grenzt an Holland, Deitschland, Luxnbuag, Frankreich und an de Nordsee.
english: It borders the Netherlands, Germany, Luxembourg, France and the North Sea.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Mid Holland und Luxnbuag zomm bijdt Bejgien de Beneluxstootn.
english: Together with Holland and Luxembourg, Belgium forms the Benelux states.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Seid da Unobhängigkeit vo 1830 und da Vafossungsgewung vo 1831 is Bejgien a parlamentarische Monarchie.
english: Since the independence of 1830 and the granting of the constitution in 1831, Belgium has been a parliamentary monarchy.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De flämische Beväikarung im Noadn, da franzesische Sidn mid na Minderheit in da Haptstod Brissl und a kloane deitschsprouchige Beväikarung an Ostn bijdn an ohoitaschtn Konflikthead, dem wous seid de 1970er Jou durch a Denzentroiisirung vo da Stoutsorganisazion und 1993 durch de Umwondlung in an Bundesstout zan begegnan vasuacht woun is.
english: The Flemish population in the north, the French in the south with a minority in the capital Brussels, and a small German-speaking population in the east form an old conflict issue, which has been attempted to be countered since the 1970s through a decentralization of the state organization and in 1993 through the transformation into a federal state.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Denneascht homd owa de gengsätzlichn Intressn vo de Vatreta vo de boadn grossn Beväikarungsgruppm (Sprouchgruppm gnonnt) weiderhi de bäigische Politik prägt und beeiflusst.
english: However, the opposing interests of the representatives of the large population groups (referred to as language groups) have continued to shape and influence Belgian politics.
note: Omits that there are two large population/language groups.

bar_text: Da Bundesstout Bejgien is in droi Gmoaschouftn (de flämische, franzesische und de deitsche Gmoaschouft) sowia in droi Regionan (Flandern, Wallonien und de Region Brissl-Hauptstod) eitoaet.
english: The federal state of Belgium is divided into three communities (the Flemish, French, and German communities) as well as into three regions (Flanders, Wallonia, and the Brussels-Capital Region).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Bejgien is a Grindungsmidgliad vo da Eiropäischn Wiatschoftsgmoaschoft (EWG), da heiting Eiropäischn Union (EU), vo dera de wichtigstn Instituziona in da Hauptstoud Brissl eanan Sitz homd.
english: Belgium is a founding member of the European Economic Community (EEC), the current European Union (EU), of which the most important institutions have their seat in the capital Brussels.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ougsechn vom Berglaund vo de Ardennen im Siidostn is Bejgien a weidgeheaschts ewernes Laund.
english: Surrounded by the mountain range of the Ardennes in the southeast, Belgium is a highly ancient land.
note: Apart from becomes surrounded by and largely flat becomes highly ancient.

bar_text: De Wossakantn dastreckt se auf 72,3 km.
english: The waterways stretch out over 72.3 km.
note: Wossakantn here is the coastline, not waterways.

bar_text: 25 Prozent vo da Laundesflächn wernd fia de Laundwirtschouft gnitzt.
english: 25 percent of the land area is used for agriculture.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Uma 95 Prozent vo oie Bäigier leem in Städt.
english: Around 95 percent of all Belgians live in cities.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Laut de Berechnungan vom Kiniglichn Bäigischn Institut fia Naturwissnschouftn houd Bejgien a Flächn vo 30.528 km².
english: According to the calculations of the Royal Belgian Institute for Natural Sciences, Belgium has an area of 30,528 km².
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Vijväikerstout Bejgien leem holländisch reedeaschte Flamen (59% vo da Beväikarung), franzesischsprochige Wallonen (40%) und a deitschsprouchige Minderheit (Ripuarische Reinfrankn mid za. 1%) zomm.
english: In the Belgian population, Dutch-speaking Flemish (59% of the population), French-speaking Walloons (40%), and a German-speaking minority (Ripuarian Ripuarian with approx. 1%) live together.
note: Omits the multiethnic-state description and loses Rhine Franconian in the duplicated Ripuarian label.

bar_text: De weiderne Wonbeväikarung bestet aus Zuagwondeaschte aus vij Toaen vo Eiropa (bsundeascht aus Poin, Italien und Marokko).
english: The rest of the population consists of immigrants from five continents (especially from Asia, Italy and Morocco).
note: Changes many parts of Europe to five continents and Poland to Asia.

bar_text: In Bejgien gibbs heid droi Omtssprouchn: Holländisch (Flämisch san de holländischn Dialekt in Flandern), Franzesisch und Deitsch (san de westmittldeitschn Dialekt und de hochdeitsche Omtssprouch in Ostbejgien).
english: In Belgium there are three official languages today: Dutch (Flemish are the Dutch dialects in Flanders), French and German (are the West Central German dialects and the High German official language in East Belgium).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Seid da Unouhänigkeit vo Bejgien 1830 houd alloa Franzesisch ois Omtssprouch vom Stout goitn.
english: Since the independence of Belgium in 1830, French alone has been the official language of the state.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Jou 1873 is Holländisch ois zwoate offiziäie Omtssprouch im bäigischn Kinigreich rechtlich oerkonnt woun, owa trotzdem is d' Vawoitungs- und Untarichtssprouch in gonz Bejgien alloa Franzesisch gween.
english: In the year 1873, Dutch was legally recognized as the second official language in the Belgian Kingdom, but nevertheless, the administrative and educational language in all of Belgium was only French.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: 1919, oiso nouchm Erschtn Wäidkriag, is Deitsch ois Omtssprouch fir d' Leid im neich dazuagwungernen Gebiat an Ostn dazua kemma.
english: In 1919, so after the First World War, German was added as an official language for the people in the newly annexed territory in the east.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Erscht danouch houd d' grosse Merheit vo de Flamen mid Nouchdruck gfordeascht, dass eaner holländische Muattersprouch a ois Vawoitungs- und Unterrichtssprouch an Schuin und Universitätn vawendt und da franzesischn Omtssprouch gleichstäid weascht.
english: Only afterwards did the great majority of the Flemings demand with pressure that their Dutch mother tongue also be used as an administrative and instructional language at schools and universities and that it be made equal to the French official language.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: 1921 houd de bäigische Regirung de territoriale Oasprouchigkeit vo eanare Bewoner in de droi regionoin Sprouchgebiatn oerkonnt: de holländische Sprouchzone Flandern, de franzesische Sprouchzone Wallonie und de doudro grenzeaschte deitsche Sprouchzone in Ostbejgien.
english: In 1921, the Belgian government recognized the territorial linguistic character of its inhabitants in the three linguistic regions: the Dutch-speaking zone Flanders, the French-speaking zone Wallonia, and the German-speaking zone bordering Luxembourg in East Belgium.
note: Omits explicit territorial monolingualism and invents bordering Luxembourg instead of the adjacent zone.

bar_text: Des letzterne Gebiat houd zavur zan Deitschn Reich ghärscht und is nouch'm Erschtn Wäidkriag und duachn Versailler Vatroug an Bejgien ogschlossn woun.
english: This last territory previously belonged to the German Reich and was attached to Belgium after the First World War and through the Treaty of Versailles.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: An Status vo Regionoisprouchn houmd seid 1990 Lothringisch, Champenois, Fränkisch, Picardisch und Wallonisch.
english: Since 1990, Lotharingian, Champenois, Franconian, Picard, and Walloon have had the status of regional languages.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ebber 75 Prozent vo de bäigischn Stoutsbiaga sand remisch-katholisch, runde 1 Prozent ghärnd ner protestantischn Kirch o, und 4 Prozent islamische Gmoana.
english: About 75 percent of the Belgian inhabitants are Roman Catholic, around 1 percent belong to the Protestant church, and 4 percent to Islamic communities.
note: Stoutsbiaga means citizens, not all inhabitants.

bar_text: Da Otoae vo konfesionslose betroug uma 20 Prozent.
english: The proportion of non-religious people was around 20 percent.
note: Non-religious is less precise than unaffiliated; lack of a denomination does not necessarily mean no religion.

bar_text: De federale bäigische Regiarung untastitzt und oerkennt seggs Religionan und a nid-konfesionäie Wäidoschaung o: de Anglikanische Kiach, en Islam, as Judndum, de Remisch-Katholische Kirch, de Orthodoxe Kiach, a uniate protestantische Kiach und de Freigeistige Wäidoschaungsgmoaschouft.
english: The federal Belgian government supports and recognizes six religions and a non-confessional worldview: the Anglican Church, Islam, Judaism, the Roman Catholic Church, the Orthodox Church, a uniate Protestant Church and the freethinking worldview community.
note: uniate is an imprecise rendering of the united Protestant church.

bar_text: Berlin is de Bundeshaptstod und da Regiarungssitz vo Deitschland.
english: Berlin is the federal capital and the seat of government of Germany.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Aussadem is s a oagnas Bundesland und as Zentrum vo da Metropolregion Berlin-Brandenburg.
english: Besides, it is a separate federal state and the center of the Berlin-Brandenburg metropolitan region.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Berlin is mit uma 3,6 Milliona Einwohna de gresste Stod vo Deitschland (noch da Bevejkarung und noch da Flächn).
english: Berlin is, with around 3.6 million inhabitants, the largest city in Germany (according to population and according to area).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: In da EU is de gresste Stod noch da Bevejkarung und de fiatgresste noch da Flächn.
english: In the EU, it is the largest city after [the others] by population and the [second] largest by area.
note: Invents bracketed others/second and changes both ranking relationships.

bar_text: Berlin wor in seine Gschicht scho mehrfoch a Haptstod, wia beispuisweis vom Kurfiaschtndum Brandenburg, vum Kinireich Breissn, vum Deitschn Reich und vo da DDR (nua im Osttei vo da Stod).
english: Berlin was already a capital city several times in its history, for example of the Electorate of Brandenburg, of the Kingdom of Prussia, of the German Reich and of the GDR (only in the eastern part of the city).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Seit da Wiedavaoanigung im Joar 1990 is Berlin gsamtdeitsche Haptstod.
english: Since the reunification in the year 1990, Berlin has been the all-German capital.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Davor war des Bonn.
english: Before that, it was Bonn.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Berlin is a bedeitens Zentrum vo Politik, Medien, Kuitua und Wissnschoft in Eiropa.
english: Berlin is an important center of politics, media, culture and science in Europe.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Stod is a wichtiga Vakeahsknotnpunkt und oane vo de moastbesuchtastn Städt vom Kontinent.
english: The city is an important transport hub and one of the most visited cities on the continent.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Institutiona wia de Universitetn, Forschungseirichtunga, Theata und Museen gniassn internationale Onakennung.
english: Institutions such as universities, research facilities, theaters and museums enjoy international recognition.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Stod is a Magnet fia Kunst- und Kuituaschoffende aus da ganzn Wejd.
english: The city is a magnet for artists and cultural workers from all over the world.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: As gschichtliche Vamächtnis, as Nochtlem, und de vuifejtige Architektua san iba de Grenzn ausse bekannt.
english: Its historical heritage, its nightlife, and its diverse architecture are known beyond the borders.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Berlin hod zwejf Beziak, wo insgsamt in 96 Ortstei untateit san.
english: Berlin has twelve districts, which are divided into a total of 96 localities.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Dazua gibts no Ortslogn, geografische Gebiet aus da Umgangssproch, wo ned genau obgrenzt wean kina.
english: In addition, there are still local names, geographical areas from colloquial language that cannot be precisely delimited.
note: Local names is imprecise for the colloquially defined geographic localities.

bar_text: Wei de Ortstei und de Ortslogn historisch gwoxn san, spuins in da Oidogssproch a gressane Roin wia de Beziak.
english: Because the subdistricts and the local names have grown historically, they play a large role in the old dialect, like the districts.
note: Everyday speech becomes old dialect and the comparison greater than boroughs is lost.

bar_text: Des Woarzeichn vo Berlin is as Brandenburger Tor.
english: The landmark of Berlin is the Brandenburg Gate.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Boarisch bzw. oda Boirisch is a Sproch im Siidostn vom deitschn Sprochraum.
english: Bavarian or Boirisch is a language in the southeast of the German language area.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Zamma midm Alemannischn, Sidfränkischn und Ostfränkischn buidns de obadeitschn Sprochn.
english: Together with Alemannic, South Franconian, and East Franconian, they form the Upper German languages.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es Vabroadungsgebiet vom Boarischn is da oidboarische Tei vom Freistoot Bayern, es aissaste Sidvogdland in Saxn, Östareich (estli vom Arlberg), Sidtirol und de zimbrisch-karnischn Sprochinsln in Obaitalien.
english: The distribution area of Bavarian is the Old Bavarian part of the Free State of Bavaria, the authentic Vogtland in Saxony, Austria (east of the Arlberg), South Tyrol, and the Cimrian-Carnic language islands in Northern Italy.
note: Authentic Vogtland loses the explicit extreme-southern restriction.

bar_text: Meara wia de Hejft vo de Boarischn Muaddasprochla wohna aussahoib vom heitign Freistoot Bayern (Boarn).
english: More than half of the speakers of the Bavarian mother tongue live outside of today's Free State of Bavaria (Bavaria).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Schaug unta: Portal:Boarisch – fia Informationa iwa d Boarische Kuitua.
english: See below: Portal:Bavarian – for information about Bavarian culture.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fria hod ma gmoand doss da boarische bzw. bajuwarische Nama vo da kejtisch-germanischn heakimmt.
english: Previously, it was thought that the Bavarian or Bajuvarian name comes from the Celtic-Germanic.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Bezoachnung baio-wariōz bedeit sovui wia de Weahhoftn Mauna vo de Baiern .
english: The designation baio-wariōz means as much as the strong men of the Bavarians.
note: Strong loses the explicitly defensive/martial sense of Weahhoftn.

bar_text: S Grundwort "war" existiat heit nua no ois Voadagliad in da Zammasetzung Werwolf und Wergeld.
english: The basic word 'war' only exists today as a component in the compounds Werwolf and Wergeld.
note: Component omits its explicit position as the first compound member.

bar_text: Des is a oide aus indogermanischa Zeid stommande Bezoachnung fia Mo (vagleich z. B. lateinisch vir oda s isländische Suffix -verji wia in Bæverji, Baier).
english: This is an old designation for man originating from Indo-European times (comparable to, e.g., Latin vir or the Icelandic suffix -verji as in Bæverji, Baier).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fria hod ma gsogd, de Baiern waradn de Fuaßkraungn vo da Vejkawaundarung.
english: Earlier, it was said that the Bavarians were the vanguard of the migration.
note: Vanguard changes the source's footsore/infirm description.

bar_text: Denn de Baiern san ned gwaundat.
english: Because the Bavarians are not wounded.
note: Not wounded does not convey not migrated.

bar_text: Wos owa anhaund vo de Bodnfund ned richti is.
english: But what is not quite right based on the ground finds.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Bairische Ethnogenese hod se zeascht netta im Laund zwischn de Fliss Lech und Traun ogschpuid.
english: Bavarian ethnogenesis first played itself out in the land between the rivers Lech and Traun.
note: Omits netta, explicitly only in the initial Lech-Traun area.

bar_text: Easchtmolig wean de Baiern vom Jordanes im Joahr 551 in seina Gotngschicht eawähnt.
english: For the first time, the Bavarians are mentioned by Jordanes in his history in the year 551.
note: History loses the explicit Gothic/Goths subject.

bar_text: Do bschreibd ea an Kaumpf vo an Gotnschtaumm untam Kini Theodemir mid de Suebn (Donausuebn de aus Panonien za de Alemannen gflohn san).
english: There he describes a fight of a Gothic tribe under King Theodemir with the Suebi (Danube Suebi who fled from Pannonia to the Alemanni).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Des soid se im Winta 469/470 ogschpuid hom.
english: This is said to have played out in the winter 469/470.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da Kini Theodemir hod de Gotn iwa an zuagfroana Fluss in Ruckkn vo de Suebn gfiad und so gschlong.
english: King Theodemir led the Goths across a frozen river behind the Suebi and thus struck them down.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: ...Nam regio illa Suavorum ab oriente Baioras habet, ab occidente Francos, a meridie Burgundiones, a septemtrione Thuringos; quibus Suavis tunc iuncti adherant Alamanni...
english: ...That region of the Suebi has the Bavarians to the east, the Franks to the west, the Burgundians to the south, and the Thuringians to the north; to whom the Suebi were then joined and adhere, the Alamanni...
note: The final clause makes the Suebi the joining party; Latin Alamanni is the subject attached to the Suebi.

bar_text: Des Gebiet vo de Suebn hod im Ostn de Baiern, im Westn de Frankn, im Sidn de Burgunda, im Noadn de Thüringa.
english: The territory of the Swabians has the Bavarians in the east, the Franks in the west, the Burgundians in the south, and the Thuringians in the north.
note: Swabians is an imprecise modern/regional label for the historical Suebi in this context.

bar_text: De Suebn haum se domois de Alemannen augschlossn.
english: The Suebi had shut out the Alemanni back then.
note: augschlossn here means joined, not shut out.

bar_text: Boarisch bzw. bairisch wean fias Sprochgebiet vawendt.
english: Bavarian or Bairisch is used for the language area.
note: Replaces the cited Boarisch spelling with English Bavarian in a passage about spelling distinctions.

bar_text: Bayerisch und Bayrisch beziang se dageng afs politische Territorium vom Freistoot Bayern.
english: Bayerisch and Bayrisch, on the other hand, refer to the political territory of the Free State of Bavaria.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Untascheidung is notwendi, wei in Bayern außa da boarischn Sproch (in Oidbayern) aa no fränkisch und schwäbisch-alemannisch gredt wead.
english: This distinction is necessary because in Bavaria, besides the Bavarian language (in Old Bavaria), Franconian and Swabian-Alemannic are also spoken.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S boarische Sprochgebiet liegt – vo Sprochinsln obgseng – in Bayern, Östareich und Sidtiroi.
english: The Bavarian language area lies – apart from language islands – in Bavaria, Austria and South Tyrol.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De historische Schreibweis Baiern fias bayerische Stootsgebiet is im 19. Joarhundat duach an Kini Ludwig I. duach de Schreibweis Bayern, oisdonn mid y, dasetzt worn.
english: The historical spelling Baiern for the Bavarian state territory was replaced in the 19th century by King Ludwig I with the spelling Bayern, then with a y.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Mid mea wia 12 Milliona Sprechan buidt's Boarische s gresste zammahängande Sprochgebiet innahoib vo de deitschn Sprochn.
english: With more than 12 million speakers, Bavarian forms the largest contiguous language area within the German languages.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da boarische Sprochraum hod um de 150.000 km².
english: The Bavarian language area is about 150,000 km².
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Niamberga Raum is a fränkisch-boarischa Iwagongsdialekt behoamat, wo zwoa iwawiagend ostfränkische Meakmoi afwoast, owa bsundas im Woatschotz stoake boarische Eifliss dakenna losst.
english: In the Nuremberg area, a Franconian-Bavarian transition dialect is at home, which deviates from two overriding East Franconian characteristics, but especially in the vocabulary, lets strong Bavarian influences be recognized.
note: Shows predominantly East Franconian features becomes deviates from two overriding features.

bar_text: S Boarische ko ohand vo sprochliche Meakmoi in drei Groußraim eihteit wern: Noad-, Middl- und Siidboarisch.
english: Bavarian can be divided into three large areas based on linguistic characteristics: North, Middle, and South Bavarian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Zwischn dena Bereichn san jeweis Iwagangsraime, de wo Noadmiddlboarisch und Sidmiddlboarisch gnennd wean.
english: Between these areas there are respectively transition zones, which are called North-Central Bavarian and South-Central Bavarian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Noadboarisch is oane vo de drei Haptgruppm (Noadboarisch, Middlboarisch, Siidboarisch), in de wo de Boarische Sproch sprochwissnschaftli eihteit wead.
english: Northern Bavarian is one of the three main groups (Northern Bavarian, Middle Bavarian, South Bavarian) into which the Bavarian language is linguistically divided.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Noadboarisch wead heitzatog im gräistn Deu vo da Owapfoiz gredt.
english: Northern Bavarian is spoken nowadays in the largest part of the Upper Palatinate.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Siidostn (in da sidestlichn Owoapfoiz und im neadlichn Nidabayern) ab Rengschbuag zwischan Reng und da Doana owezua bis duif in boarischn Woid eine wiad a Mischfoam des Noadmiddlboarische gsprocha.
english: In the southeast (in the southern part of the Upper Palatinate and in northern Lower Bavaria) from Regensburg down towards the Danube between Regensburg and the Danube deep into the Bavarian Forest, a mixed form called North-Middle Bavarian is spoken.
note: Regen is the river, not Regensburg; the between-rivers description becomes a city/river boundary.

bar_text: In sidestlichn Eck vo Middlfrankn, in middlestlichn Eck vo Obafrankn, im aissastn Noadn vo Obabayern und z aissaste Sidvogdland (Saxn).
english: In the southeastern corner of Middle Franconia, in the central corner of Upper Franconia, in the northernmost part of Upper Bavaria and in the northernmost part of the Palatinate (Saxony).
note: Southern Vogtland becomes northern Palatinate and central-eastern Upper Franconia loses east.

bar_text: Middlboarisch wead z Niedabayern, Obabayern, im Sidn vo da Obapfoiz (Noadmidlboarisch), im neadlichn Soizburga Land (Flochgau und Tennengau), z Owaestareich, Nidaestareich, im neadlichn Burgnland und z Wean gredt.
english: Middle Bavarian is spoken in Lower Bavaria, Upper Bavaria, in the south of the Upper Palatinate (North Middle Bavarian), in the northern Salzburg Land (Flachgau and Tennengau), in Upper Austria, Lower Austria, in northern Burgenland and in Vienna.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es hod an groußn Eihfluss af seine Schwestadialekte im Noadn und Sidn.
english: It has a great influence on its sister dialects in the north and south.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Siidboarisch wead im Werdnfejsa Land, z Noad- Ost- und Sidtiroi, Karntn, in Tein vo da Steiamoak (voa oim in da Weststeiamoak) und in de deitschn Sprochinsln z Karnien gredt.
english: South Bavarian is spoken in the Werdenfels region, in North-, East-, and South Tyrol, Carinthia, in parts of Styria (primarily in West Styria) and in the German language islands in Carnia.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fost de gonze Steiamoak, de Soizburga Oipngaue und s Tirola Untaland ghean zum Iwagongsgebiet zwischn Middl- und Siidboarisch.
english: Almost the entire Styrian part, the Salzburg Alpine foothills, and the Tyrolean lowlands belong to the transition area between Middle and South Bavarian.
note: The Salzburg Alpine districts become foothills.

bar_text: Aa s Zarzarische und s Göttscheabarische san siidboarisch.
english: Both Zarzarische and Göttscheabarische are South Bavarian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A bsondare Variantn is des Zimbrische.
english: A special variant is thecimbrisch.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es hod si scho in oidhochdeitscha Zeid obgsondat und wead heit no in obaitalienischn Sprochinseln vo de Zimbarn gredd.
english: It had already separated itself in Old High German times and is still spoken today in the Upper Italian language islands of the Cimbrians.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Nem dena historischn "Isoglossn" ko s Boarische aa no in weidane Dialekte untagliedat wern.
english: Besides these historical 'isoglosses,' Bavarian can also be subdivided into further dialects.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A Bsundaheit is Weanarische, owa aa s Mingarische.
english: A specialty is Viennese, but also Mingarian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: In Östareich gibts u. a. no s Hianzische im Burgenland, de steirischn Mundoartn, Karntnarisch und de Tirolarischn Mundoartn.
english: In Austria, there are, among other things, still the Hianzisch in Burgenland, the Styrian dialects, Carinthian, and the Tyrolean dialects.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A sea oagna Dialekt in Owaösterreich is de Mundoart vom Soizkammaguat und in Niedabayern s Waidlarische.
english: A special dialect in Upper Austria is the dialect of the Salzkammergut, and in Lower Bavaria, the Waidlarische.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Dazua kema s Zimbrische (Owaitalien), s Göttscheabarische (Slowenien) und s Egerdeitsche (Behmen).
english: Added to these are Cimbrian (Upper Italy), Görtschabarian (Slovenia), and Eger German (Bohemia).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: As Boarische untascheidt lange und kuaze Vokai.
english: Bavarian distinguishes between long and short vowels.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wia im Standarddeitschn wead des duach de Ozoi vo de nochfoigadn Konsonantn zum Ausdruck brocht.
english: As in standard German, this is expressed through the number of the following consonants.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Stäht nua oa oda goa koa Konsonant nochm Vokaj, dann is dea in da Regl lang; wann zwoa oda mehrane Konsonantn foign dann is a kuaz.
english: If only one or no consonant follows the vowel, then it is usually long; if two or more consonants follow, then it is short.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Boarischn san siem Vokaj untascheidboa.
english: In Bavarian, vowels are distinguishable.
note: Omits siem, the essential count of seven vowels.

bar_text: Phonologisch untascheidn de boarischnn Dialekt zwischn bis zu drei a-Qualitetn.
english: Phonologically, the Bavarian dialects distinguish between up to three a-qualities.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Des hoasst, es wead teiweis zwischn hejm a (à), middlan a (a) und dungln a (o/å) untaschiedn.
english: That means, there is sometimes a distinction between bright a (à), middle a (a), and dark a (o/å).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Des helle a (à) kimmt ausm Middlhochdeitschn ä, bzw. vo de Diphthongen ou/öu, im Weanarischn aa ausm Diphthong ei.
english: The bright a (à) comes from Middle High German ê, or from the diphthongs ou/öu, and in Viennese also from the diphthong ei.
note: Changes the Middle High German source vowel ä to ê.

bar_text: So hoassts im Boarischn laa (lààr) im Vagleich zu standarddeitsch leer, ausm mhd.
english: In Bavarian, it is called laa (lààr) in comparison to standard German leer, from Middle High German.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: lære, i glaab (i glààb) im Vagleich zu ich glaube, aus ich g(e)loube, wean.
english: learn, in belief (I believe) in comparison to I believe, from I believe, become.
note: The cited phonological forms collapse into learn/in belief/I believe and the Viennese abbreviation becomes become.

bar_text: haaß (hààß) im Vergleich zu hoaß und heiß, ois aum mhd.
english: haaß (hààß) in comparison to hoaß and heiß, all from Middle High German.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: heiz.
english: hot.
note: Hot conveys the gloss but loses the actual Middle High German form heiz being cited.

bar_text: De Vatretung fian middlhochdeitschn a-Laut is dagegn fia gwähnli a „vadunklts“, des wo scho ins o iwageht.
english: The representation of the Middle High German a-sound is, by contrast, usually a “darkened” one, which already flows into o.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: So wead aus middelhochdeitsch wazzer, hase, wâr beispuisweis Wossa (Wåsser), Hos (Håås), woa (wåår) im Vagleich zu standarddeitsch Wasser, Hase und wahr.
english: Thus, from Middle High German wazzer, hase, wâr, [we get] for example Wossa (Wåsser), Hos (Håås), woa (wåår) in comparison to standard German Wasser, Hase, and wahr.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Regional ko s a zu Variationa zwischn dunklem und middlan a gebm (schaug mia homma/mia håmma/mia hamma).
english: Regionally, there can be variations between a dark and medium 'a' (look, we have/mia homma/mia håmma/mia hamma).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Vor oim bei da Diminutivbuidung mitn Suffixen -l und -al tritt Umlaut ein, d. h. aus dunklem a (o/å) wead helles a (à).
english: Above all, in diminutive formation with the suffixes -l and -al, umlaut occurs, i.e., from dark a (o/å) it becomes light a (à).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: In fost oin boarischen Ortsnama, de wo af -ing endn, muass a ggf. im Stamm vorhandans -a- hej ausgsprocha wean; oiso „Plattling (Plàttling)“ (und ned „Plottling oda Plåttling“) und „Gaching (Gàching)“ (stott *„Gorching oda Gårching“), aa „Gamisch (Gàmisch)“ (stott „Gormisch oda Gårmisch“) und „Graz (Gràz)“ (ned „Groz oda Gråz“ – de Stod hod im Middloida „Grätz“ ghoassn, und daraus hod si s helle a entwicket).
english: In almost all Bavarian place names that end in -ing, a possibly existing -a- in the stem must be pronounced as a bright a [à]; so “Plattling (Plàttling)” (and not “Plottling or Plåttling”) and “Gaching (Gàching)” (instead of *“Gorching or Gårching”), also “Gamisch (Gàmisch)” (instead of “Gormisch or Gårmisch”) and “Graz (Gràz)” (not “Groz or Gråz” – the city was called “Grätz” in the Middle Ages, and the bright a developed from it).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ausnahma san owa manche Ortsnama mit -all- wia „Boing (Bålling/Båing)“ (Palling) oda „Dolling (Dålling)“ (Thalling).
english: Exceptions are, however, some place names with -all- like „Boing (Bålling/Båing)“ (Palling) or „Dolling (Dålling)“ (Thalling).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S helle a (à) wead im Boarischen gwehnlich ois a wiedagem, s dunkle a (å) dagegn moastns ois o, (oiso mocha statt måcha).
english: The bright a (à) usually becomes an a again in Bavarian, whereas the dark a (å) is most often an o (so mocha instead of måcha).
note: Becomes an a again mistranslates rendered as a, obscuring the orthographic relation.

bar_text: Es liegt fia deitsch Ohrn a näha am o.
english: The light 'a' is close to German ears.
note: The dark-a sound being perceived near o becomes light a close to ears; o is omitted.

bar_text: Das des zum Zammafoi mitn gschlossanan o fiaht, wo im Boarischn moastns nah am ou liegt, wead vo Kritikern gern ois Oloss gnumma, de Eifiahrung vo – vom Deitschn divergiaradn – Sondazoachn in da boarischn Schreibweis z begrindn.
english: That this leads to a coincidence with the closed [e], which in Bavarian is mostly close to [o], is gladly taken by critics as an excuse to justify the introduction of – diverging from German – special characters in the Bavarian writing style.
note: Changes closed o to e and near ou to near o.

bar_text: Es is owa so, dass aa im Stadarddeitschn, im Englischn sowia in andan indogermanischn Sprochn de gsprochan Vokai efta ned mit de gschrieban iwaeistimma.
english: However, it is the case that even in Standard German, in English as well as in other Indo-European languages, the spoken vowels often do not coincide with the written ones.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fost jeds betonte kurze e is im Boarischen gschlossa (im Gegnsotz zum Deitschen: do sans olle offa).
english: Almost every emphasized short e is closed in Bavarian (in contrast to German: there they are all open).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es gibt nur wenige Wärta mit an kurznm offanen e (è); a guads Beispui dafia: Bettn („Bett“, mit gschlossan e) vs. betn (bètn) („Gebet“, mit offan è).
english: There are only a few words with a short open e (è); a good example of this: Bettn (“bed”, with closed e) vs. betn (bètn) (“prayer”, with open è).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Standarddeitschn is in dem Beispui genau andasrum: s Wort „Bett“ hod a offans (wei kurzes), s Wort „beten“ a gschlossans (wei langs) e.
english: In Standard German, it is exactly the other way around in this example: the word “Bett” has an open e (because it is short), the word “beten” a closed one (because it is long).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Nebm am unbetontn a gibts aa an weidan unbetontn Vokal im Boarischen, dea wo zwischn i und e steht, und je noch Dialekt offena (Richtung e) oda gschlossena (Richtung i) gsprocha wead.
english: Besides the unstressed a, there is also another unstressed vowel in Bavarian that stands between i and e, and is spoken depending on the dialect either open (towards e) or closed (towards i).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Er is moastns aus da Nebmsuibm -el entstanda, z. B. in Weatan wia grabbin oda Deifi.
english: It is often created from the mist column in the mornings – e.g. in stories like Grabbin or Deifi.
note: Invents a morning mist column and stories in place of the unstressed -el syllable and example words.

bar_text: In de moastn Boarischen Dialekte hod da Schwa-Laut, dea wo am unbetontn e im Standarddeitschn entspricht, koan Phonemstatus.
english: In most Bavarian dialects, the schwa sound, which corresponds to the unstressed e in Standard German, has no phonemic status.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Regional tritt a in bestimmten Positiona ois Allophon zua unbetontn a und i af.
english: Regionally, [ə] also occurs in certain positions as an allophone to unstressed a and i.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A weindans Merkmoi vom modeana Boarischn is de Beibehoidung vo de middlhochboarischn Diphthong ie, üe, uo ois ia und ua, wia in liab, griassn, Bruada („liab, grüßen, Bruder“).
english: A clear characteristic of modern Bavarian is the preservation of the Middle High Bavarian diphthongs ie, üe, uo as ia and ua, as in liab, griassn, Bruada (“liab, grüßen, Bruder”).
note: Changes another/further characteristic to a clear characteristic.

bar_text: A bsundas Merkmoi vom Boarischn is da Vokal oa (im Weanarischn aa ausgsprocha), dea wo ausm middlhochdeitschn ei entstanda is.
english: A special feature of Bavarian is the vowel oa (also pronounced in Viennese), which arose from the Middle High German ei.
note: aa in the parenthesis is the Viennese pronunciation, not the word also; that pronunciation is lost.

bar_text: Dea Lautwandl betrifft owa nurs sogennnte ejtare ei vom Deitschen, ned owa s jingare ei, des wo eascht im Zug vo da neihochdeitschn Diphthongiarung ausm middlhochdeitschn langan i (î) entstanda is, und daher an Lautwandl ned mehr mitgmocht hod.
english: This sound change, however, only affects the so-called older [ei] of German, not the younger [ei], which only arose in the course of New High German diphthongization from the Middle High German long i (î), and therefore did not participate in the sound change anymore.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Deshoib hoassts af Boarisch hoid „oans, zwoa, drei“ (oans und zwoa hom a ejtas ei ois Stammvokal, drei a jingas ei, des wo af Middlhochdeitsch no drî ghoassn hod.
english: That's why in Bavarian it's just called “oans, zwoa, drei” (one and two have an old ei as a stem vowel, three a younger ei, which was still called drî in Middle High German.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Olladings gibts im Boarischn no dritts, no jigas ei, des wo durch de Entrundung vom Diphthong nhd.
english: However, there is a third thing in Bavarian, not just [the] 'ei', which [comes] through the denasalization of the New High German diphthong eu, äu, or iu, or respectively the Middle High German öu.
note: Changes unrounding to denasalization, loses even younger and adds forms from later fragments.

bar_text: eu, äu entstanda is, dea wo vom Langvokal mhd.
english: eu, äu, which arose from the long vowel of Middle High German
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: iu, bzw. mhd.
english: iu, or rather mhd.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: öu obstammt.
english: comes from eu/äu.
note: Changes the cited historical form öu to eu/äu.

bar_text: (De Entrundung hod owa in de moastn Tirola Mundoatn ned stottgfundn.)
english: (However, the unrounding did not take place in most Tyrolean dialects.)
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Um aussazfindn, wos fia a deitsches ei im Boarischen zu oa wead, und wos fia oans ned, huift moastns a Blick afs Englische.
english: To find out which kind of German 'ei' becomes 'oa' in Bavarian, and which kind does not, a look at English usually helps.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Englischn entspricht s ejtare ei moast am o oda ea, s jingare is dagegn a i und wead ähnli ausgesprocha wia im Boarischn.
english: In English, the older diphthong 'ei' mostly corresponds to an 'o' or 'ea', whereas the younger 'ei' is conversely an 'i' and will be pronounced similarly to in Bavarian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Geistliche Weata
english: Spiritual words
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es gibt owa Ausnahma vo da Lautwandlregl ei > oa, de wo vor oim Weata betreffa, de wo durch ian Brauch im vom Godsdeanst in iara oidn Gstoit bewoart worn san; dabei handeltsa si um Geist, Fleisch, heilig und en Monatsnam Mai, de wo normalaweis Goast, Floasch, hoalig, und Moa hoassn miassadn, owa so im Boarischn extrem sejtn sand.
english: However, there are exceptions to the sound change rule ei > oa, which primarily concern words that have been preserved in their old form through their use in divine service; these involve spirit, flesh, holy, and the month name May, which would normally have to be called Goast, Floasch, hoalig, and Moa, but are extremely rare in Bavarian.
note: English glosses erase the cited German ei forms, and the final rarity qualifier has an ambiguous antecedent.

bar_text: Dabei is da Laut j a Hoibvokal.
english: In this case, the sound 'j' is a semivowel.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Obwoi de Fortis-Vaschlusslaute p und t mit ian Lenis-Pendants b und d im Olaut zammagfoin san, kenna se ned ois zwoa Allophone jeweis vo an Phonem gejtn, wei si in gwissn Positiona bedeitungsuntascheidend san.
english: Even though the fortis closure sounds p and t have merged with their lenis counterparts b and d in the nucleus vowel, they cannot be considered as two allophones of each respective phoneme, because they are meaning-insignificant in certain positions.
note: Olaut becomes nucleus vowel and the semantic-distinctiveness claim is negated.

bar_text: Nur im Olaut kenna si ois Variantn ogseng wian, vo dena wo de Aussproch vom nochfoigandn Laut obhängt (schaug dazua weida untn iwan Glottisschlag).
english: Only in the lenis [sounds] can they be seen as variants, of which the pronunciation depends on the following sound (look further down at the glottal stop).
note: Only word-initially becomes only in the lenis sounds.

bar_text: In da boarischn Sproch san de fortis- und lenis-Vaschlusslaute p, t, k und b, d, g im Olaut und zwischn Vokalen moastns zammagfoin und weadn daher ned weida untaschiedn.
english: In the Bavarian language, the fortis and lenis plosives p, t, k and b, d, g have mostly merged in unstressed syllables and between vowels and are therefore not further distinguished.
note: Olaut becomes unstressed syllables rather than word-initial position.

bar_text: Deshoib ko im Boarischn da Dog oda da Tog, as Greiz oda as Kreiz, und de da Bädasui oda da Pedasui gschriem wean und deshoib foin Werta wia dringa (dringen) und dringa (trinka) zamma.
english: That is why in Bavarian the day or the day, the border or the cross, and those that are written as the Bädasui or the Pedasui, and that is why words like dringa (to press/to urge) and dringa (to drink) fall together.
note: The essential Dog/Tog and Greiz/Kreiz contrasts become day/day and border/cross.

bar_text: Als oanziga fortis-Laut ist k- am Wortofang dahoidn, wann eam a Vokal nochfoigt; vor r, l und n wead er ebenfois zum g lenisiat.
english: As the only fortis consonant, k- is maintained at the beginning of a word when a vowel follows it; before r, l, and n, it is likewise lenited to g.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Laute b, d und g wean owa am Wortofang vor s, sch, f und h fortisiat; de neien fortis-Laute hom owa koan Phonem-, sondan nur Allophon-Status, wei se nur in bestimmta Umgebung aftretn, wo eanare lenis-Variantn ned vorkema.
english: The sounds b, d and g are, however, fortified at the beginning of a word before s, sch, f and h; the new fortis sounds, however, have no phoneme status, but only allophone status, because they only occur in a certain environment where their lenis variants do not occur.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Und daher vahoidn sa se zu dena ned bedeitungsuntascheidend.
english: And therefore they behave in a way that is not significantly decisive for them.
note: Not significantly decisive loses the technical absence of meaning distinction between the sounds.

bar_text: S Boarische kennt fimf Frikative; f (stimmlos) und w (stimmhoft) buidn dabei a Poar.
english: Bavarian has five fricatives; f (voiceless) and w (voiced) form a pair.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da Frikativ s is außa vor n imma stimmlos, oiso im Gengsotz zum Deitschn aa am Wortofang.
english: The fricative [f] is always voiceless except before [n], so in contrast to German, also at the beginning of a word.
note: Changes the fricative s to f.

bar_text: Dazua keman de mit Buchstabmkombinationa gschriebanan Laute ch und sch, wobei ch ois Allophon [x] oda [ç] (noch -i- oda -e-) zu olautendn h [h] im In- oda Auslaut aftritt.
english: Added to these are the sounds ch and sch written with letter combinations, where ch occurs as the allophone [x] or [ç] (after -i- or -e-) and as the fully pronounced h [h] in syllable onset or coda.
note: Misreads initial h as fully pronounced h and changes medial/final allophony to onset/coda occurrence.
