bar_text: Da Laut ch kimmt andas ois im Standarddeitschen ned noch -n- vor, daher Minga, mank, Menk vs. stdt.
english: The sound 'ch' occurs differently than in Standard German—it does not precede '-n-'—therefore Minga, mank, Menk vs. stdt.
note: Does not occur after n becomes does not precede n, reversing the order.

bar_text: München, manch, Mönch.
english: Munich, many, monk.
note: Translates away the German ch-bearing forms that are the phonological examples; manch is also imprecisely many.

bar_text: S Boarische hod s gleiche Sonorantninventar wia s Standarddeitsche, nämli de Nasallaute m, n und ng [ŋ] sowia l, r und j. S r wead in mangn Gegandn mit da Zunganspitzn geroit, in andan Gegandn mitn Gaumenzapfal (sog. uvulares r), ohne dass des vo Boarisch-Sprechan ois Fehla empfundn wead.
english: Bavarian has the same sonorant inventory as Standard German, namely the nasal sounds m, n and ng [ŋ] as well as l, r and j. The r is produced with the tip of the tongue in many regions, in other regions with the uvula (so-called uvular r), without this being perceived as an error when speaking Bavarian.
note: Produced omits the explicitly rolled/trilled manner of r.

bar_text: Da stimmlose glottale Plosiv (Glottisschlag) tritt wia im Standarddeitschn vorm vokalischn Olaut (duatn vapflichtend) af.
english: The voiceless glottal plosive (glottal stop) occurs, as in Standard German, before a vocalic semivowel (mandatory).
note: Vowel-initial onset becomes semivowel and mandatory loses its Standard-German scope.

bar_text: Im Gengasotz dazua is des oba nur am Sotzofang oda am Ofang vo am Einschub vapflichtend: Sunstan ko ma Weata owa scho zammziagn.
english: In contrast to that, however, it is only mandatory at the beginning of a sentence or at the beginning of an insertion: But on Sunday, one can pull oneself together.
note: Otherwise contracting words becomes pulling oneself together on Sunday.

bar_text: De gsamte boarische Nominalflexion richt si am Substantiv aus.
english: The entire Bavarian nominal inflection is based on the noun.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S grammatische Gschlecht (Genus) vom Haptwort bestimmt de Deklination vo da Nominalphrasn; d. h. sowoi da Artikl ois aa s Adjektiv und andare Attribute miassn in Genus, Kasus und Numerus ans Substantiv, wo se begleitn, anglicha wean.
english: The grammatical gender (genus) of the headword determines the declension of the noun phrase; i.e., both the article as well as the adjective and other attributes must become similar to the noun they accompany in gender, case, and number.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S gibt drei Genera: maskulin, feminin und neutrum.
english: There are three genders: masculine, feminine and neuter.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ois paradigmatische Kategorien gibts de Fälle (Kasus) Nominativ, Dativ und Akkusativ sowia de Numeri Singular und Plural.
english: As paradigmatic categories, there are the cases (Kasus) nominative, dative and accusative as well as the numbers singular and plural.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Adjektive käna aa gsteigat wean.
english: Adjectives can also be inflected.
note: General adjective inflection does not specify comparison/degrees, which is the source's claim.

bar_text: Da unbstimmte Artikl is dageng fia olle drei Genera im Nominativ identisch
english: The indefinite article is, however, identical for all three genders in the nominative.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da Artikl wead im Boarischn flektiat, d. h. da Kasus wead so deitli gmochd.
english: The article is inflected in Bavarian, i.e., the case is made so distinct.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wei de moastn Substantive im Boarischn olle Kasusendunga valuan hom, wead da Kasus praktisch nur iwan Artikl ozoagt.
english: Since most nouns in Bavarian have lost all case endings, the case is practically only shown via the article.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da unbestimmte Artikl is etymologisch duach de unbetonte Aussproch vom Zoiwort "oa" entstondn (noch oidboarischa Schreibung <ain>, gsprochn /oã/).
english: The indefinite article etymologically arose through the unstressed pronunciation of the numeral 'oa' (according to Old Bavarian spelling <ain>, pronounced /oã/).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da unbestimmte Artikl wead z. B. ois /ə/, /ɐ/ o.
english: The indefinite article is, for example, pronounced as /ə/, /ɐ/.
note: The completed list omits the source's trailing or indicating further similar realizations.

bar_text: ä. ausgsprochen, im Dativ z. B. /ənə/, /ɐnɐ/ o.
english: ä. pronounced, in the dative e.g. /ənə/, /ɐnɐ/ etc.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: ä. Gschriebm wead da unbestimmte Artikl in da boarischn Dialektliteratur und heitign Umschriftn, z. B. in Internetforen, haifi ois <a>, sejten aa ois <oa>, im Dativ ois <ana>, vor oim im Dat.
english: e. In Bavarian dialect literature and today's transcriptions, e.g., in internet forums, the indefinite article is often written as <a>, sometimes also as <oa>, and in the dative as <ana>, especially in the dat.
note: Sometimes weakens sejten, rarely, for the oa spelling.

bar_text: aa ois <oana>.
english: also as <one>.
note: The cited written form oana is replaced by the English word one.

bar_text: Im Ostmiddlboarischn imma ois <a> und <ana>.
english: In East Central Bavarian, it is always <a> and <ana>.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: As Substantiv gheat im Boarischn zu de flektiaradn Woatoartn.
english: As a noun, it belongs to the inflected parts of speech in Bavarian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wia in andane germanische Sprochn is es Geschlecht (Genus) es markantaste Kriterium vom Haptwort.
english: As in other Germanic languages, gender (genus) is the most prominent criterion of the noun.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: E Boarische hod no drei vo de urspringli via germanischn Kasus: Nominativ, Dativ und Akkusativ.
english: Bavarian still has three of the original via Germanic cases: nominative, dative and accusative.
note: Leaves via untranslated and thus loses the original count of four.

bar_text: De letztn zwoa foin zum Tei zamma.
english: The last two sometimes merge.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da Genitiv is nur in a poar Redewendunga dahoidn.
english: The genitive is only preserved in a few idioms.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wia im Standarddeitschn wead es boarische Substantiv nur sejtn dekliniat, sundan druckd an Kasus durch de Artikl aus.
english: As in standard German, the Bavarian noun is not only declined in the singular, but expresses the case through the article.
note: Rarely declined becomes not only declined in the singular, inventing a number-based restriction.

bar_text: Es gibt vaschiedane Deklinationsklassn, de wo se haptsächli in da Pluralbuidung untascheidn.
english: There are different declension classes, which mainly differ in plural formation.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ois grobe Richtlinie wead zwischn da schwochn Deklination (sog. n-Klasse) und da stoarkn Deklination (sog. a-Klasse) untaschiedn.
english: As a rough guideline, a distinction is made between the weak declension (so-called n-class) and the strong declension (so-called a-class).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Schwoche Substantive endn fia gewähnlich af -n im Plural.
english: Weak nouns usually end in -n in the plural.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Vui schwoche Feminina buidn an Singular af es Suffix -n, so dass se im Plural entweda glei hoassn oda a -a ofiagn.
english: Many weak feminine nouns form a singular with the suffix -n, so that they in the plural either remain the same or end in an -a.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Bsundas de schwochn Maskulina hom im Singular a Endung fia de obliquen Kasus, d. h. fia olle Kasus aussam Nominativ.
english: Especially the weak masculines have an ending in the singular for the oblique cases, i.e., for all cases except the nominative.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Se hom moastns a -n am End.
english: They mostly have an -n at the end.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Zua Klassn vo de schwochn Substantive (W1) zejn Maskulina und Feminina af -n im Plural und aa olle Feminina mit da Pluralendung -an (de moastns im Singular af -ng endn; es -a- is dabei a sog. Sprossvokal bzw. epenthetisch).
english: The class of weak substantives (W1) includes masculines and feminines ending in -n in the plural, as well as all feminines with the plural ending -an (which most often end in -ng in the singular; the -a- is a so-called epenthetic vowel).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Driwa ausse lossa se olle Maskulina und Neutra, de wo im Singular af es Suffix -i endn, do einordna.
english: All masculines and neuters that end in the suffix -i in the singular are to be classified outside.
note: Changes additional membership of the class to classification outside it.

bar_text: Bei de stoarkn Deklinationsklassn gibts koane Kasusendungan; de oanzige Vaendarung am Woat findt bei da Numerusflexion stodd, oisdann beim Wechsel vom Singular zun Plural.
english: In the strong declension classes, there are no case endings; the only change to the word takes place during number inflection, i.e., during the change from singular to plural.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es gibt dabei vaschiedene Meglichkeitn, an Plural im Boarischn z markian.
english: There are various possibilities to mark a plural in Bavarian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Stoarke Maskulina und Neutra nutzen de Endung -a, de moast aus da middelhochdeitschen Endung -er entstandn und ois soiche im Neihochdeitschn no dahoidn is.
english: Strong masculine and neuter nouns use the ending -a, which mostly arose from the Middle High German ending -er and as such is still preserved in New High German.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es gibt oba a Weata, de wo se eascht in neia Zeit in de Klase eingreiht hom, oiso an a-Plural buidn, ohne jemois an er-Plural ghobt z hom.
english: But there are also words that only joined a class in modern times, so they form an a-plural without ever having had an er-plural.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Feminina buidn eanan Plural oft mit da Endung -an, so wias es Woat Endung sejm duat: oa Endung, zwoa Endungan.
english: Feminine nouns often form their plural with the ending -an, just as the word 'ending' does: one ending, two endings.
note: Translates the example Endung/Endungan into ending/endings, replacing the demonstrated -an plural with English -s.

bar_text: Ma ko Substantive afgrund eanara Pluralsforman in vaschiedene Klassn eintein.
english: Nouns can be classified into different classes according to their plural forms.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De haifigstn Meglichkeitn vo da Pluralbuidung san Umlaut od Suffigiarung; boade Meglichkeitn kena aa kombiniad wean.
english: The most common possibilities for plural formation are umlaut or suffixation; both possibilities can also be combined.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De do ogfiadn Beispui buidn de de Klass 1 und 2 vo de stoarkn Substantive, vo dena as Kennzeichn a Umlautplural is.
english: The examples provided here form classes 1 and 2 of the strong substantives, which are characterized by an umlaut plural.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Klass (S1) hod nebmam Umlaut koa weidas Pluralkennzoachn, is oiso endungslos; ia ghean nur Maskulina und Feminina o. Oft kimmt im Plural no a Vokalkiazung dazua, beispuisweis: Hand – Händt, Stod – Städt, Wand – Wändt, Grund – Grindt.
english: Class (S1) has no further plural markers besides the umlaut, so it is thus end-less; it only belongs to masculines and feminines. Often, a vowel shortening is also added in the plural, for example: Hand – Händt, Stod – Städt, Wand – Wändt, Grund – Grindt.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Zua Klass S2, de wo im Umlautplural plus Endung -a (de wo moastns da deitschn Endung -er entspricht) hom, ghean oanige Maskulina und vui Neutra.
english: Class S2, which has the umlaut plural plus the ending -a (which mostly corresponds to the German ending -er), includes some masculines and many neuters.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es gejten de gleichn Umlautregeln wia obm:
english: The same umlaut rules apply as above:
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Zur Klasse S3 ghean olle Maskulina, Feminina und Neutra ohne Umlaut mit Pluralendung -a; dabei endn de moastn Feminina im Singular af de urspringlige Dativendung -n.
english: Class S3 includes all masculines, feminines, and neuters without an umlaut with the plural ending -a; in doing so, most feminines end in the singular with the original dative ending -n.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ois letzte storke Klasse (S4) gejten Substantive mit Nullplural, zum Beispui ‚Fisch‘
english: As the last strong class (S4), nouns with zero plural apply, for example 'Fisch'
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: (m) und ‚Schof‘
english: (m) and 'Schof'
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: In manchen Dialektn druckn de Substantive den Plural owa durch Vokalkiazung oda -längung aus, beispuisweis da Hund und de Hundt.
english: In some dialects, nouns express the plural through vowel shortening or lengthening, for example the dog and the dogs.
note: Dog/dogs loses the actual da Hund/de Hundt forms that demonstrate the claimed vowel change.

bar_text: De Klass bstäht eigentli nur aus Maskulina und Neutra; olle Feminina af -n, de wo historisch gseng zu de schwochn Substantivn ghean, kena owa aa dazuazejt wean, wei ia Plural ebenso unmarkiat is: ‚Antn – Antn‘ „Ente“.
english: The class actually consists only of masculines and neuters; however, all feminines ending in -n, which historically belong to the weak nouns, can also be counted among them, because their plural is likewise unmarked: 'Antn – Antn' 'duck'.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Feminina wexln owa langsam zur Gruppe S3 und nehman im Plural de Endung -a o (vgl. obm s Beispui Ein „Eule“).
english: The feminine forms, however, are slowly changing to group S3 and take the ending -a in the plural (cf. the example above, an “Eule”).
note: Ein, the cited owl form, becomes an instead of preserving the noun example.

bar_text: Vuifoch wead d/ iwa de Wortgrenz wegga assimiliat (Sandhi), so hoassts moastns Nom.
english: Often, it is assimilated (Sandhi) across the word boundary, so it is mostly Nom.
note: Omits the specified assimilating sound d/.

bar_text: b Vodan und b Buam(a).
english: and the father and the boy(s).
note: Translates away the actual assimilated b Vodan/b Buam(a) forms, which are the example.

bar_text: Ebenso wia Voda flektian Baua, Boi, Breiss, Depp, Buasch [österr.], Frank, Franzos, Hiasch, Hos, Läw und andare mehr.
english: Just like Voda, Baua, Boi, Breiss, Depp, Buasch [Austrian], Frank, Franzos, Hiasch, Hos, Läw and others more inflect.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ähnli wia Bua flektian de Wärter Rob und Schwob: olle Forman außa Nominativ Singular hom an Stej vo -b an Stammauslaut -m: Rom (Robm), Schwom (Schwobm); de Pluralform Roma (Robma), Schwoma (Schwobma) san sejtn.
english: Similar to the word Bua, the words Rob and Schwob decline: all forms except the nominative singular have a change from -b to the stem consonant -m: Rom (Robm), Schwom (Schwobm); the plural forms Roma (Robma), Schwoma (Schwobma) are rare.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: As grammatische Gschlecht vo an Substantiv wead am Artikel markiat.
english: The grammatical gender of a noun is marked by the article.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Oft is as Gschlecht wia im Deitschn.
english: Often the gender is like in German.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Bei de Personalpronomina untascheidd s Boarische teiweis, so wia vui romanische und slawische Sprochn, zwischn betontn und unbetontn Foama im Dativ (nur 1.,
english: Regarding personal pronouns, Bavarian partially distinguishes, like many Romance and Slavic languages, between stressed and unstressed forms in the dative (only 1.,
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: 2. Singular) und Akkusativ (nur
english: 2. Singular) and accusative (only
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: * De Foama gejten ois „weniga“ boarisch, san dafia oba typisch ostfränggisch.
english: * These forms are considered “less” Bavarian, but are in return typically East Franconian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Bei da Kombination vo mearan unbetontn Personalpronomina, de wo af -'s verkiazt san, wead da Bindevokal -a- einegschom; bei da Reihenfoige vo da Ordnung gibts, im Gengasotz zum Deitschn, vaschiedane Variantn.
english: When combining several unstressed personal pronouns that are shortened with -'s, the connecting vowel -a- is inserted; regarding the order of the sequence, there are different variants, in contrast to German.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Dabei ko in (1.a) und (1.b) ebmso weng wia im Deitschn untaschiedn wean, obsa si bei erra um de 3. Person Singular feminin oda um de 3. Person Plural handlt.
english: In this regard, (1.a) and (1.b) can be distinguished about as much as in German, whether it concerns the 3rd person singular feminine or the 3rd person plural.
note: Loses the explicit cannot/as-little distinction and the actual ambiguous form erra.

bar_text: Aa de Possessivpronomina deina und seina flektiaen so.
english: The possessive pronouns deina and seina also inflect like this.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S Possessivpronomen (Fem. Sg.) iara is vom Standarddeitschn iwanumma woan; urspringli vawendt s Boarische fia weibliche Bsitza ebmfois s Pronomen seina.
english: The possessive pronoun (fem. sg.) iara was generally taken from Standard German; originally, Bavarian also used the pronoun seina for female owners.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Oft wead a s substantiviate Adjektiv da mei(nige) (da dei(nige), da sei(nige), im Plural: de meinign, de deinign …) vawendt: „Wem ghead der?“ – „Des is da mei!“
english: Often a substantivized adjective is used as my (yours, his, in the plural: mine, yours, his ...) : “Whom does it belong to?” – “That is mine!”
note: English glosses replace the actual mei(nige)/dei(nige)/sei(nige) and plural forms being exemplified.

bar_text: So wia de Possessivpronomina flektian de Indefinitpronomina koana sowia oana; ma ko vors Letztare s Wort iagad- stejn.
english: Just as the possessive pronouns inflect, the indefinite pronouns koana and oana do so in the same way; one can place the word iagad- before the last syllable.
note: Before the latter pronoun becomes before the last syllable.

bar_text: Do wead oiso ned zwischn de Geschlechta, sundan zwischn Persona und Socha untaschiedn.
english: Thus, a distinction is not made between the genders, but rather between person and thing.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Vui vo de boarischn Adjektive hom a Kurzfoam und a Langfoam.
english: Many of the Bavarian adjectives have a short form and a long form.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Kurzfoam wead in prädikativa Stellung vawendt.
english: The short form is used in a predicative position.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: D. h. dann, wen s Adjektiv mitm Huifsverb sein a Prädikat buidt (de Schuah san schwoaz).
english: I.e. that is, when the adjective with the auxiliary verb forms a predicate (the shoes are black).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Langfoam kimmt dann vor, wann s Adjektiv ois Attribut vo am Substantiv vawendt wead (de schwoazn Schuah).
english: The long form then occurs when the adjective is used as an attribute of a noun (the black shoes).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Moastns liegt da Untaschied zwischn Kurz- und Langfoam im Endkonsonanten.
english: Most of the time, the difference between short and long forms lies in the final consonant.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Oft san des -n, -ch, -g.
english: Often these are -n, -ch, -g.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wia im Deitschn wean Adjektive in attributiva Stejung flektiat, d. h. se griagn vaschiedne Endunga.
english: As in German, adjectives in attributive position are inflected, i.e., they receive different endings.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Dabei muass untaschiedn wean, obs mid an Substantiv mid bstimmtn Artikl gengan (und dahea sejm in bstimmta Foam flektian), oda obs mid an unbstimmtn Artikl zamm san (und nacha dementsprechend nach an unbstimmtn Musta dekliniat wean).
english: In this case, a distinction must be made whether it is with a noun with a definite article (and therefore must be inflected in a certain form), or whether it is together with an indefinite article (and is then subsequently declined according to an indefinite pattern).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wean Adjektive substantiviat vawendt, oiso nua mit Artikl, nacha richtn sa si ebnfois noch dem.
english: When adjectives are used substantively, i.e., only with an article, they also inflect accordingly.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ois Beispui deant as Adjektiv schee, des wo am Stamm bei da Flexion um -n daweitad wead (aussa beim Neutrum Singular).
english: As an example, the adjective 'schee' (beautiful) serves, which is extended by -n at the stem during inflection (except in the neuter singular).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Boarischen deant as Suffix -a zur Buidung vom Komparativ, vo da easchtn Steigarungsform.
english: In Bavarian, the suffix -a is used to form the comparative, from the first degree of comparison.
note: From misstates the relationship between comparative and first degree.

bar_text: Grundlog vom Komparativ is de obm bschriebane Langform; bei mangn Adjektivn kimts zu Umlautn, bei andan zua Vaendarung in da Vokalleng oda im konsonantischn Auslaut.
english: The basis of the comparative is the long form described above; with many adjectives it leads to umlauts, with others to a change in the vowel or in the consonantal coda.
note: Generic change in the vowel loses the source's specific length change.

bar_text: Fian Superlativ wead je nach Landschaft, a eigane Form af -st buidd oda owa aa ned.
english: For the superlative, depending on the region, a special form ending in -st is formed, or not.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: In letztan Foi wead da Komparativ ois Superlativasotz heagnumma.
english: In the last case, the comparative is taken as a superlative sentence.
note: Superlativasotz means superlative substitute/replacement, not a superlative sentence.

bar_text: So ko da Sotz „Max Müller ist der größte der zwölf Knaben“ im Boarischen foigende Varianten produzian: „Vo de zwejf Buam is da Müller Max am gressan (Komparativ)/am gresstn (Superlativ)/sejtn da gresste/da gressane.“
english: Thus the sentence “Max Müller is the greatest of the twelve boys” can produce the following variants in Bavarian: “Of the twelve boys, Müller Max is the greatest (comparative)/the greatest (superlative)/seldom the greatest/the greatest.”
note: All cited comparative/superlative forms become greatest, losing the actual morphological variants.

bar_text: Boarische Zoiweata endn moastns af -e, des wo owa in attributiva Stejung oft wegfoid.
english: Bavarian number words mostly end in -e, which often falls away in the attributive position.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Numeralia flektian ned, Ausnohm is as Zoiwoat oans fia de Zoi 1.
english: Numerals do not inflect, with the exception of the number word one for the number 1.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Boarischn is da Iwagang vo da Wortbeigung zum Sotzbau (Sidntax) oft fliaßend, desweng kena vui Bereiche in da boarischen Grammatik vo da Morphosyntax am bestn eafosst wean.
english: In Bavarian, the transition from word inflection to sentence structure (syntax) is often fluid, which is why many areas in Bavarian grammar can best be understood as morphosyntax.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Prepositiona kena im Boarischn wia im Deitschn mit am bestimmtn Artikl zu am Woat vaschmejzn (vgl. dt. bei dem = beim, an dem = am, unter den = untern usw.).
english: In Bavarian, like in German, prepositions can merge with a definite article into a single word (cf. German bei dem = beim, an dem = am, unter den = untern, etc.).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Boarisch wead des vui efta ogwendt.
english: In Bavarian, this is used much more frequently.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wei Prepositiona de Betonung af s nochfoigande Sotzelement lenka, kena eahna nua betonte, obwa nia unbetonte Peasonalpronomina foign.
english: Since prepositions direct the emphasis onto the following sentence element, they can only be stressed if no unstressed personal pronouns follow.
note: Changes which personal pronouns can follow into a condition on stressing the prepositions themselves.

bar_text: Im Boarischn wean fia Ortschaftn und Städt eascht seitm Eifluss ausm Hochdeitschn aa "nach" und "in" braucht.
english: In Bavarian, the prepositions 'nach' and 'in' have also been used for villages and towns only since the influence of High German.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Traditionej sogt ma im Boarischn owa a oda af/auf (= nach) und z (= in).
english: Traditionally, however, one also says in Bavarian 'oda af/auf' (= nach) and 'z' (= in).
note: a is the first preposition and oda means or; the output loses a and invents the quoted form oda af/auf.

bar_text: Ma foaht oisdann af Augschburg oda bleibt z Minga.
english: One then drives towards Augsburg or stays in Munich.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Bei Feiatog findt se je noch Region entweda ebmfois as z: z Ostan, z Weihnachtn; oda af: af Ostan, af Weihnachtn; oda untam Eifluss vo da Standardsproch an.
english: On holidays, depending on the region, it is either influenced by: at Easter, at Christmas; or by: on Easter, on Christmas; or under the influence of the standard language.
note: Loses the actual z/af forms and omits the third option an.

bar_text: Im Boarischn sogt ma soichane Weata owa nia nid ohne Prepositiona zua Zeitogob.
english: In Bavarian, however, such words are never used regarding a time period without prepositions.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A regionale Besonderheit is de temporale Konjunktion aft, de wo in großn Toaln vom boarischn Sprochgebiet vawendt wiad.
english: A regional peculiarity is the temporal conjunction 'aft', which is used in large parts of the Bavarian language area.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Etymologisch gseng entspricht des am englischn after und hoasst „nacha, danoch“.
english: Etymologically speaking, this corresponds to the English 'after' and means 'after, afterwards'.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: In de siidboarischn Dialekte tretn präpositionslose Orts- und Richtungsogobm (Adverbialien) af.
english: In the South Bavarian dialects, prepositionless locational and directional specifications (adverbials) occur.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ma gähd oisdann ned in de Kira oda afn Moakt, sundan ma gähd Kira/Moakt, ohne a Präposition z vawendn.
english: One doesn't go into the church or to the market then, but one goes [to] church/market, without using a preposition.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Lokalbedeitung wiad duachs Ausbleibm vom Artikl markiat, dea wo sont bei jedm Substantiv obligatorisch is.
english: Local meaning is marked by the absence of the article, which is mandatory with every noun.
note: Omits otherwise from the general article requirement, obscuring the stated exception.

bar_text: Weidane Beispui: i wohn Augschburg, i wor Schui, ea gähd easchte Klass Schui (vgl. aa lat. Romae in Rom, Romam nach Rom; Hindi Dillî calnâ af Delhi foahn, stott Dillî ko calnâ).
english: Further examples: I live [in] Augsburg, I was [at] school, he goes [to] first grade school (cf. also lat. Romae in Rome, Romam to Rome; Hindi Dillî calnâ from Delhi, instead of Dillî ko calnâ).
note: af Delhi foahn means travel to Delhi, not from Delhi.

bar_text: S Boarische hod a komplexes System vo Richtungsadverbialien, de wo oan Bezug zua Perspektivn vom Sprecha nehma.
english: Bavarian has a complex system of directional adverbials, which take reference to the perspectives of the speaker.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wia im Deitschn muass, je noch dem, ob de Bewegung vom Sprecha weg oda zum Sprecha hi voizong wiad, a ensprechends Affix ogfiagt wean (im Weanarischn san de zwoa Affixe zammagfoin, s wead do oisdann koa Untaschied mea gmocht).
english: As in German, depending on whether the movement is counted away from or towards the speaker, a corresponding affix must be attached (in Viennese, the two affixes have merged, so no distinction is made there anymore).
note: Movement counted is imprecise for movement performed/directed.

bar_text: Im Deitschn wean de Affixe ois Präfixe (hin- bzw. her-) vawendt, oisa am Adverb vorogstejt.
english: In German, the affixes are used as prefixes (hin- or her-), thus placed before the adverb.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Boarischn wean de Affixe ois Suffixe eigsetzt, d. h. am Adverb hinten ogfiagt; s Suffix -hin wead zu -i, regional -e obgschwächt, s Suffix -her zu -a.
english: In Bavarian, the affixes are used as suffixes, i.e., attached to the end of the adverb; the suffix -hin becomes -i, regionally weakened to -e, the suffix -her to -a.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Iwasicht zoagt de Richtungsadverbien, wias worscheinli im gonzn boarischn Raum iblich gwen san.
english: The overview shows the directional adverbs as they were probably common throughout the entire Bavarian region.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im westlichn Obabayern gengan de Formen scho längere Zeit ollawei mehra zruck und ma verwendt Formen de näha on da Hochsproch und näha am Schwäbischn san.
english: In western Upper Bavaria, the forms have been receding more and more for a long time, and forms are being used that are closer to the standard language and closer to Swabian.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es is dort oiso im easchtn Schritt "auffi, auffa", "obi, oba", "eini, eina", "ummi, umma" durch "nauf, rauf", "no, ro", "nei, rei", "num, rum" ersetzt worn.
english: There, in the first step, it was therefore replaced by [the forms] 'auffi, auffa', 'obi, oba', 'eini, eina', 'ummi, umma' with 'nauf, rauf', 'no, ro', 'nei, rei', 'num, rum'.
note: Replaced by old forms with new forms makes the replacement direction grammatically ambiguous.

bar_text: Wei se "no, ro" und "num", "rum" aa net so hochsprochli ohearn, wead des haintztog aa oft mit "nunta, runta" und "niba/nüba, riba/riwa/rüba" ersetzt.
english: Because [forms like] 'no, ro' and 'num', 'rum' also do not sound so high-register, nowadays they are also often replaced with 'nunta, runta' and 'niba/nüba, riba/riwa/rüba'.
note: Changes standard-language likeness to high register.

bar_text: Es gibt an broatn Stroafa wo ma "nauf, rauf"... und "auffi/auffar" … nebmanand verwendt.
english: There is a broad spectrum where one uses both 'nauf, rauf'... and 'auffi/auffar' … alongside each other.
note: The geographic broad strip becomes a broad spectrum.

bar_text: Im Sidwestn vo Oberbayern hom se de Richtungsadverbien mit da Nochsuibm "i" und "a/ar/r" bessar hoitn kenna wia im Nordwestn vo Obabayern.
english: In the southwest of Upper Bavaria, they were able to hold onto the directional adverbs with the suffix 'i' and 'a/ar/r' better than in the northwest of Upper Bavaria.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Boarischn hods an Prozess gebm, dea wo in da Sprochwissnschoft Klitisiarung hoasst.
english: In Bavarian, there has been a process that is called cliticization in linguistics.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wos Boarische betrifft, so is damit s Drohenga vo Personalpronomina ans konjugiate Verb gmoant.
english: As far as Bavarian is concerned, this refers to the dropping of personal pronouns from a conjugated verb.
note: Drohenga means attaching, not dropping pronouns from the verb.

bar_text: Aus mia wiad -ma, aus dia wiad -da, se wiad zu -s usw. Vo da Obschwechung is nacha aa nua mea a kloana Schritt zua Kontraktion vom Verb mitm Personalpronom.
english: From me becomes -ma, from you becomes -da, she becomes -s etc. After the weakening, it is then also just a small step towards the contraction of the verb with the personal pronoun.
note: Replaces the essential input forms mia/dia/se with English pronouns, losing the formal reduction examples.

bar_text: De Klitisiarung is a da Grund, weshoib s Pronoma vo da 1. Person Plural im Boarischn af m- olautet.
english: Cliticization is the reason why the 1st person plural pronoun in Bavarian ends in m.
note: af m- olautet means starts with m-, not ends in m.

bar_text: De middlhochdeitsche Verb-Endung -n und da Olaut vom Persoanalpronom wir san zum m vaschmoizn (ebenso im Schwäbischn).
english: The Middle High German verb ending -n and the umlaut of the personal pronoun wir are used to form the -m (likewise in Swabian).
note: Misidentifies wir's initial sound as an umlaut.

bar_text: m is dann vom Sprecha nimma länga ois Verb-Endung ogseng worn, sondan ois Olaut vom Personalpronom.
english: [m] is then no longer perceived by the speaker as a verb ending, but as a full vowel of the personal pronoun.
note: Changes initial consonant m into a full vowel of the pronoun.

bar_text: Des Phänomen tritt oba ned nua in da 1. Person Plural im Nominativ af, a andane Persona wean klitisiat.
english: This phenomenon does not only occur in the 1st person plural in the nominative; other persons are also cliticized.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Omeakung: De klitisiatn Personalpronoma san durch Bindestriche trennt.
english: Note: The cliticized personal pronouns are separated by hyphens.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im easchtn Beispui weads direkte Objekt (Akkusativobjekt) klitisiat, wearend im zwoatn Subjekt und Akkusativobjekt ons Verb ogfiagt wean.
english: In the first example, the direct object (accusative object) is cliticized, whereas in the second, the subject and accusative object are attached to the verb.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im drittn Beispui gengan sogoa Subjekt, Akkusativ- und Dativobjekt a Vabindung mitm Verb ein.
english: In the third example, even the subject, accusative, and dative objects form a connection with the verb.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Oba ned nua de Verbn kenna ois Element gnutzt wean, an de wo de obgschächtn Personalpronomina ogfiagt wean.
english: But not only verbs can be used as an element to which the cliticized personal pronouns are attached.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Des is aa bei Nebmsotzeinleitan mäglich.
english: This is also possible with nebulizer inhalation.
note: Nebmsotzeinleitan means subordinate-clause introducers, not nebulizer inhalation.

bar_text: Wen a Personalpronoma klitisiat worn is, dann deaf de Voifoam davo nimma im gleichn Sotz vorkema: Se schloft oda Schloft-s?
english: Once a personal pronoun has been cliticized, then the full form of it may no longer appear in the same sentence: Se schloft or Schloft-s?
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: owa nia ned Se schloft-s, des warad ungrammatisch.
english: but never ever she sleeps, that would be ungrammatical.
note: Drops the clitic -s, incorrectly presenting ordinary she sleeps as the ungrammatical example.

bar_text: A Sondafoi und a Ausnohm za dem buidd de Nominativ-Form vo da 2. Person Singular und in an grossn Tei vom Boarischn aa de 2. Person Plural, sowia ia a poa Regiona aa de 1. Person Plural.
english: A special case and an exception to this picture is the nominative form of the 2nd person singular and, in a large part of Bavarian, also the 2nd person plural, as well as in a few regions also the 1st person plural.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Do liegt nacha ned nua a Klitisiarung vor, sondan de ehemolign Klitika hom scho an Status vo ana Flexionsendung.
english: In this case, it is not just cliticization that occurs, but the former clitics already have the status of a inflectional ending.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Das du vo da 2. Person Singular is scho im Oidhochdeitschn duach inverse Sotzstellung an de urspringliche Endung -s ogfiagt worn, de wo de heite aa standardsprochliche Endung -st eagem hod.
english: The fact that 'du' is the 2nd person singular was already in Old High German, where the original ending -s was added through inverse word order, which has since been replaced by today's standard language ending -st.
note: Garbles attachment of du to -s and replaces the resulting formation of -st with a later replacement.

bar_text: Regional kena aa andane Obweichunga fiakema.
english: Regionally, other deviations can also occur.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Manche Verbn vom Boarischn erfordan a andane Rektion wia im Standarddeitschn, z. B. diaschtn („duastig sei“), drama („träumen“) und rein („bereuen“).
english: Some Bavarian verbs require a different government than in Standard German, e.g., diaschtn (“to be dusty”), drama (“to dream”) and rein (“to regret”).
note: duastig means thirsty, not dusty.

bar_text: Se wean mitm logischn Subjektiv im Dativ oda Akkusativ gnuzd (sog. Quirky Case).
english: They are used with the logical subject in the dative or accusative (so-called Quirky Case).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A formals Subjekt ist efta ned voahandn.
english: A formal subject is often not present beforehand.
note: Adds beforehand; vorhanden only means present/existing.

bar_text: Im Boarischn wean, andas wiar im Standarddeitschn, Adjektive in attributiva Stejung markiat; dazu deant s invariable Suffix -a bzw. -e; s handelt se dobei um erstoarte Nom.
english: In Bavarian, unlike in Standard German, adjectives in the attributive position are marked; for this purpose, the invariable suffix -a or -e is used; these are inflected nouns.
note: Fossilized nominative forms become inflected nouns.

bar_text: -Forman (maskulin bzw. feminin).
english: -forms (masculine or feminine).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Soichane Attribute kenna af Subjekt wia aa Objekt bezogn sei.
english: Such attributes can be related to a subject as well as an object.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Des schmeggt koida bessa.
english: Nobody tastes it better.
note: That tastes better cold becomes nobody tastes it better, changing the subject and omitting cold.

bar_text: – Das schmeckt kalt besser.
english: – That tastes better cold.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fost hedns eam lebanda eigrom.
english: They almost had him buried alive.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: – Fast hätten sie ihn lebendig eingegraben.
english: – They almost buried him alive.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Boarischn kimmt da doppetn Vanaanung a grosse Bedeitung zua.
english: In Bavarian, double negation takes on great importance.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Beispui: In da Stod huift koana neamd neda.
english: Example: In the city, no one helps anyone.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Boarischn ko a Sotz amoi oda meamois vaneint wean, da Sinn bleibt in da Regl da gleiche.
english: In Bavarian, a sentence can sometimes be negated once or mostly, but the meaning remains the same in principle.
note: Once or multiple times becomes once or mostly, confusing number of negations with frequency.

bar_text: * neamdm und neamdn san vo da Aussproch hea ned zan Untascheidn.
english: * first and last names cannot be distinguished by pronunciation.
note: The cited pronoun forms neamdm/neamdn become first and last names.

bar_text: S formale Subjekt es wiad efta elidiat, z. B. er is da gresste Depp, wo gibt.
english: The formal subject is often elided, e.g., he is the biggest idiot there is.
note: Omits the specific elided form es and translates away the example's visible Bavarian omission.

bar_text: A kloana Ibablick iba de wichtigstn Wortfejda und Meglichkeitn vo da Wortbuidung:
english: A small overview of the most important lexical fields and possibilities of word formation:
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Um dena regionaln Untaschiedn grecht zum wean, wean mange Wäate gsondat kennzeichnet: A Österreichischa Wortschotz B Oidbayrischa Wortschotz H Burgnländischa Wortschotz (Heanzisch) K Karntna Wortschotz S Steirischa Wortschotz T Tirola Wortschotz W Weana Wortschotz
english: To do justice to the regional differences, many words will be specially marked: A Austrian vocabulary B Old Bavarian vocabulary H Burgenland vocabulary (Hianzisch) K Carinthian vocabulary S Styrian vocabulary T Tyrolean vocabulary W Viennese vocabulary
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fleischa (Metzger), Tischla (Schreiner), Spangla (Klempner), Bäck (Bäcker), Zeidla (Imker), Hafna (Töpfa), Sandla (W; Obdachlosa), Striezi (W; Zuahejta)
english: Butcher (Metzger), carpenter (Schreiner), plumber (Klempner), baker (Bäcker), beekeeper (Imker), potter (Töpfer), homeless person (W; Obdachloser), outsider (W; Zugehörter)
note: Replaces Bavarian words with English and misrenders the pimp item as outsider/Zugehorter.

bar_text: S Boarische hod oft a Vuizoi vo ausdrucksstoarkn Begriff fia a Soch.
english: Bavarian often has a multitude of expressive terms for a thing.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fia Mund gibts zum Beispui Mai (ugs.), Goschn (frech) oda Goschal (liabevoi), Babbn (frech), Lätschn (obweatend) oda Fotzn (beleidigend).
english: For mouth, there are, for example, Mai (colloquial), Goschn (cheeky) or Goschal (full of love), Babbn (cheeky), Lätschn (disrespectful) or Fotzn (insulting).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A fias Gwand gibts an Hafa typisch boarische Ausdrick: Gwand sejm,Joppn („Jackn“), Pfoidl oda Pfoadl (fia Hemad), Diandl z. B.
english: For clothing, there is a wealth of typical Bavarian expressions: Gwand (clothing), Joppn (“jacket”), Pfoidl or Pfoadl (for shirts), Diandl, for example.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fia d Viecha gibt aa an bsondan boarischn Woatschotz, z. B. Giggal (Hahn), Bibbal oda Ziwarl (kloans Hendl), Heiß(al) (jungs Pferd, Foihn), Goaß, Hebbal (junge Goaß), For(n) (Jungstia, Stiakaibe), Böichn (ahd. belihha; Blässhendl), da Imp oda de Impn (Biene), Oachkatzl, Brotz (lat. Loanwoat, Grod), Hotz (Eichlhäha) usw.
english: For animals, there is also a special Bavarian vocabulary, e.g., Giggal (rooster), Bibbal or Ziwarl (small chicken), Heiß(al) (young horse, foal), Goaß (goat), Hebbal (young goat), For(n) (young animal, male deer), Böichn (Old High German belihha; speckled chicken), da Imp or de Impn (bee), Oachkatzl (squirrel), Brotz (Latin loanword, Grod), Hotz (squirrel) etc.
note: Young bull becomes deer, coot becomes speckled chicken, jay becomes squirrel, and Grod/toad is not translated.

bar_text: Zum boarischn Vokabulaa im Bereich vo de Lebmsmiddl schaug: Austro-Boarischa Kuchlwoatschotz.
english: For Bavarian vocabulary in the area of food, see: Austro-Bavarian kitchen vocabulary.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Des produktivste Suffix zua Buidung vo Adjektiven is -ad; des gehd entweda afs Suffix -ert zruck, oda afs Suffix -end, dees wo eigentli zur Buidung vom Partizip Präsens vawendt wiad (boade Suffixe san im Boarischen lautli zammagfoin).
english: The most productive suffix for the formation of adjectives is -ad; this either goes back to the suffix -ert, or to the suffix -end, which is actually used for the formation of the present participle (both suffixes have merged phonetically in Bavarian).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Stammendunga in Klamman (moast -g oda -ch) wean im traditionejn Boarisch nur gsogt, wens Adjektiv flektiat wead und daduach a vokalische Endung dahoit.
english: Derivations in parentheses (mostly -g or -ch) are only used in traditional Bavarian when the adjective is inflected and thereby maintains a vocalic ending.
note: Stem endings become derivations, and only pronounced becomes only used, confusing sound realization with general occurrence.

bar_text: Es gibt owa aa regionale und lokale Ausnohma.
english: However, there are also regional and local exceptions.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: 12:15 – Viadl noch zwejfe (sejtana: Viadl iwa zwejfe); weanarisch, nordobaboarisch : Viadl aans
english: 12:15 – Quarter to twelve (seldom: Quarter past twelve); Viennese, North Upper Bavarian: Quarter one
note: Quarter to twelve contradicts the 12:15 value and quarter-past expression.

bar_text: 12:30 – hoibe/a oans
english: 12:30 – half past twelve/half one
note: Half past twelve is correct, but the alternative half one conventionally means 1:30 in English.

bar_text: 12:45 – Dreiviadl oans/Viadl vor oans, sejten: Viadl af oans
english: 12:45 – Three quarters one/Quarter to one, rarely: Quarter to one
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Bei voin Stundn, ob viar kimmt imma no a -e dazua:
english: For full hours, even four, an -e is always added:
note: Starting at four becomes even four, changing the rule's scope.

bar_text: 16:00 – viare
english: 16:00 – four o'clock
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: 16:30 – hoibe fimfe
english: 16:30 – half past four
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wia im engl.
english: As in English.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Sprochraum wead in Bayern des 12 h Format vawendd:
english: The 12-hour format is used in the Bavarian language area:
note: Widens the source's Bavaria to the whole Bavarian language area.

bar_text: 14:30 – hoibe drei (am Nammidog)
english: 14:30 – half three (in the afternoon)
note: Half three conventionally means 3:30 in English, not 14:30.

bar_text: De boarischn Wochadogsnama, de wo vom Standarddeitschn etymologisch obweicha (oiso da Deansdog und da Dunnasdog), stamma ausn Einflussbereich vo da Gotischn Sproch.
english: The Bavarian names of the weekdays, which etymologically deviate from Standard German (namely Deansdog and Dunnasdog), stem from the sphere of influence of the Gothic language.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Fir Details schaug: De boarische Wocha
english: For details look: The Bavarian Week
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Es gibt zwoa aa im Standarddeitschn verbale Prefixe, im Boarischn san de owa vui produktiva.
english: There are also two verbal prefixes in standard German, but in Bavarian they are much more productive.
note: Misreads the concessive zwoa ... owa as two verbal prefixes.

bar_text: da- (< der-) entspricht am standarddeitschn er-, kimmt owa a mit Verben voa, de wo im Hochdeitsch des Präfix ned hom kena.
english: da- (< der-) corresponds to the standard German er-, but also occurs with verbs that did not have the prefix in High German.
note: Did not have weakens the source's cannot have restriction.

bar_text: zamm (zamma) [com-] entspricht am Standarddeitschn zusammen-, es wead no haifiga vawendt ois dees.
english: zamm (zamma) [com-] corresponds to the Standard German zusammen-, it is used even more frequently than that.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S Boarische hod regional vaschiedane Diminutivsuffixe, vo dena -l, -e und -al (< -erl) de haifgstn san.
english: Bavarian has regionally different diminutive suffixes, of which -l, -e and -al (< -erl) are the most common.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Des -l is sogoa stoark lexikalisiat, d. h. s wiad oft gor nimma ois Diminutiv vastandn.
english: The -l is even strongly lexicalized, i.e., it is often no longer understood as a diminutive.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Vui vo de Diminutive ohne a Grundwort beziang se oft af Meschn, deo wo oan af irenoa Oat load doa.
english: Many of the diminutives without a base word often refer to people who behave in their own particular way.
note: Omits that the people evoke pity; behaving in their own way is not leid tun.

bar_text: Im Berchtesgoana Land, Cheamgau, Toaln vom Soizburga Land, Soizkammaguad und vom Bayrischn Oberland sowia aa im Tirola Untaland und im steirischn Tauerngebiet is des Diminutivsuffix moast ned -(a)l, sondern -ei.
english: In the Berchtesgaden area, Chiemgau, the valleys of the Salzburg area, Salzkammergut and the Bavarian Upper Land, as well as in the Tyrolean Lowland and the Styrian Tauern region, the diminutive suffix is mostly not -(a)l, but -ei.
note: Parts of the named areas become their valleys.

bar_text: Da Hiasl wiad dann zum Hiasei.
english: Hiasl then becomes a Hiasei.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Andane Beispui: Dirnei fia Madl, Hansei fia Hansl usw.
english: Other examples: Dirnei for girls, Hansei for Hansl, etc.

english: Together with Sundays, holidays are treated as “days of rest from work and of spiritual improvement”.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Gsamtwiatschaftsleistung in Deitschland wead duach eppa 2,1 % im primean Sektor (Landwiatschaft), 24,4 % im sekundean Sektor (Industrie) und 73,5 % im tertiean (Deanstleistung) Wiatschaftssektor eazuit.
english: The total economic output in Germany is distributed as approximately 2.1% in the primary sector (agriculture), 24.4% in the secondary sector (industry), and 73.5% in the tertiary (service) economic sector.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Ois hochentwicklts Industrieland is Deitschland af wejdweite Rohstoffimporte ogwiesen.
english: As a highly developed industrial country, Germany is dependent on global raw material imports.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Eiropäische Union (amtl: Europäische Union, obkiazt: EU) is a Staatnbund, dea wo aus 27 eiropäischn Staaten bestäht.
english: The European Union (official: European Union, abbreviated: EU) is a union of states that consists of 27 European states.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Beväikarung in dena EU-Ländan umfosst deazeit rund a hoiwe Milliardn Einwohna.
english: The population in the EU countries currently comprises around half a billion inhabitants.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Gmoasam eawirtschafdn de Mitgliedstaaten im eiropäischn Binnenmoakt s gresste Bruttoinlandsprodukt vo da Wäid.
english: Collectively, the member states in the European single market have the largest gross domestic product in the world.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Gengwäatig grindt se s politische System vo da EU afan am 1. Novemba 1993 in Kroft tretanan Vatrog iwa de Eiropäische Union, dea wos zletzt im Joa 2001 durch an Vatrag vo Nizza gändat woan is.
english: Currently, the political system of the EU is based on the Treaty on European Union, which came into force on November 1, 1993, and was last changed in the year 2001 by the Treaty of Nice.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Aufm EU-Vatrog basian de sognenntn drei Säuln vom Staatnvabund: Eiropäische Gmoaschoftn (EG), Gmoasame Außen- und Sicherheitspolitik (GASP) sowia Polizeiliche und justizielle Zammaorbat in Strofsocha (PJZS).
english: The so-called three pillars of the state union are based on the EU Treaty: European Communities (EC), Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) as well as Police and Judicial Cooperation in Criminal Matters (PJCCM).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Noch mehran Erweidarungsrundn stähd da Staatnvabund deazeit voa interna Struktuaproblema.
english: Following more rounds of enlargement, the state union is currently facing internal structural problems.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da Eiropäische Rat hod dahea am 13. Dezemba 2007 a Vatrog vo Lissabon untazeichnet.
english: The European Council signed a Treaty of Lisbon there on 13 December 2007.
note: Changes the causal therefore to locative there.

bar_text: De Ratifiziarung in dena Mitgliedstaatn soi bis Mitte 2009 obgeschlossn sei; olladings is dea Zeitplan durch de Oblehnung vom Vatrog in am Referendum in Irland im Juni 2008 in Frog gstäit.
english: Ratification in the member states is to be completed by mid-2009; however, the schedule is called into question by the rejection of the treaty in a referendum in Ireland in June 2008.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Eiropäische Union hod a Flächn vo 4.324.782 km² und a Küstnläng vo 65.413,9 km.
english: The European Union has an area of 4,324,782 km² and a coastline length of 65,413.9 km.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Sie reicht im Nordostn bis Finnland, im Nordwestn bis Irland, im Siidostn bis Zypern und im Sidwestn bis Portugal.
english: It reaches in the northeast as far as Finland, in the northwest as far as Ireland, in the southeast as far as Cyprus and in the southwest as far as Portugal.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Olle Stootn (mid da Ausnahm vo de Iwaseeterritorien und Zypern) lieng in Eiropa.
english: All states (with the exception of the overseas territories and Cyprus) lie in Europe.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: 2004 is mid Zypern aa a Stoot aufgnumma worn, der geografisch zu Asien zöid wead.
english: In 2004, Cyprus was also admitted as a state, which is geographically counted as part of Asia.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De gsamte Eiropäische Union (ohne de Aussnterritorien) liengan auf da Eirasischn Plottn.
english: The entire European Union (without the overseas territories) lies on the Eurasian plate.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da geografische Mittlpunkt ve da Eiropäischn Union is Kleinmaischeid im Westerwald in Deitschland.
english: The geographical center of the European Union is Kleinmaischeid in the Westerwald in Germany.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da Mont Blanc liegt in de Savoya Oipm und is mid 4808 m da hächsde Berg vo da EU.
english: Mont Blanc is located in the Savoy Alps and is the highest mountain in the EU, at 4,808 m.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da gresste See ist da Väna Sää, a Binnensee im Sidwestn vo Schwedn mid ana Flächn vo 5650 km².
english: The largest lake is Lake Vänern, an inland lake in the southwest of Sweden with an area of 5,650 km².
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da längste Fluss is de Donau mid 2850 km, vo dera owa nur 1627 km die EU durchfliassn.
english: The longest river is the Danube with 2,850 km, of which however only 1,627 km flow through the EU.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Sie entspringt im Schworzwoid und mündt im Donaudäita ins Schwoaz Meer.
english: It rises in the Black Forest and flows into the Danube Delta into the Black Sea.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: S Klima reichd im Noadn vom koidn Klima bis zum subtropischm Klima im Sidn.
english: The climate ranges from the cold climate in the north to the subtropical climate in the south.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Im Noadn (Finnland) lieng de Durchschnittstemparatuan bei -13 °C im Winta und +15 °C im Summa.
english: In the north (Finland), the average temperatures lie at -13 °C in winter and +15 °C in summer.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Dageeng wead im Sidn (Malta) im Winta a durchschnittliche Temparatua vo +12 °C und im Summa vo +25 °C darreicht.
english: In contrast, in the south (Malta), an average temperature of +12 °C is reached in winter and +25 °C in summer.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: A jede Sproch, de in am Mitgliedsstoot primäre Aumtssproch is, guit im Eiropäischn Parlament und ba da Kommission ols Aumtssproch.
english: Every language that is a primary official language in a member state is valid in the European Parliament and at the Commission as an official language.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: So hot zum Beispui a jeda Obgeordnete und jede Obgeordnetin im Eiropaparlament des Recht, dass er oda sie in seiner oda ihra Hoamatsproch Redn holtn kou und a a Iwasetzung va die onnan kriagt.
english: For example, every Member and every Member of the European Parliament has the right to give speeches in his or her home language and also to receive interpretation from the others.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Des hot oan damols festglegt ols Zeichn, dass die Sprochn ols Kuitua va die Vöiker olle gleich vui wert sei sulln.
english: This was once established as a sign that the languages, as a culture of the peoples, should all be worth just as much.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Heit iwalegt oan awa scho, ob oan de Regelung in Zukunft holtn kou.
english: Today, one is already wondering whether one can maintain the regulation in the future.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Bsundas jetz, wo Rumänien und Bulgarien dazua kemm san und wo a Minderheitnsprochn wia de vo die Roma onerkounnt weadn sull, is as Problem, dass oan nocha völli mehr Iwasetzer ols wia Obgeordnete hot, walst jo fia jede Sproch mindestns so vui Iwasetza brauchst, wie onnare Sprochn san.
english: Especially now, where Romania and Bulgaria have joined and where a minority language like that of the Roma should be recognized, the problem is that one has completely even more interpreters than deputies, because you need at least as many interpreters for every language as there are other languages.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Frankreich (franzesisch: France, amtli: République française) is a demokratischa, zentralistischa Stoot im Westn vo Eiropa.
english: France (French: France, official: République française) is a democratic, centralized state in western Europe.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Haptstod is Paris.
english: The capital is Paris.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: In Eiropa grenzt Frankreich on Bejgien, Luxnbuag, Deitschland, de Schweiz, Italien, Monaco, Spanien, Andorra, on de Nordsee, onan Atlantik mitm Ärmekanei und ans Middlmeea.
english: In Europe, France borders Belgium, Luxembourg, Germany, Switzerland, Italy, Monaco, Spain, Andorra, and the North Sea, the Atlantic with the English Channel, and the Mediterranean Sea.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Insgsomt hods „franzäsische Muaddaland“ in Eiropa Flächn vo 543.965 km².
english: In total, the “French motherland” in Europe has an area of 543,965 km².
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Weng seina Foam weads aa l’Hexagone (Sechseck) gnennd.
english: Because of its shape, it is also called l’Hexagone (the hexagon).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Da häxte Beag vo Frankreich und vo de Oipn is d Mont Blanc (4.810 Meta).
english: The highest mountain in France and in the Alps is Mont Blanc (4,810 metres).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De mid Obstond wichtigste und gräßte Stod is de Haptstod Paris mid rund zwejf Milliona Eihwohna in da Agglomeration (Region Île-de-France) (2013).
english: The most important and largest city in terms of distance is the capital Paris with around twelve million inhabitants in the agglomeration (Île-de-France region) (2013).
note: mit Obstond means by far, not ranking the city in terms of distance.

bar_text: De Groußraime um Marseille, Lille und Lyon hom aa mehra wia a Million Eihwohna.
english: The metropolitan areas around Marseille, Lille and Lyon also have more than a million inhabitants.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Obwois Gebiet vom heitign Frankreich scho in da remischn und in da fränggischn Gschicht voakimmt, beginnt de eignständige franzesische Gschicht eascht mid da Afteilung vom Reich vom Karl am Großn zwischn dena Enkln mitm Vatrog vo Verdun im Joar 843.
english: Even though the area of today's France already appears in Roman and Frankish history, independent French history only begins with the division of the empire of Charlemagne among his grandsons with the Treaty of Verdun in the year 843.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Mit da Franzesischn Revolution 1789 is as Ancien Régime gstiazt woan, des wo 1200 Joa gheascht hod.
english: With the French Revolution in 1789, the Ancien Régime that had lasted for 1,200 years fell.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Nacha is a Umbruch-Periodn kema, wo wexlnd republikanische, napoleonisch-imperiale und monarchistische Stootsformen gheascht hom.
english: Afterwards, a period of upheaval came, in which changing republican, Napoleonic-imperial, and monarchist forms of state existed.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Napoléon hod grouße Tei vo Eiropa beheascht.
english: Napoleon ruled a large part of Europe.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Mit seina Niedalog san de moastn Eaobarunga wieda valoan woan.
english: With his defeat, most of the conquests were lost again.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Noch da Restauration vo da Monarchie hod Frankreich sei Mocht owa wieda ausbaut, hod weidane Kolonien eaobat und hodn Ospruch afs gsomte Rhein-Westufa eahom.
english: After the restoration of the monarchy, France rebuilt its power again, conquered further colonies, and laid claim to the whole of Rhineland-Westphalia.
note: The entire western bank of the Rhine becomes Rhineland-Westphalia, a different territory.

bar_text: In Frankreich gibts a Buidungspflichd owa koa Schuipflicht.
english: In France there is compulsory education but no compulsory schooling.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Des hoaßt de Buidung ko ma si aa duach Hausuntaricht oda duach sejm lerna beibringa.
english: This means that one can also teach oneself education through homeschooling or by learning on one's own.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Frankreich untahoit Natuaschutzgebiet in vaschiedanen Kategorien im eiropäischn Kernland und in de Iwasää-Départements.
english: France contains nature protection areas in various categories in the European heartland and in the overseas departments.
note: Contains loses the active maintains/manages relation.

bar_text: Weidane Natuaschutzgebiet san in Planung und Voabereitung.
english: Further nature reserves are in planning and preparation.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Geografie is de Wissnschoft vo da Erdobaflächn, vom Roum und Oat vo da Eadn im ojgemeinen und a vo da Beschoffnheid da Eadn söbsd.
english: Geography is the science of the Earth's surface, of the space and nature of the Earth in general and also of the composition of the Earth itself.
note: Oat means place, not nature; the space-and-place distinction is lost.

bar_text: Se eafosd, bschreibd und eakläat de Struktuan und de Vuagäng ouf da Eadobaflächn und emfois de Auswiakungen ouffn Menschn und de Hondlungen vo d'Menschn.
english: It explores, describes, and explains the structures and the processes on the Earth's surface and also the effects on humans and the actions of humans.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: De Geografie buidt de Bruggn zwischn de oanzelnen Natua- und Sozjoiwissnschofftn.
english: Geography builds the bridge between the individual natural and social sciences.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Se enwtickit de Konzepte zua Vaständnis und zua Löösung vo de Probleme zwischn da Wöd und' Menschn.
english: It develops concepts for the understanding and for the solution of the problems between the world and humans.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Gegnstond vo da Geografie is de gsommte Geosfäre.
english: The subject of geography is the entire geosphere.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Vorlage:Infobox Fluss/NACHWEISE_ausVorlage:Infobox Fluss/Veraltet
english: The planning and implementation was the responsibility of the Regional Office for Water Management and the city of Munich. Embankments were removed and the river bed was widened, establishing connections to surrounding flood plains.
note: The source is a residual infobox/template identifier rather than an interpretable prose translation unit.

bar_text: De Isar is a Fluss, der wo vo de Oipn durch Minga fliaßt und letzendlich gengiba vo Degndorf in d Donau münden duat.
english: The Isar river enters Germany near Mittenwald and flows through Krün, Wallgau, Bad Tölz, Munich, and Landshut, before entering the Danube near Deggendorf.
note: Omits the Alps and adds a detailed route through other towns.

bar_text: Da Ursprung liagt in Estareich im Hinteraudoi vom Kawendl-Gebirg.
english: Its source is in the Karwendel mountain range of the Alps.
note: Omits Austria and the Hinterautal location.

bar_text: Zwischn Scharnitz und Mittnwoid fliaßts iaba d' Grenz vo Estareich noch Bayern (Deitschland).
english: The Isar river enters Germany near Mittenwald and flows through Krün, Wallgau, Bad Tölz, Munich, and Landshut, before entering the Danube near Deggendorf.
note: Omits Austria, Bavaria and Scharnitz and adds the subsequent route to the Danube.

bar_text: Se hod a Leng vo 295 Kilometa.
english: It is located some 12 km south of Lenggries.
note: A location south of Lenggries does not convey the source's 295 km length.

bar_text: Neba Minga liang de Städt Däiz, Freising, Moosburg und Landshuad an da Isar.
english: The Isar river enters Germany near Mittenwald and flows through Krün, Wallgau, Bad Tölz, Munich, and Landshut, before entering the Danube near Deggendorf.
note: Omits Freising and Moosburg and adds other towns and the Germany-to-Danube route.

bar_text: De greaßtn Zufliass han d' Amper bei Moosburg, d' Loisach bei Wolfratshausn und d' Moosach bei Freising.
english: The Isar river flows through a sub-alpine, glacial morainic landscape towards Wolfratshausen.
note: The landscape-route statement conveys none of the tributary identifications.

bar_text: D' Isar is noch da Donau, am Inn und am Main da viertlängste Fluss in Bayern.
english: The Isar (pronounced [ˈiːzaʁ] ⓘ) is a river in Austria and in Bavaria, Germany. Its source is in the Karwendel mountain range of the Alps.
note: Retains the river and Bavaria but omits the entire fourth-longest ranking and comparands.

bar_text: Lange Zeit hods ghoaßn, der Nama Isar dad ausm keltischn kemma und sovui wia reißnds Wossa (ys = schnej, reißnd und ura = Wossa, Fluss) bedeitn.
english: Following their executions on October 16, 1946, there were unconfirmed reports that the ashes of the convicted Nazi war criminals Joachim von Ribbentrop, Hans Frank, Wilhelm Keitel, Alfred Jodl, Alfred Rosenberg, Ernst Kaltenbrunner, Wilhelm Frick, Arthur Seyss-Inquart, Fritz Sauckel, and Julius Streicher were scattered in the Isar, as were those of Hermann Göring who had committed suicide the previous night in defiance of his scheduled execution.
note: The war-criminal ashes account conveys none of the name-etymology statement.

bar_text: Des guid inzwischn ois vaaltate Meinung.
english: At Bad Tölz, the Isar leaves the Bavarian Alps.
note: Leaving the Alps at Bad Tölz does not convey that the previous etymological opinion is outdated.

bar_text: D'Sprachforscher moana jetzad es dad vo da indogermanischn Wurzl es/is (fia fließnds Wossa) kemma, de se a in fui andane Flußnama wiadafindt und se in aktuelle Sprachn nua no aufs feste Wossa, oiso s Eis bziagt.
english: One theory is that the name Isar stems from *es or *is in the Indo-European languages, meaning "flowing water", and later turned into a word with a meaning narrowed to frozen water (hence English ice, German: Eis) in Proto-Germanic. The name itself is mentioned for the first time in 763 as Isura.
note: Omits other river names/current-language wording and adds Proto-Germanic examples and a first-attestation date.

bar_text: A guads Drum vom Wossa des auf'd boarischn Oipn unds Kawendl foid fliaßt durch d' Isar zur Donau und so bis ins Schwoazze Meea.
english: Passing Landshut, the river makes its way through the Tertiary Hills of Lower Bavaria all the way into the Danube river. The Isar river descends some 848m to flow into the Danube, about five kilometres away from Deggendorf.
note: Only the Isar-to-Danube connection overlaps; Alpine precipitation and the Black Sea are missing, with route/elevation facts added.

bar_text: S' gsamte Einzugsgebiat hod a Flächn vo 9000 Quadratkilometa.
english: The drainage basin contains some 9,000 square kilometers (roughly 3,500 square miles).
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Wei a Guads vom Niedaschlog in de Berg ois Schnee foid hods zur Schneeschmelz as meiste Wossa.
english: During the winter, most of the precipitation in the Alps turns into snow. The snowmelt can result in an increased water flow down the Isar rivers during the spring meltdown.
note: Weakens the snowmelt peak to a possible increase and adds winter/spring timing and a most-precipitation claim.

bar_text: Mit am mittlern Abfluss vo 175 Kubikmeta in da Sekund zählt d' Isar zu de mittlgroßn deitschn Flüss.
english: With 295 km (183 mi) length, it is among the longest rivers in Bavaria, and it is Germany's second most important tributary of the Danube.
note: Length/importance claims replace the 175 cubic metres per second discharge and medium-sized classification.

bar_text: Ma kos sogseng mit am Lech, da Mosel, am Main und am Neckar vagleicha.
english: The Isar river enters Germany near Mittenwald and flows through Krün, Wallgau, Bad Tölz, Munich, and Landshut, before entering the Danube near Deggendorf.
note: The route through towns does not convey comparison with Lech, Moselle, Main and Neckar.

bar_text: Da Ursprung vo da Isar liagt im Hinteraudoi im Karwendl auf 1.160 Meta iaba Normalnui ( Koordinaten fehlen! Hilf mit. ...).
english: The official source of the Isar is located in the Hinterau valley east of the village Scharnitz in the Karwendel mountains at 1160m above sea level. The Lavatschbach is the Isar's longest headstream.
note: Adds Scharnitz-relative location and the longest-headstream claim, omitting the editor note.

bar_text: Do fliaßt da Lafatsch an de Isarquelln vorbei.
english: Just north of the town the Loisach flows into the Isar.
note: Describes the Loisach joining the Isar, not Lafatsch passing the Isar springs.

bar_text: Da Lafatsch hod sei Quelln in da Nach vom Hallerangerhaus.
english: The Lavatschbach is the Isar's longest headstream.
note: Longest headstream does not convey that its source is near the Hallerangerhaus.

bar_text: Er is da längste vo de Quellbäch.
english: The Lavatschbach is the Isar's longest headstream.
note: All substantive source claims preserved.

bar_text: Sei Nama ändert se bei de Isarquelln in Isar, oafach wei de Quelln vui mehra Wassa bringa, ois ea sejba hod.
english: Following their executions on October 16, 1946, there were unconfirmed reports that the ashes of the convicted Nazi war criminals Joachim von Ribbentrop, Hans Frank, Wilhelm Keitel, Alfred Jodl, Alfred Rosenberg, Ernst Kaltenbrunner, Wilhelm Frick, Arthur Seyss-Inquart, Fritz Sauckel, and Julius Streicher were scattered in the Isar, as were those of Hermann Göring who had committed suicide the previous night in defiance of his scheduled execution.
note: The ashes account conveys none of the name change or water-volume explanation.

bar_text: In de Berg han ois wichtige Nebnflüß da Rißbach, d' Achn und d'Jachn zum dawähna.
english: Its source is in the Karwendel mountain range of the Alps. The Isar river enters Germany near Mittenwald and flows through Krün, Wallgau, Bad Tölz, Munich, and Landshut, before entering the Danube near Deggendorf.
note: The source and route account omits the named mountain tributaries.

bar_text: Da Rißbach kimmt aus da Eng und trifft bei Vorderriß auf d' Isar.
english: Just north of the town the Loisach flows into the Isar.
note: Names Loisach rather than Rissbach and omits Eng and Vorderriss.

bar_text: D'Achn kimmt vom Achensee und mündt in Sylvensteinsee, dem sei Zua- und Abfluß d' Isar is.
english: The Isar (pronounced [ˈiːzaʁ] ⓘ) is a river in Austria and in Bavaria, Germany. Its source is in the Karwendel mountain range of the Alps.
note: General Isar origin/location facts omit the Ache and both lake-flow relationships.

bar_text: D'Jachn kimmt vom Walchasee, fliaßt durch d' Jachenau und mündt in da Nach vo Fleck und Wegscheid.
english: The Isar river enters Germany near Mittenwald and flows through Krün, Wallgau, Bad Tölz, Munich, and Landshut, before entering the Danube near Deggendorf.
note: The general Isar route does not convey the Jachen's Walchensee origin, Jachenau course and mouth.

bar_text: De wichtigstn Nebenflüß außahoib vo de Berg han d' Amper und d' Loisach.
english: The Isar river drains a substantial part of the Bavarian Alps and parts of the Karwendel mountains.
note: Alpine drainage area does not identify Amper and Loisach as the principal tributaries outside the mountains.

bar_text: De meistn Inseln und Kiesbänk in da Isar untaliegn wega de starkn Hochwassa a ständign Änderung in ihra Form und Log.
english: Some of the Isar waters are channeled via the Rißbach into the Walchensee, the Rißbach flow direction having been reversed. The Isar water flows into the giant downpipes of the Walchensee Hydroelectric Power Station.
note: Diversions and power-station pipes do not convey flood-driven island/gravel-bank changes.

bar_text: D'Isar werd auf vaschiedne Artn zur Energie-Gewinnung gnutzt.
english: The Isar water flows into the giant downpipes of the Walchensee Hydroelectric Power Station.
note: Describes a specific power-station pipe flow rather than use of the Isar in various ways for energy.

bar_text: A guada Tei vom Isarwossa werd in da Nach vo Mittnwoid zum Woichnsää umgleit.
english: 22 km just north of Scharnitz and the Isar is dammed for the first time between Mittenwald and Krün.
note: Damming near Scharnitz/Mittenwald does not convey substantial diversion to Walchensee.

bar_text: Des werd gmacht, wei s' Woichnsääkraftwerk mehra Wossa bracht, ois vo sejba in See fliaßt.
english: Some of the Isar waters are channeled via the Rißbach into the Walchensee, the Rißbach flow direction having been reversed. The Isar water flows into the giant downpipes of the Walchensee Hydroelectric Power Station.
note: Describes routing and pipes but omits the causal claim that the plant needs more than natural lake inflow.

bar_text: Da Sylvenstoa is a Stausee, dear vor oim gegas Hochwassa baut worn is, aba a zua Stromerzeugung gnutzt werd.
english: The construction of the Sylvenstein Dam and numerous regulations relating to the river, pushed through in the early 19th century, have strongly enhanced its character. The construction of the Sylvenstein dam has prevented the river from overflowing its banks.
note: Omits electricity generation and adds early-nineteenth-century regulations and river-character claims.

bar_text: Im weidan Valauf gibts mehrane Flußkraftwerke z. B. am neadlichn Stadtrand vo Däiz und de Isarwerke 1-3 inahoib vo Minga.
english: For example, just north of Mittenwald all the river's water was diverted to the lake Walchensee in 1923 for the Walchensee hydroelectric plant.
